The AMPLE language specification

Spec version 1.0, status: provisional. This is the description of the AMPLE source language (.amplet) and of the data files around it. The machine-readable half lives in spec/; when a page here and the data disagree, the data is the one the tools follow and the page is fixed.

Which syntax? A song is a list of blocks. A block has a type, a name, a place on the timeline and a body: drums beats at 1 for 16 {. Lines inside say what the block does (pattern ...) and what feeds it (from keys.audio -> audio). The first line is the composition line: composition "name" { ample 1 tempo 100 master-seed 7 }.

The machine-readable half

spec/ holds the same facts as data: grammar.ebnf, tokens.json, types.json, classes.json, templates/*.json, diagnostics.json, lint-rules.json, plugins.json, version.json and JSON Schemas in schema/. A program can read them instead of hard-coding the language.

01 Overview

Goals

  • A song is text that can be read, diffed, versioned and generated. The node editor, the arrangement and the source editor are three views of the same text (source-and-views).
  • Reproducible by default: every random choice is derived from a master seed; AI results are recorded as takes with their plans (06).
  • Good errors: one front end produces diagnostics with stable codes and exact ranges for the editor, the terminal and CI (08).
  • Small and checkable: a line-oriented syntax a person can write by hand and a tool can recover from.

Non-goals (spec 0.1)

General-purpose programming (no variables, loops or functions yet); defining new block types in the language (templates come from the library and plugins); audio DSP details (the engine's business).

The model in one paragraph

A song file declares a composition (name, language version, tempo, master seed), optional features and lint settings, and a list of blocks. A block has a type (from the template catalogue), a unique name, an optional pinned@version, optional placements on the timeline, optional flags, parameters and from lines that connect another block's output port to one of its own input ports. The blocks and their from lines form a directed acyclic graph that the engine builds into audio.

File kinds

File Format Defined in
*.amplet the song source pages 02 to 09
*.amplelrc (lyrics) timed lyrics 10
pack.json sound pack manifest
plugin.json plugin manifest
ample.lock pinned versions and hashes, written by the tool

Conformance

A tool conforms to spec 0.1 when it passes the corpus in spec-tests/: the same diagnostics (code, severity, range) for every case in invalid/, no errors for every case in valid/, identical output for format/, roundtrip/ and the recovery expectations in recovery/.

02 Lexical structure

Text

  • Encoding UTF-8, no BOM required (a BOM is accepted and removed by the formatter). Line endings \n or \r\n; the formatter writes \n.
  • The language is line oriented: one statement per line, except a block, which opens with a header line ending in { and closes with } alone on a line.
  • Positions are 1-based line and column, columns counted in characters (code points). The language server converts to UTF-16 for editors. A diagnostic range is [col, endCol) on one line.

Comments

# starts a comment that runs to the end of the line. A comment that reads # ample-ignore L001, L005 silences those lint rules for the next block (08). Comments are preserved by the formatter.

Names

  • identifier: one or more of letters, digits, _ and -. Examples: drums, kit, lm_seed, master-seed, felt-piano.
  • string: double quoted, with the escapes \", \\, \n, \t; any other backslash sequence stands for the escaped character itself (a parser never fails on an escape). A name is an identifier or a string; use a string when the name contains spaces or other characters.
  • Block names are compared exactly (case sensitive); two names that differ only by case trigger lint rule L008.

Numbers

integer is digits; number is digits with an optional .digits. There are no negative literals in structure positions (tempo, bars, seeds); a parameter value is free text and may contain a leading - (for example -4 dB). Seeds are unsigned 64-bit integers from 0 to 18446744073709551615.

Keywords

Keywords are reserved only in their own position (a block may be named at if it is quoted). The list is in ../../spec/tokens.json: project features lint layout tempo master-seed at for as from bake lock refresh freeze seeds plan stable pinned live on off assist diff button auto info warning error.

Operators and punctuation

{ } , . -> @. -> and . appear only in from lines; @ only in pinned@version; , only between placement parts and inside nothing else.

Limits (spec 0.1)

Tempo 20 to 300. Project master seeds and block seeds range from 0 to 18446744073709551615. Meter: a song is in 4/4 unless its composition line says meter 3/4 (the top number 1 to 16, the bottom number 2, 4, 8 or 16; AMP1120 otherwise): a bar then has the quarter-note beats of that meter (3/4 and 6/8: three, 5/4: five, 7/8: three and a half), and everything that counts bars follows it (see "Meter" in 03-syntax).

03 Syntax

The grammar below is the same text as ../../spec/grammar.ebnf (a test compares them). It describes the structure; the meaning of block types, parameters and ports comes from the template data (05).

(* AMPLE source grammar, spec version 1.0 (provisional). One statement per line; blocks span lines.
   Notation: ISO-style EBNF; "..." terminals; [ ] optional; { } repetition; ( | ) choice; (* *) comment.
   The prose in docs/language/03-syntax.md contains the same grammar; validate-spec checks they are equal. *)

file        = { line } ;
line        = blank | comment | composition | features | settings | lint | layout | view | use | block ;
blank       = eol ;
comment     = "#" , { any-char } , eol ;
ignore      = "#" , "ample-ignore" , rule-code , { [ "," ] , rule-code } , eol ;

composition = ( "composition" | "project" ) , string , "{" , [ "ample" , integer ] , "tempo" , number , [ "meter" , integer , "/" , integer ] , "master-seed" , integer , "}" , eol ;   (* "project" is the old word: still read, with AMP1117 *)
features    = "features" , "{" , { feature-pair } , "}" , eol ;
feature-pair = module , ( "on" | "off" ) | "assist" , assist-level ;
module      = "quality" | "credits" | "signing" | "secrets" | "lyrics" | "git-mirror" ;
assist-level = "off" | "diff" | "button" | "auto" ;
settings    = "settings" , "{" , { setting-pair } , "}" , eol ;
setting-pair = identifier , "." , identifier , whitespace , ( string | setting-atom ) ;
setting-atom = { any-char-except-space-or-brace } ;
lint        = "lint" , "{" , { rule-code , level } , "}" , eol ;
level       = "off" | "info" | "warning" | "error" ;
rule-code   = "L" , digit , digit , digit ;
layout      = "layout" , name , integer , integer , eol ;

view        = "view" , "{" , eol , { view-line } , "}" , eol ;   (* what the editors remember besides the sound; the song does not depend on it *)
view-line   = blank | comment | view-group | view-size | view-pin | view-section | view-line-name | view-order ;
view-group  = "group" , name , "{" , eol , { blank | comment | identifier , value-text , eol } , "}" , eol ;   (* title, member, x, y, label and other fields of the group *)
view-size   = "size" , name , number , eol ;
view-pin    = "pin" , name , eol ;
view-section = "section" , string , "at" , integer , "for" , integer , eol ;   (* bars 1 to 256, no two overlap *)
view-line-name = "line" , name , string , eol ;   (* a name for the line that holds this block *)
view-order  = "order" , name , { name } , eol ;   (* the order of the lines, by one block of each *)

use         = "use" , module-ref , "as" , name , "{" , eol , { use-line } , "}" , eol ;
module-ref  = ( identifier , { "/" , identifier } | string ) , [ "@" , version ] ;
use-line    = blank | comment | parameter | from ;

block       = block-header , "{" , eol , { block-line } , "}" , eol ;
block-header = block-type , name , [ pinned-version ] , [ placement ] , { flag } , [ freeze ] ;
block-type  = identifier ;
pinned-version = "pinned" , "@" , version ;
version     = digit-run , { "." , digit-run } ;
placement   = "at" , part , { "," , part } ;
part        = integer , "for" , ( integer | "auto" ) , [ "as" , name ] ;
flag        = "bake" | "lock" | "refresh" | "disabled" ;
freeze      = "freeze" , ( "seeds" | "plan" ) ;
block-line  = blank | comment | parameter | from | expanded-midi-notes | notes-expression | random-stream | embedded-sequence ;
expanded-midi-notes = "notes" , "{" , eol , { comment | midi-note } , "}" , eol ;
notes-expression = "notes" , expression-text , eol , { { blank | comment } , "|>" , expression-text , eol } ;   (* a note pipeline: docs/language/12-note-pipelines.md; a pipe line continues the expression, so do braces and parentheses that are still open *)
expression-text = { any-char-except-eol } ;
random-stream = "random-stream" , whitespace , identifier , whitespace , expression-text , eol ;   (* a named random cursor of a clip: docs/language/13-randomness.md *)
embedded-sequence = "sequence" , "{" , eol , { sequence-line } , "}" , eol ;
sequence-line = { any-char-except-eol } , eol ;
midi-note   = "note" , "{" , eol , { comment | midi-note-field } , "}" , eol ;
midi-note-field = identifier , value-text , eol ;
parameter   = identifier , value-text , eol ;
from        = "from" , name , "." , name , "->" , name , eol ;

name        = identifier | string ;
identifier  = letter-or-digit-or-dash-or-underscore , { letter-or-digit-or-dash-or-underscore } ;
string      = '"' , { string-char | escape } , '"' ;
escape      = "\" , ( '"' | "\" | "n" | "t" ) ;
number      = digit-run , [ "." , digit-run ] ;
integer     = digit-run ;
value-text  = { any-char-except-eol } ;

(* A module file, modules/NAME.module: the declarations first, then ordinary blocks and nested use statements.
   Inside the module, "from in.<input> -> port" reads a module input; "$name" in a value stands for a parameter. *)
module-file = { blank | comment } , module-decl , { blank | comment | param-decl | input-decl | output-decl | block | use } ;
module-decl = "module" , module-ref , "version" , version , eol ;
param-decl  = "param" , identifier , value-text , eol ;
input-decl  = "input" , identifier , eol ;
output-decl = "output" , identifier , name , "." , name , eol ;

Statements

Statement Shape Notes
composition composition "name" { ample 1 tempo 92 master-seed 424242 } required exactly once; missing is AMP1001. ample N is the AMPLE version the song was written for (see below); the old word project is still read, with the warning AMP1117 and a quick fix
features features { quality off lyrics on assist diff } modules are on/off, assist is off diff button auto
lint lint { L004 error L005 info } only entries that differ from the default; levels off info warning error
settings settings { acestep.synthModel sft acestep.vocalIsolation ace } plugin settings of this song, pairs of plugin.name and a value (text with spaces in quotes); part of the plan of the blocks of that plugin, so changing one makes a new take; at most one line; malformed is AMP1112. Project-level settings are only the starting point for new songs
layout layout "name" 280 20 node editor position; no meaning for the sound
view view { … } at the end of the song what the editors remember besides the sound: group (title, members, place), size, pin, section "Drop" at 33 for 32 (a named stretch of bars, 1 to 256, no overlap), line kick "Kick stack" (a name for the line that holds the block) and order kick snare (the order of the lines). The song does not depend on it: it changes no plan, take or sound. Error AMP1114 for any other line; AMP1121 to AMP1123 for sections. Since spec 1.1
block type name [pinned@version] [at ...] [flags] [freeze ...] { ... } see below
comment # text # ample-ignore L001 silences rules for the next block

Finals are project metadata kept in .ample/finals.json and managed through the Finals view or API; they are not a statement or block in the AMPLE song language.

Blocks

drums beats at 1 for 8 as intro, 9 for 8 as outro lock {
  kit kit/tape
  from chords.notes -> trigger
}
  • Header order is fixed: type, name, pinned@version (only for a pinned block), placement, flags, freeze. A block that is not pinned follows the definition of its type; whether it is dynamic (live) comes from that definition too.
  • Pinned: piano keys pinned@2.1 at 1 for 8 { keeps that version of the block: the same major (the same sound), at least that minor. Block versions are major.minor only.
  • Placement: at <bar> for <bars> [as <name>], several separated by commas. Parts of one block may not overlap (lint L004).
  • Flags: bake (the take is stored and used), lock (the value is kept), refresh (always fetch again), disabled (the block produces no take). A connected block that requires a disabled block is implicitly disabled with the warning AMP5253; an unconnected disabled block is simply omitted. lock with refresh is contradictory (L003).
  • Freeze: freeze seeds or freeze plan (06).
  • Body lines: a parameter is name value (the value is the rest of the line, free text, validated by the template); a from line is from <block>.<output> -> <input>. A parameter name appears once per block.
  • The closing } is alone on its line.

Expanded MIDI notes

Only midi-clip may use a nested notes body. It represents the same notes as the compact notes parameter and remains in source after editing:

midi-clip verse {
  ppq 480
  notes {
    # comment stays with this note
    note {
      bar 18
      start 22
      length 72
      pitch 121
      velocity 96
      channel 5
      bank 0
      program 60
      tie-id 2
    }
  }
}

bar is one-based. start and length use quarter-note beats (up to six decimal places) when ppq is absent or uses the legacy million-unit scale; otherwise they use integer ticks at the clip's ppq. pitch is 0–127 and velocity is 1–127. channel, bank and program are optional as a complete set; tie-id is optional and identifies bar-split segments. The clip remains in 4/4 for note placement; imported meter events stay available in the MIDI event source. # comments are retained verbatim and ignored when building note data.

Error recovery (normative)

A conforming parser never stops at the first error and never throws on any input. Required behaviour:

  1. A line that is not any statement reports AMP1100 and parsing continues with the next line.
  2. A bad block header reports an error (AMP1102-AMP1106); the block body is still consumed up to its } so later blocks are found. If the header yielded a type and name, the block is kept in the tree (so the editor can still show it); otherwise its body is skipped.
  3. A bad body line (AMP1107-AMP1109) does not remove the block; the rest of the body is parsed.
  4. An unclosed block at the end of the file reports AMP1101 at the block header and keeps the block.
  5. Semantic checks (AMP2xxx, lint) run on everything that parsed, even when syntax errors exist; blocks that are known to be broken (skipped) take no part in them.
  6. The order of diagnostics in the output is by position (line, column, then code) when a tool prints them; implementations may produce them in another order internally, and the corpus compares them as a set sorted by (line, column, code).

The recovery corpus (../../spec-tests/recovery/) fixes the expected blocks and codes for broken inputs.

Modules (use and module files)

use <module>[@version] as <name> { ... } puts an instance of a reusable module into the song. The body gives the module's parameters (name value) and connects its inputs (from block.output -> input, where the last word is the module's input name). Other blocks read the instance like a block: from intro.audio -> mix, where audio is one of the module's outputs. The parser only checks the shape; the module is found and expanded when the song is built (ample modules expand, 07).

AMPLE versions

ample N says which version of the language and of the built-in blocks a file was written for. It is a whole number that goes up only when a change could alter how an existing song sounds or reads; it is not the number of the program.

  • In the composition line: composition "name" { ample 1 tempo 92 master-seed 424242 }. A song that says nothing is read as the current version and gets the info AMP1118 with a quick fix that adds it. A number this AMPLE does not know (0, or higher than it reads) is the error AMP1119.
  • In a definition, not in a song: the definition of a built-in block (and of a component) says since which AMPLE version it reads the same ("stableSince" in the template, 1 when it says nothing). A song cannot claim that for its own blocks. When a block was changed after the version a song was written for, that block is shown read-only (with its migrated values) until the song is migrated.
  • Never upgraded by itself: an older song is carried to the current version in memory, step by step (AmpleVersions.Upgrade), and the text on disk only changes when its author migrates it. Every step must keep the sound: where a default or a name changed, the step writes the old value explicitly.
  • Files that import another file keep that file's own number: a component imported with use is read as the version its own file states, never as the importing song's.

Controls

A control is a number over time that comes out of a block (follow, curve, map) and steers a parameter that can be automated (volume gain, pan, filter cutoff, the mix of the effects, compressor threshold, stretch speed, pitch semitones; the templates mark them with "automatable": true).

  • Types. control is the general one: a level from 0 to 1 that is scaled to the range of the parameter. control<Hz>, control<dB>, control<%>, control<ms>, control<st>, ... know their unit and only steer a parameter in that unit (AMP2253). A control never connects to audio or MIDI.
  • Expression. A parameter may read controls: cutoff 600 Hz + 3000 * traffic.level. Numbers (with a unit), + - *, brackets and block.output. Everything is integer fixed point with three decimals, so a build is the same everywhere; a general control is a fraction (so 3000 * level is 0 to 3000). Errors: AMP2251 (not valid), AMP2252 (not a control).
  • Connection. from traffic.level -> cutoff connects a control to the parameter named like the input. A parameter has one source: an expression and a connection together are AMP2254.
  • Build. The block that reads a control waits for the block that makes it (cycles are AMP2010). The control is a take of its own (CTL1: 1000 integer values per second from the first bar of its source); before the renderer runs, a parameter that reads a control is turned into the points of an automation curve, so every renderer follows it like auto(...).
  • Components. A component port may be Control or Control<unit>, follow and map are stages of an audio pipeline (emit audio |> follow(band="low") |> map(unit="Hz", out_high=4000) -> traffic), curve starts a control from nothing (emit curve(value="auto(1:0, 4:1000)") -> sweep) and fire turns a control into notes that an instrument plays (emit audio |> follow(band="low") |> fire(note=36) |> piano() -> audio).

repeat in the process of an audio component

audio |> repeat(times=cars, delay=2bar, length=24bar) makes the sound again and again and mixes the copies into one sound. times is a whole number from 1 to 16 and may be a property (property cars: Int = 4), so the component decides how many copies there are; delay is the time before the first copy (default none); the copies are spread evenly over what is left of length (the first at delay, then every (length - delay) / times), or at a fixed distance with every=4bar instead of length. Times are written with a unit (bar, beat, s, ms) and may be calculated from properties. Example: demo-projects/components/components/street-cars.amplec (cars that pass a street, with the road also as an output of its own to tweak).

trim

trim finds where the sound of a recording is (the stretches above threshold that a silence of at least gap separates) and cuts the silence around it, keeping padding, with a short fadein and fadeout if you like. Several stretches in one recording: sections warn (default) cuts from the start of the first to the end of the last and puts a warning in the report of the block; all does the same without the warning; first and last take that one stretch. In a component: road |> trim(sections=all) |> repeat(times=cars, length=length), so that each car starts at its first sound and a replaced recording still fits.

if / else and silence in a component

In the process of an audio component a branch can be chosen by a property: if (tone) { ... } else if (level) { ... } else { ... }. The condition is a Bool property, a number (0 is false) or a calculation, and the branch that is taken is known when the graph is built, so the lines of the other branches are not part of it. A let in a branch is available after it, so every branch should give the same names. In a calculation a Bool is 1 or 0, and if(condition, a, b) picks one of two values.

silence() is blank audio as long as the block it is in (auto); silence(10s) is as long as you say. It stands where a branch has no sound: let bed = if... is written as if (tone) { let bed = sad |> gain(-6dB) } else { let bed = silence() }.

Meter

composition "waltz" { ample 1 tempo 96 meter 3/4 master-seed 7 }: the optional meter sits between tempo and master-seed. Without it a song is in 4/4. The top number is the beats of a bar (1 to 16), the bottom number the note that gets a beat (2, 4, 8 or 16); anything else is AMP1120 and the song stays in 4/4.

What follows from it, for the whole song: a bar lasts 4 x top / bottom quarter-note beats (3/4 and 6/8: three, 5/4: five, 7/8: three and a half); at 3 for 2 still counts bars; the beat of a note (bar:beat:length:pitch:velocity) runs from 0 up to the beats of the bar; 1bar in the note language is one such bar; the grid of a drums pattern and of a sequencer row is sixteenth notes, so a bar has 12 steps in 3/4 (a pattern of 16 characters is cut after 12 in a 3/4 song, write 12); chords Am.F shares a bar between two chords; a note value such as 1/16 stays a fraction of a whole note (four beats) in every meter; the tempo is quarter notes per minute in every meter, so 6/8 at 120 is a bar of three quarter notes (1.5 seconds).

The studio follows the meter: the piano roll (the bar lines, the snap to a bar, the metronome accent), the step grid of the drum and strum editors (12 steps in 3/4), the lengths shown in seconds, and the local preview in the browser all use the beats of the bar. One meter for the whole song: a change of meter inside a song, and a meter per clip, are not built; MIDI import and export use the meter of the file: the module is cut at the bar lines of its first time signature, the converter records it as meter=N/D and warns that the song using the module must say the same meter, and the export reads it back so the notes return on the same ticks. A file that changes meter inside gets one meter and a warning.

04 Types and ports

A connection can be temporarily switched off without removing it: from kit.audio -> in disabled. The canvas retains it as a dimmed dashed line; its context menu enables it again. Disabled connections supply no input and do not create active build dependencies. Mixer inputs are optional; a mixer processes the active channels, or produces no take when none remain. Required consumers and audio/render effects with their main input switched off become implicitly disabled. Enabling a connection restores its original endpoints.

Every block template declares input ports and output ports, each with a type. The types of spec 0.1 are in ../../spec/types.json:

Type Meaning
audio rendered sound
render an immutable source recipe with ordered effects, materialized when audio is requested or the effect is explicitly built
midi notes and timing (textual MIDI)
midi-sequence a bounded MIDI event stream with tick order
text words, such as lyrics
data structured data: style, external values
any matches every type except render; used by groups

Connection rule

from <block>.<output> -> <input> connects when the output type and input type are equal, or either is any, except that render only connects to render. This keeps source recipes distinct from materialized audio even at group boundaries. There are no implicit conversions. A mismatch is AMP2007.

Render recipes

Audio sources expose audio and render outputs. audio is the ordinary built sound. render carries an immutable recipe for that source and does not change its ordinary take. Effects accept either an active audio input or an active render input; both connections may be present when one or both are disabled. An effect can pass the recipe onward through render or materialize it at its existing audio output.

drums.render -> eq.render -> reverb.render
reverb.audio -> mixer.in1
drums.audio -> mixer.in2

The effect chain is collected in order and the source is rendered with those effects when its audio output is consumed or the final effect is explicitly built. Intermediate render links create no takes. The mixer receives the effected variant on in1 and ordinary drums on in2. Two render branches remain independent. Connecting drums.audio -> eq.audio keeps the existing post-render effect path.

The plan and cache identity include the source and its inputs, then the ordered effects and parameters. A changed effect rebuilds its variant and dependent audio consumers. render is not MIDI/events, and any cannot convert it.

Port rules

  • An input takes one source (AMP2008 for a second). To combine several sources use a mixer-like block.
  • A block cannot read itself (AMP2009); the graph must be acyclic (AMP2010, with the cycle path in the message).
  • A required input with no source is lint rule L002 (a warning by default): the template marks which inputs are required.
  • Naming a missing block, output or input is AMP2004, AMP2005, AMP2006; the hint lists the valid names.
  • Output ports may stay unconnected. Unused outputs are lint rule L001 (info); audio that never reaches a master block is L007.

Groups

A group block has one any input and one any output and may contain an inner graph that is edited in the node editor. Inner graphs are not part of the .amplet text in spec 0.1.

05 Blocks and templates

A template defines a block type: its ports, parameters, class, version, whether it is dynamic, and which plugin it needs. The catalogue is data: one file per template in ../../spec/templates/<id>.json, validated by ../../spec/schema/template.schema.json. The generated help (help.html) renders one card per template; this page defines the rules.

The provisional voice-clone block reads a project voice sample from file and speaks its text. model selects XTTS, Qwen3 or Chatterbox; language is passed to that model. Qwen3 additionally needs reference_text, unless auto_detect on is selected. The sample is hashed into the build plan, so changing it invalidates the generated take. Common audio formats are accepted and converted to WAV internally when needed. Model weights are configured locally and are not downloaded by the plugin.

Version pin

A block header has no class and no number: a block follows the current version of its type (every built-in block is 1.0). To say which version a block was written for, add pinned@<major.minor> after the name:

eq tone pinned@1.0 {
}

A pin is a request, and lint L006 reports a pinned block whose version is older than the type's current one. Block versions are major.minor only (no patch, no ^ or ~); components keep full semantic versions (pinned@^1.2). A change that alters the sound is a new major version. Live blocks cannot be pinned: bake them.

Parameters

splitter takes audio and exposes mono audio outputs left and right. It preserves channel level and duration; mono input is duplicated onto both outputs. The node preview plays the original input. Connect a render chain's materialized audio output to the splitter; the splitter itself does not forward render recipes.

splitter channels {
  from level.audio -> audio
}
eq left_eq {
  from channels.left -> audio
}
eq right_eq {
  from channels.right -> audio
}

The volume effect accepts either audio (audio) or a render recipe (render). It exposes three fixed audio outputs: left and right are individual mono output channels; audio carries both output channels as stereo (before v1 it was called mixed). The render output continues the recipe. The block preview plays the mixed output.

The two channel faders use left_gain and right_gain (−60 to +12 dB, default 0). With linked on (default), moving either fader moves both by the same amount and preserves their difference, stopping at the shared bounds. Properties can set exact values independently. Linking is a UI setting and does not alter audio by itself. The existing gain parameter remains a common gain, default 0 dB. Positive gain can clip rendered PCM.

mono on averages the input channels before applying common gain, separate channel gains and mutes. Left and right remain separate ports with their connections intact; turning mono off restores stereo routing. left off and right off silence their respective output channels. Mono input feeds both channels. All settings are available in source and Properties; the canvas and advanced controls provide L/R faders, meters, mutes and Mono. enabled off bypasses processing while preserving every output.

volume level {
  left_gain -3 dB
  right_gain -6 dB
  linked on
  left on
  right off
  mono off
  from kit.audio -> audio
}
  • A block accepts only the parameters its template lists (AMP2003 otherwise; the hint lists the valid ones).
  • The template gives each parameter a type (number or text) and a default. A missing parameter takes the default.
  • A parameter appears once per block (AMP1109).
  • Seed parameters (seed, lm_seed) are the word derived or an unsigned 64-bit integer 0 to 18446744073709551615 (AMP2011). A custom seed is allowed and recorded (L009).
  • A template may declare modalEditor: true for text that benefits from the property's expanded … editor, and multiline: true when line breaks are meaningful. Multiline values are stored as the existing \n source escape and restored as line breaks by the property editor; a single-line value visibly wraps but line breaks are converted to spaces when saved.
  • A template may declare affectsOutput: false on a parameter that is an execution policy rather than a sound setting: a hint about how the renderer gets to its result (for example a time/memory trade-off) where every option gives byte-identical audio. It defaults to true. A studio panel may show such parameters apart from the musical controls (denoise's optimize does); a renderer that sets it false must prove the claim (same input, same output, for every option) before relying on it, since nothing else enforces it.

The universal block header flag disabled is independent of template parameters and effect enabled off bypass. It keeps the block visible but returns no take. Blocks depending on its required inputs, including audio and render effect chains, become implicitly disabled without a build failure; the block reports the warning AMP5253 so it is visible why it produced nothing. Optional inputs, such as mixer channels, omit the disabled branch so other channels can still render. A mixer with no connected inputs or only disabled inputs produces no take and is implicitly disabled. Implicit disabling is derived from connections and disappears when an upstream input becomes active; it does not write a disabled flag into downstream source.

Audio sources expose a render output alongside ordinary audio. Built-in audio effects accept an audio input for post-render processing or a render recipe input for a source variant. Both connections may be present when at least one is disabled; only active connections determine the effect input. The next audio connection materializes the whole recipe as a variant take; explicitly building a render-connected effect also materializes that effect's variant. Intermediate render links create no takes. Effects remain independent blocks with their own parameters.

Block takes use local time: their first placed part starts at local bar 1, without leading silence from the arrangement position. Moving the whole block preserves its take and the takes of its audio/render effects; relative gaps between multiple parts remain part of its content. Mixer and master inputs apply arrangement placement and range cropping, and their plans include that placement. Moving a block invalidates the arranged mix, which can be regenerated using cached local takes. The local-v1 plan marker separates these takes from earlier song-length renders; existing selected frozen takes retain their original content until explicitly replaced.

The midi-clip template also accepts an optional structured notes value. It can be a space-separated list of bar:beat:length:pitch:velocity entries or a persistent notes { note { ... } } body with named fields. Beat and length use quarter-note beats with up to six decimal places by default; set ppq to use exact integer ticks per quarter note instead. Eight-field entries can append channel:bank:program to retain source instrument routing; generated nine-field entries add a tie identity so bar-split sustains remain distinct from repeated notes. A compact entry may append ;pan=, ;fine=, ;rel=, ;cut=, ;slide= or ;port=; the language server completes these keys after a semicolon, and invalid values produce AMP2012. The expanded body accepts bar, start, length, pitch, velocity, optional routing fields and optional tie-id; # comments stay in source beside the note or field they describe. Notes are polyphonic, must fit within one 4/4 bar, and represent a tie across a bar as one entry in each bar. GM/SF2, synth and sample-set piano/bass/guitar render per-note expression; slide renders a glide without a retrigger. MIDI module import/export retains supported note-start expression and writes pitch-bend ramps for slide notes. Portamento settings round-trip as CC65/CC5; renderer portamento is not implemented. The empty default keeps existing chords and melody behavior unchanged. The short melody form has dynamics: a note can carry its own velocity (c4:1:110), a marker word pp p mp mf f ff (velocity 32 to 112, f = 96 = the default) sets the velocity of the notes after it, and < (crescendo) or > (decrescendo) ramps the notes after it, by their place in time, to the next marker word (to ff or pp at the end of the melody when none follows): melody "mp c4 d4 < e4 g4 ff c5:4". A note with its own velocity is never changed by a marker, and markers take no time.

Compact notes additionally accept ;tie=N (integer 0 through 2000000) to join consecutive bar-split pieces without explicitly setting channel, bank or program. Expanded tie-id also works without routing fields. Nine-field ties remain supported; writing both forms on one entry, or repeating tie, is invalid. A long piano-roll note is stored as these valid bar segments; the editor merges them for display and resizing. This preserves the connected instrument's inherited routing when a note grows over a bar line.

The midi block exposes notes, the complete typed sequence, and audio ports. Connect the sequence to midi-render to render the file through a project SF2 file or the installed GM pack with a gain control. MIDI, midi-render and GM instrument blocks default to an integer soft limiter before PCM output; set limiter off only when hard clipping is wanted. The song mixer also soft-limits summed inputs. If an SF2 bank lacks a source bank/program, the GM renderer uses the matching GM program (or piano) and reports the fallback. The notes port remains available for piano, GM and other instrument blocks.

The midi data block reads a project .mid or .midi file. Its track parameter is all or a zero-based track index; its notes:midi output has the same shape as midi-clip, and its optional warnings:text output describes unsupported note-adjacent events. The block may also retain source-file, variant-file and variant-module for an editable MIDI variant: Edit MIDI variant opens the module, saving it exports a new active MIDI asset, and the context menu can switch between Original and Edited.

File parameters and what can be dropped on them. A parameter of kind: file lists the extensions it takes in accept (for example .mid, .midi for the file of midi; .sf2 for gm and midi-render); a parameter of kind: sampleset takes a folder. The web app uses these lists to decide which blocks a file can be used in (Use in song, drag and drop). A new file parameter that should take drops needs an accept list.

Fades: fadein, fadeout and the fade and crossfade blocks

A fade is a value that goes from silence to full (a fade in) or from full to exact silence (a fade out). It is written as the value of a volume gain or of the mix of an effect:

volume v {
  from drums.audio -> audio
  gain fadeout(5, 2, equal)      # from bar 5 over two bars, ends in silence
}
  • fadein(start, length [, shape]) and fadeout(start, length [, shape]). A fade in is silent before its start and full after its end; a fade out is full before its start and exactly silent after its end.
  • Units: a plain number is bars (5 is the start of bar 5, 5.5 is half way through it; the start counts from bar 1; the length 0.5 is half a bar). A number with an s is seconds (12s, 1.5s); a start in seconds counts from the beginning of the song. Start and length may use different units. Up to six decimals.
  • Shapes: lin (a straight line in volume, the default), equal (equal power: a fade in and a fade out of the same length add up to constant power for unrelated sounds, so use it for a crossfade) and exp (starts slowly, ends fast).
  • All arithmetic is integer, so every machine gets the same bytes. A fade on a pan, a cutoff or a threshold is refused with AMP5371.

The fade block does the same with one audio input and one output (direction out or in, start, length, shape). The crossfade block has two inputs, a and b: a fades out and b fades in over the same stretch (start, length, shape, equal power by default). Both build the same fade text and use the same engine as the formula, so a block and a formula with the same settings give the same bytes. The curve editor (the ∿ button) has a Fade… button for a gain and a mix.

Patterns and sections. drums and guitar take two optional parameters, patterns (named patterns, name=grids / name=grids) and song (the sections in order, verse*4 fill chorus*8); see Samples.

Time stretch. stretch.speed is a percentage from 25 to 400; 50 plays at half speed and keeps pitch. It also accepts auto(bar:percent, ...), such as speed auto(1:100, 9:50), for a linear speed ramp by bar. The rendered block keeps its length. This does not change the project's tempo.

Example, needs and sound source in a template

Besides ports and parameters, a template file in spec/templates/ carries three fields for people and tools:

  • example (required): the text of a small .amplet song in v1 form that uses a block of this type. A test parses every example with the spec and requires no errors and a block of the template's type. The docs show it on the card of the block, and demos and mp3 renders can be made from it.
  • needs (optional list of sentences): what the block needs besides its input, for example a drum kit folder (a sampleset parameter), a SoundFont or recording (a file parameter) or a plugin. It is derived from the parameters of kind sampleset, file and engine and from the plugin.
  • soundSource (optional, true): the block makes a sound by itself from notes, files or settings, so its example can be rendered to hear it. Effects are not sound sources: they need a source in front of them.

Adding a template means adding its example; the description should say in one or two sentences what the block does, what it needs and what it gives.

Dynamic blocks and plugins

A template can be dynamic (its result can change, for example an AI take) and can require a plugin. A block whose plugin is not installed is AMP5001, a warning: AMPLE reports it instead of silently skipping the block. Plugins are listed in ../../spec/plugins.json (opt-in or built in).

The catalogue (spec 0.1, provisional)

midi-clip, midi, gm, synth (a small subtractive synth on MIDI notes), sampler (one sample played on notes, moved in pitch from a root note), import-audio (plays a WAV file of the project), the MIDI effects transpose, midi-humanize, quantize, arpeggiator and chord (notes in, notes out, between a clip and an instrument), send (a shared effect bus: through and send outputs), drums, bass, piano, the effects eq, distortion, delay, reverb, compressor, filter, limiter, width, pan, gate, deesser, chorus, flanger, phaser, bitcrusher, pitch, stretch and duck (audio in, audio out, with an enabled off bypass), ai-voice, ace-music, mood-scene, choir, lyrics, weather, import-audio, mixer, master, variants, scorer, group. gm plays a zero-based General MIDI program and bank from the installed MuseScore General SF2 pack or a project-local .sf2 file. ai-voice is for isolated vocals: its voice parameter is a vocal direction, not a selected speaker identity, and it requires linked lyrics. Both ACE blocks expose guidance (CFG) as a stored generation parameter, visibly resolved to 7 for Base/SFT and 1 for Turbo; changing it changes the requested ACE guidance scale and can change the sound. Keep it fixed when comparing seeds. ace-music intentionally allows accompaniment and has optional lyrics, so it can make an instrumental. mood-scene.style supplies reusable scene direction to either ACE block. Adding or changing a template is a language change (99).

Filter wobble. A filter block can move its cutoff with lfo_rate (off, 1/1 through 1/32, and triplet rates 1/4t, 1/8t, 1/16t), lfo_depth (0–8 octaves above the base cutoff), and lfo_shape (sine, triangle, saw, square). The oscillator phase follows the song bar, so rendering a selected range keeps the same phase as rendering the whole song.

Example

example: compiles
composition "demo" { ample 1  tempo 92  master-seed 424242 }
midi-clip chords {
  chords Am F C G
}
piano piano pinned@2.0 at 1 for 8 as verse {
  from chords.notes -> notes
}

chords takes one chord per bar. A chord is a root and a quality (Am, F, G7, Cmaj7, Dsus4, Bbm7, Fm6, Cadd9); C/E is a slash chord that puts the named bass note lowest (a first inversion here; a bass note that is not in the chord is added below it); two chords joined by a dot (Am.F) share one bar, two beats each. Without a slash or a dot a chord sounds exactly as before (root position).

Parameter names for time and speed

One scheme for every effect: a duration is written in milliseconds with its unit (attack 10 ms), a position in a file in seconds, a free-running speed as rate in Hz, and a tempo lock as a note value (sync). A template may list aliases on a parameter: extra names the parser accepts and rewrites to the real name before anything else reads the song. chorus, flanger and phaser accept rate 0.5 (Hz) for period 2000 ms (the value is converted); filter accepts lfo_sync for lfo_rate; arpeggiator accepts sync for rate. The old names stay valid. Completion offers the real names only.

Effect limits

filter has resonance (0 to 100 %, automatable like the cutoff: resonance auto(1:0, 9:90)); its type can also be bandpass or notch, and slope (dB per octave: 12 default, 24, 36 or 48) runs the filter two, three or four times for a steeper cut. eq has a low shelf, a high shelf and one fixed mid band, no free peak; for free bands use peq (parametric EQ: six bands band1_type (peak, lowshelf, highshelf, notch, lowcut, highcut; lowcut and highcut are 12 dB per octave high-pass and low-pass), band1_hz, band1_gain, band1_q up to band6_...; band1_enabled off leaves a band out, and a band at 0 dB changes nothing). gate reacts to the level, so on a steady pad it does nothing: use tremolo with shape gate, a sync note value and a step pattern such as "x.xx.xx.x.xx.x.x" (x open, . closed, the letters a to i a level from 10 to 90 percent open such as "xdx.bxdx.xdx.x"; depth 100 for silence): a tempo-locked trance gate with a 2 ms fade at every change. See plan/effect-limits.md for what would fix these.

06 Seeds and determinism

The explanations live in determinism, controllability and regeneration safety; this page states what the language says.

Master seed

composition "name" { ... master-seed N } sets the master seed (unsigned 64-bit integer 0 to 18446744073709551615). Explicit block seeds use the same range; derived follows AMPLE's stable generator. Every block with random behaviour derives its own seeds from the master seed and a stable path (block identity and purpose), so a song is a pure function of its text and its recorded takes. The derivation uses the stable integer-only generator; its algorithm and test vectors will be added here and are frozen once released (rngVersion).

Seed parameters

A block may set seed or lm_seed to derived (default) or to a number. A number is a custom seed: allowed, recorded, and reported as lint L009 (info). Changing a seed later means takes made with the old one cannot be reproduced from the new one.

Flags and freeze

Syntax Meaning
bake the rendered take is stored and used instead of rendering again
lock the value (for data blocks) is recorded and kept
refresh always fetch again (contradicts lock: L003)
freeze seeds the seeds are fixed; the same inputs and seeds are rendered the same way (when the plugin is deterministic)
freeze plan seeds and the melody plan are stored; the voice may be re-rendered

bake is the top of the freeze ladder (free, seeds, plan, take). freeze and bake are mutually consistent: a baked block needs no freeze word (the serializer omits it).

What the language does not promise

Regenerating an AI block is only guaranteed to give the same result on the same machine and toolprint. Notices AMP5101 and AMP5102 say so (08); the stored take is what guarantees the song.

Algorithms (RngVersion 1, frozen once released)

  • Seed expansion: SplitMix64 (state += 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15; z = (z ^ z>>30) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9; z = (z ^ z>>27) * 0x94D049BB133111EB; output z ^ z>>31). A seed is expanded into four 64-bit state words by four calls.
  • Stream: xoshiro256** (result = rotl(s1 * 5, 7) * 9; t = s1 << 17; s2 ^= s0; s3 ^= s1; s1 ^= s2; s0 ^= s3; s2 ^= t; s3 = rotl(s3, 45)).
  • Bounded integers: unbiased by rejection: discard values below (264 - bound) mod bound, then take the value mod bound. Unit fractions: the top 53 bits as an integer divided by 253 (the only floating-point step; both numbers are exact). Shuffle: Fisher-Yates from the end, j = bounded(i + 1). Pick: bounded(count).
  • Seed derivation: SipHash-2-4 with key (k0 = master seed, k1 = 0x414D504C45534545, the ASCII text "AMPLESEE") over the bytes: the RngVersion byte, then for each path part either 0x01, the UTF-8 length as 4 bytes little endian and the UTF-8 bytes (a string), or 0x02 and the value as 8 bytes little endian (a non-negative integer). The 32-bit seed is the low 32 bits.
  • Verification: the vectors in spec-tests/prng/vectors.json (checked against the published SplitMix64 outputs for seed 1234567 and the SipHash-2-4 paper vector) are tested by the C# code (Ample.Audio.Random) and the JavaScript twin (web/lib/stable-rng.js). Changing any of this creates a new RngVersion; plans store the version they used.

Guarantee layers

  1. A stored take plus the deterministic mix is bit-identical (hash verified).
  2. Everything AMPLE renders itself is identical on every supported platform.
  3. Regenerating an AI block is guaranteed only locally; the regeneration flow verifies and defaults to restoring the previous take.

What a change of the master seed reaches

The master seed only changes a block whose seed is derived from it. A block does not follow it when it has a custom seed (seed 77), when its seed is locked (the take bank keeps the locked value), or when its block type never reads a seed (clips, mixer, master, groups, lyrics, import, effects and the like): the plan of such a block carries seed 0, so it keeps its take when the master seed or the block's name changes. The editor shows the same: after a new master seed only the blocks that follow it, and the blocks that read them, lose their built state (GET /api/doc/inputs lists them as followsMaster).

07 References and modules

Names and references

  • Block names are unique in a song (AMP2002) and are the only identifiers references use. A from line names <block>.<output>; both parts may be quoted when they contain spaces.
  • Reference resolution is by exact name. A near miss gets a hint ("Did you mean ...?") and a quick fix, never an automatic correction.
  • Apply (the editor's action) matches text blocks to the existing graph by name and type: the same name and type keeps its identity, its inside and its cache state; a new name creates a block; a name that is gone removes the block (source-and-views).

Files

Blocks that point at files (for example lyrics with file lyrics/chorus.lyr) use project-relative paths with / separators; a path never escapes the project or a registered link. Resolution order: project, linked folders, the user library, installed packs. A missing file is a diagnostic with a "relocate" fix. (Built as a service, not yet as a static diagnostic; see the library manager. Names are written without the file extension; the order is the project folder (<name> or assets/<name>), the project's linked folders, the user's linked folders, installed packs; codes AMP5290, AMP5291, AMP5294.)

Plugins, packs, locks

  • Plugins and packs are referenced by name and version in the project and pinned by hash in ample.lock, which the tool writes and people do not edit.
  • A template that needs a plugin that is not installed is AMP5001 (a warning).

Modules (spec 0.1)

features { ... } switches opt-in modules on or off: quality, credits, signing, secrets, lyrics, git-mirror; assist sets how much help the editor gives (off diff button auto). Reusable block modules are defined below (added in chunk 94).

Not yet specified

include of other .amplet files, imports of audio, MIDI or lyrics files, and the statement style of the older examples. They are tracked in open-questions.

Reusable modules (use and module files)

A module is a file modules/<name>.module in the project (or in a linked folder or pack, found the same way as other assets). Its first line says what it is, then it declares its knobs and doors, then it holds ordinary blocks:

module groove version 1.2
param kit kit/tape        # a parameter with its default
input chords              # a door the song connects
output audio mix.mix      # what the song can read: <block>.<port> inside the module

bass bass {
  from in.chords -> notes # "in.<input>" reads the module's input
}
drums drums {
  kit $kit                # $name stands for the parameter
}
mixer mix {
  from drums.audio -> audio1
  from bass.audio -> audio2
}

The song uses it with use groove@1.0 as intro { kit kit/808 from chords.notes -> chords } and reads from intro.audio -> mix.

  • Expansion. Before a song is built each use becomes plain blocks named <instance>/<block> (nested instances: outer/inner/block). The tool expands in memory; the song file keeps the short use. ample modules expand song.amplet prints the result.
  • Seeds. A block's seed is derived from its name, so the seeds of an instance depend on the instance path: the same module used twice gives two different sets of seeds, each stable, and renaming an instance changes its seeds (like renaming a block).
  • Parameters. The use may set any declared parameter; the others keep their default. $name is replaced in parameter values only.
  • Versions. @1.0 asks for the same major version and a minor version that is not older; no @ takes any. The versions and hashes that were used are pinned in ample.lock (a modules section); a changed module is AMP5328 until ample lock update.
  • Not in a module: placement (at ... for ...) works as written but cannot be moved by the use, and a module cannot read a block of the song except through its inputs.
  • Diagnostics (runtime): AMP5320 to AMP5328 are reported at the use line. The editor (parser) does not load modules; it accepts the shape of use and references to an instance.

08 Diagnostics and lint

The catalogue of codes is data: ../../spec/diagnostics.json (code, severity, title, explanation, wrong and right example, since, stage) and ../../spec/lint-rules.json. The generated help renders every code on its own anchor (help.html#AMP2003); ample explain AMP2003 prints the same text. This page defines the rules around them. Background: language-support.

The record

Every diagnostic has: code, severity (error, warning, info), a range (line, col, endCol, 1-based, one line), message (one plain sentence), optional hint, optional related (another place that matters), and optional fixes (a label and a text edit, marked safe or risky).

Code ranges

Range Meaning
AMP1xxx syntax: the text is not shaped right (AMP10xx project, features and lint lines; AMP11xx blocks)
AMP2xxx meaning: the text is shaped right but says something impossible
AMP5xxx environment and runtime: depends on what is installed or what happened (AMP50xx static warnings, AMP51xx regeneration notices)
Lxxx lint rules: compile but probably not what you meant
plugin prefixes (ACE1xxx) codes contributed by a plugin, declared in its manifest, same record shape

Stability: a code is never reused. A retired code stays in the catalogue (retired: true). Each code's stage is static (found by reading the song) or runtime (found by running or regenerating). Messages may be reworded; codes, severity and ranges are the contract.

Severity and blocking

error blocks Apply and leaving the source editor. warning and info never block. A lint rule raised to error blocks like any error.

Ranges

A diagnostic points at the smallest range that is wrong (the parameter name, not the whole line). Where a code can point at two places the range is the one the message talks about; the other is related.

Lint rules

Nine rules in spec 0.1 (see lint-rules.json for names, defaults and descriptions): L001 unused-output, L002 missing-input, L003 lock-and-refresh, L004 overlapping-parts, L005 dynamic-not-fixed, L006 pinned-outdated, L007 no-path-to-master, L008 name-case-clash, L009 custom-seed.

  • Level per rule in the song: lint { L004 error L005 info } (only entries that differ from the default). Unknown rule AMP1007, bad level AMP1008.
  • Suppression: a comment # ample-ignore L004, L005 silences those rules for the next block only. Since 0.5 it silences any warning or note (not only lint rules) by code, in two places: on the line above a block header (which cannot end with a comment), and at the end of a line inside a block, for that line only: program programFor(phase()) # ample-ignore AMP2073. An error is never silenced. The source editor writes these comments for you (the tooltip button Suppress here); Ignore this session only hides the message in the browser until the page is reloaded and changes nothing in the song.
  • Static checks of helper bodies (0.5): a helper is read in every branch, also in the ones that never run: AMP2082 a name that is not a parameter, a variable, a constant or a word of the language (an error inside a calculation, where even a pitch class like b is never a number); AMP2044 a literal return that cannot be what the helper says it returns; AMP2083 a path that ends without a value (an if without an else); AMP2084 a variable never read; AMP2085 a statement that does nothing; AMP2086 a helper no clip, property or helper calls; AMP2087 a call of a helper whose declaration has a syntax error (instead of a second, confusing unknown operator). AMP2084, AMP2085, AMP2086, AMP2087 are notes; all but errors can be silenced with # ample-ignore CODE.
  • Lint runs only on blocks that parsed; it never changes the sound.

Notices about regeneration

AMP5101 (info): regeneration is only guaranteed to give the same result on this machine with the same plugin, model and GPU setup. AMP5102 (warning): the toolprint differs from the one that made the take, or the plugin's determinism is unverified. Both are runtime stage; the exact wording is in diagnostics.json and is shown by the UI, the CLI and the help (regeneration safety).

Output formats

Text (for people), JSON (the record above, one per diagnostic) and SARIF (later). The corpus compares JSON records as a set sorted by (line, col, code).

09 Formatting

The output of the formatter is the canonical form. ample fmt rewrites a file to it; the language server's formatting does the same; the corpus (../../spec-tests/format/ pairs and roundtrip/ files) defines it by example.

Rules (spec 0.1)

  1. UTF-8, \n line endings, no trailing whitespace, exactly one final newline; a BOM is removed.
  2. Indentation is two spaces inside blocks; tabs are replaced.
  3. Blank lines: a run of blank lines collapses to one; blank lines inside a block are kept as one.
  4. Single spaces between words in a header, between a parameter name and its value, and around ->; no space before , and one after it.
  5. Brace lines (project, features, lint) read keyword { pair pair }: one space inside the braces, two spaces between pairs.
  6. A block header ends with {; the closing } is alone on its line.
  7. Comments are preserved exactly, except that trailing whitespace is removed and the line is indented to its context (no indent at top level, two spaces inside a block). A comment after code on the same line is not part of the language (it would make the line unreadable to the parser).
  8. The formatter never reorders statements, parameters or from lines, and never changes values or names.
  9. The formatter is idempotent: formatting its own output changes nothing, and parsing then printing a canonical file gives the same bytes (round trip).

Behaviour on broken input

The formatter formats everything it understands and leaves a line it cannot parse unchanged (besides trailing whitespace and indentation inside blocks). It never refuses.

10 Lyrics format

Status: only partly specified. The own lyric format .amplelrc (all lyric information in one extensible structure: words, line and word timing, syllables, sounds, singers, language, notes; it states format: amplelrc and a version) is decided in principle (decisions, "Lyric formats") but its field-by-field layout is still open design work (open-questions).

What exists (provisional)

The sketch's lyrics block points at a plain file (lyrics/chorus.lyr) with one line per row, written [bar 9] text. The file is the canonical source: the Lyrics editor reads and writes it, and linked AI voice or ACE music blocks receive its marker-free words. The old text parameter remains as a compatibility fallback only when the file is absent or empty; it is not edited by the Lyrics editor. The editor checks live: the first line within 5 seconds, lines in order, lines outside the block's placement, empty lines, long lines, too many words for the gap.

Importers (planned, not part of the grammar)

.lrc, enhanced .lrc, .srt/.vtt, TextGrid and aligner JSON convert to and from .amplelrc.

Plan

This page becomes normative when .amplelrc is designed: a JSON Schema in ../../spec/schema/, a conformance corpus under ../../spec-tests/lyrics/, and the checks listed above as diagnostic codes.

11 Versioning and compatibility

Spec version

../../spec/version.json holds specVersion (major.minor) and status (provisional or settled). A song may state the language version it was written for on its composition line (ample 1); it is optional, and ample migrate moves an older song to the current version.

  • Patch-level wording fixes do not change the version.
  • Minor versions add things in a backward-compatible way (a new template, a new optional parameter, a new diagnostic code).
  • Major versions break compatibility and come with a migration note in CHANGELOG.md.
  • Before 1.0 a minor version may break; every break has a migration note and the tool offers ample migrate once real songs exist.

Stability of the data

  • Diagnostic and lint codes are never reused or renumbered; retired codes stay listed.
  • Template ids are never reused; a template is provisional, stable, deprecated or retired, with since and optionally deprecated (the version and the replacement).
  • The canonical plan form and the stable random generator are frozen once released and carry their own version (rngVersion); see 06.

Compatibility promise (at 1.0)

A song that is valid at 1.x stays valid at every later 1.y and builds to the same take references; deprecated features keep working with a warning for at least one minor version.

File format versions

.amplet, .amplelrc, .ample exports and plugin.json each carry a format version; opening an older format runs a migration with a backup copy first (project-management).

12 - Note pipelines and note bake

Status: built (2026-10-28; spec 0.5): the pipelines, for auto, the bake stage and the live diagnostics are implemented in C# and in the browser. Nothing in this page changes the meaning of a file that parses today: a plain notes literal stays a literal. The page is the contract for two evaluators (JavaScript in the browser, C# on the server) that must agree byte for byte; the shared test corpus is spec-tests/note-pipelines/, the operator catalog is spec/note-ops.json.

1. Idea

Note data is a value. A midi-clip can say where its notes come from with a pipeline instead of a literal:

midi-clip melody at 1 for auto {
  notes take.notes
    |> bars(1..=8)
    |> transpose(-12)
    |> bake lowered {
      input-hash "..."  notes-hash "..."  span 8bars
      notes 1:0:1:48:100 1:1:1:50:100
    }
    |> humanize(timing=20ms, seed=7)
}

The graph keeps its blocks (transpose, quantize, midi-humanize...) for live instrument chains. A pipeline step and the block of the same name use the same operator code (one catalog entry, one implementation per language), so they cannot drift apart.

2. The Notes value

  • Events: at (micro-beats from the origin of the value, may be negative inside a pipeline), len, pitch 0..127, vel 1..127 and the per-note extensions of the compact format (;pan= ;bend= ...), which every operator carries along untouched.
  • Span: the length of the value, needed by concat, loops and window selection. Span is explicit when the source knows it (a bake records it, a window has the length of the window, a clip has its for); otherwise it is the end of the last note rounded up to a whole bar (minimum one bar).
  • A value is never shorter than its notes: after shift, merge and replace the span grows (in whole bars) to cover the furthest note end.
  • Output order is canonical: by at, then pitch, then the order of arrival (stable).
  • Resolving to text: bars are 1-based, a note that crosses a bar line is written as consecutive pieces of the same pitch that share a ;tie=N id (N from 1,000,000 up, unless the note has its own), so they play as one note instead of being struck again (the existing roll convention, see splitAtBars); beats are decimals with up to six places, trailing zeros removed. Notes that start before the origin are dropped with a warning (before-origin).

3. Time model

  • One exact unit: the micro-beat (1 beat = 1_000_000; 1 bar is 4 beats in 4/4 and the beats of the song's meter otherwise). No floating point anywhere: literals are exact decimals (BigInt rationals).
  • Units on quantities: bar/bars, beat/beats, s, ms, ticks (ticks follow the clip's ppq). A unitless number is only legal where the operator says so (transpose(+12) semitones, bar coordinates inside bars(...)).
  • Coordinates and lengths. Inside bars(a..b) / beats(a..b) the numbers are coordinates, 1-based like bar numbers (1 is the start of the first bar, 1.5 the middle of it). Inside time(a..b) they are seconds from the origin (0-based). shift, stretch and other operators take lengths with a unit (shift(+250ms)).
  • Ranges are half-open: bars(1..5) is four bars. bars(1..=4) is the inclusive spelling for whole bars (..= requires an integer end). A fractional position is legal but gives the warning fractional-bar (non-fatal, no automatic fix); ..= with a fraction is read as .. plus the same warning.
  • Seconds and milliseconds convert with the song tempo: micro-beats = round_half_even(seconds * tempo / 60 * 1_000_000), computed as one exact rational. The tempo is part of the hash of every stage that uses seconds. Placement (at, for) stays whole bars (see AMP1104); sub-bar offsets belong in the pipeline.

4. Operators (catalog: spec/note-ops.json)

Kind Operators Meaning
source block.port, literal entries, editable { ... } take.notes reads the notes output of a block (same spelling as from take.notes -> in)
select bars, beats, time, mask (range arguments of remove, cut, replace and mask are written like the select steps: bars(1..2), beats(..), time(..)) bars/beats/time(range) keep the notes that start inside the window, shorten those that run past its end, and move the window start to the origin; the span becomes the window length. mask(range) does the same but keeps positions and the span
delete/insert remove(range), cut(range), replace(range, notes) remove deletes the notes starting in the range and leaves a gap; cut also closes the gap (later notes move earlier, span shrinks); replace removes the range and puts the given notes there (rebased to the start of the range)
transform transpose(st), shift(length) transpose clamps pitch to 0..127 and semitones to +-48, exactly like the block; shift moves every note (negative allowed; notes moved before the start are dropped with a warning)
combine concat(notes), merge(notes) concat puts the argument after the span of the value; merge layers both (span = the longer one)
freeze bake name { ... } see section 6

More operators (all in the catalog, all deterministic, all in both evaluators):

Kind Operators Meaning
transform reverse(), stretch(f), legato(), quantize(grid) mirror inside the span; multiply starts, lengths and span by a factor between 1/64 and 64; every note lasts until the next start; snap starts to a grid (ties to even)
seeded humanize(timing=20ms, velocity=4, seed=7) small changes from a splitmix64 generator seeded by seed (required; the notes are taken in canonical order); the same notes in JavaScript and C#
generate repeat(n), arp(rate), euclid(hits, steps, pitch=, step=, velocity=, rotate=) copies one after the other (n at most 1024); spread chords over their length; a Euclidean rhythm as a source (steps at most 256)
select where(pitch=lo..hi, velocity=lo..hi) keep notes whose pitch/velocity is in the range (half-open, ..= includes the end)

Notes keep their length when shift, humanize or merge move them, so a note can run past the end of the value (the span grows to cover it); legato() leaves the last note as it is. Cut the result with bars(1..=n) (or mask) when a pipeline must end on a bar line. Arguments may be positional or named (name=value). A midi block (a project MIDI file) is a valid source: song.notes reads all its notes (or the chosen track). Every operator declares: parameter types and units, whether it needs a seed, a version (part of every hash), and a cost class. Not yet: chords, scale.

5. Where each kind of error is found

Time Examples
Live, static (no evaluation) syntax, unknown operator (with "did you mean"), arity, argument and unit types, reversed constant range, fractional bar, unknown reference, reference to a non-notes port, reference cycle, invalid literal note, missing seed, stale or dirty bake (hash compare), static upper bound of the event count against the project cap, for auto without a known span
Bake time real note count, empty result, span, fuel and wall-clock use, memory, cap hit, source take missing, notes before the origin, cancellation
Build time rendering, instruments, pinned files, downstream rebuilds

Symbolic ids used by the corpus until codes are allocated: unknown-operator, unknown-reference, reference-cycle, range-reversed, fractional-bar (warning), missing-unit, wrong-unit, bad-argument, before-origin (warning), stale-bake, dirty-bake, cap-events, evaluators-disagree. Codes come from the free ranges (AMP11xx syntax, AMP20xx semantic, AMP57xx runtime) when the parser lands; every static code needs an invalid case in spec-tests/invalid.

6. Bake

|> bake name { ... } stores the output of everything before it in the pipeline.

|> bake lowered {
     strict                      # optional: a manual change is an error instead of a warning
     input-hash "sha256:..."     # recipe hash up to this stage
     notes-hash "sha256:..."     # signature of the stored notes
     span 8bars
     notes 1:0:1:48:100 ...      # or:  file "bakes/melody-lowered.notes"   (any file you choose)
   }
  • Recipe (Merkle) hash. input-hash = hash of the normalized expression up to this stage + operator versions + tempo (when seconds are used) + seeds + the hashes of what it reads: a baked block or stage contributes its stored notes-hash, an unbaked formula its own recipe hash, a MIDI file its file hash. Staleness therefore needs no evaluation and is visible while typing.
  • Signature. notes-hash signs the stored data (inline or in the file). A manual change makes the stage dirty: warning, or error with strict. Fixes: Accept (re-sign; the stage becomes editable or is detached into a literal) or Re-bake (revert).
  • States: fresh, stale (recipe changed), dirty (data changed), editable (owned by hand), detached (bake removed, notes kept as a literal).
  • Build policy: a bake is authoritative: downstream uses the stored notes (reproducible); a stale bake warns and offers Re-bake, Detach, Use live formula. Unbaked pipelines are evaluated by the build (pure, capped) and their resolved-notes hash goes into the plan id.
  • Edits live only in literals (editable { notes ... } or a detached bake), never as a patch over derived output.
  • Naming: the block header flag bake (freeze a take) and the plan intent bake keep their meaning; this feature is called note bake.

6b. Randomness

Seeds, forks, streams and every seeded operator share one model, described in 13-randomness.md. The recipe hash of a pipeline contains the master-seed when it uses stable(...).

7. Limits

Three numbers guard a pipeline: the limit of the server (2,000,000 notes, fixed), the limit of the project (default 200,000 when building and 100,000 in the editor; raise it on purpose with settings { notes.maxEvents 500000 }, never past the server's limit) and a time budget of 30 seconds. A static upper bound (a repeat multiplies, a concat adds) warns before anything runs (AMP2037); repeat, arp and every step check the real size before they build it (AMP5701).

Server hard cap (configuration only) > project setting (lower default, raisable up to the hard cap on purpose) > file or section directive (may use what the project allows). Counters: events, fuel steps, wall clock, memory. Loops exist only with constant bounds; there is no while, so an endless loop cannot be written. A bake is evaluated into a temporary result, validated, then committed in one journaled write; cancel or failure leaves the source untouched.

8. Two evaluators

The JavaScript evaluator (web/lib/note-pipeline.mjs) serves the live editor, Jam and the preview. The C# evaluator is authoritative: it runs on save, on "Verify", before a bake commit and in the build. Both run the same corpus; a disagreement is the diagnostic evaluators-disagree with both hashes and never silently picks one. Builds never depend on the JavaScript result.

9. Compatibility

  • A notes value that starts with a digit entry (1:0:...) or { is the literal it always was; a value that starts with an identifier or ( is an expression. Existing songs, demos and plan ids do not change, and the midi-clip renderer keeps its version: the build resolves an expression to the same notes JSON the literal path produces.
  • New syntax is additive in a minor spec version; older tools see an unknown parameter value, never a changed meaning.

13 - Seeds and randomness

Status: built, on the note pipelines (page 12). Everything here is deterministic: the same song gives the same notes on every machine, in JavaScript and in C#, and a song never changes because something unrelated changed.

1. The model in one page

Thing What it is Has state? Depends on
seed a 64-bit key, a point in a tree of keys no master-seed (for stable), nothing (for explicit seeds)
stable("name") the key of a song-global namespace no master-seed + name
.fork("label") a child key of any seed no parent key + label
seed=123456 an explicit, pinned seed no only the number
draw one value from a seed: draw(key, purpose, address) no key + what is drawn + where
random-stream a named counter over one seed, declared in a clip yes (a cursor) seed + number of earlier next() calls in that clip
random-seed() "pick one for me" no OS randomness once, then stored as an explicit seed

Rules that follow:

  • Keys are derived by hashing, not by seed + offset: key' = first 8 bytes of SHA-256("ample-seed/1" \n kind \n parent \n label). A fork is a path, not a cursor. stable("verse").fork("chords") written in three places is the same key in all three, and none of them shares a hidden next().
  • A draw is addressed: draw = first 8 bytes of SHA-256("ample-seed/1" \n "draw" \n key \n purpose \n address). The address is the explicit round= of a call, or, inside a per-note operator, the identity of the note (start:pitch:duplicate). It is never "the n-th random call so far". Adding a random call (or a note) somewhere else cannot move any other stable result.
  • Only a stream has an order. random-stream chords stable("verse").fork("chords") declares a counter; chords.next() is random(seed=<that seed>, round=<cursor>) and then the cursor moves. Streams are declared in a clip (never inline), start at 0 every time the clip is worked out, and are reported in the provenance (seed and how many values were consumed).
  • stable follows the master-seed, explicit seeds do not. Change master-seed and every stable result becomes a new, again reproducible, variant; seed=123456 stays exactly as it was.
  • The recipe hash of a pipeline (and so every bake) contains the master-seed whenever the pipeline uses stable(...) (directly or through a stream or a clip it reads). Changing the master-seed therefore makes such bakes stale, the same way changing the tempo does for seconds.

2. What is part of the identity of a random result (and what is not)

In the derivation Not in the derivation
master-seed (only through stable) the name of the block or clip
the stable name and the fork labels where the clip sits in the song (at, for)
the purpose (humanize.timing, thin, random...) the order in which things are worked out
the address (round, or note identity, or bar) other random calls, other notes

So: renaming a block, moving it, or adding a random call elsewhere never changes the music. Renaming or re-labelling a stable name does (that is the point of a name), and the editor warns when a name is used only once and looks like a typo of another.

Per-note identity is start:pitch:duplicate in the notes the operator receives (clip-relative micro-beats). Adding or removing other notes does not move a note's draw; moving the note itself does, because it is a different note.

3. Syntax

seed=123456                          # explicit, pinned
seed=stable("verse")                 # follows master-seed
seed=stable("verse").fork("drums")   # a branch; forks nest: .fork("a").fork("b")
seed=stable("verse").fork(3)         # a fork label may be a whole number
seed=random-seed()                   # unresolved until you pick one (fix: "Pick a seed"); then it is an explicit seed

Values:

random(0..100, seed=S, round=0)            # whole number, half-open (..= includes the end); decimals and lengths work too: random(10ms..40ms, seed=S)
choose(a, b, c, seed=S, round=2)           # one of the listed values
chance(0.25, seed=S, round=4)              # 1 with that probability, else 0

The same seed, purpose and round always give the same value; another round gives another (stable) value. round defaults to 0.

Streams (declared in a clip, used in that clip):

midi-clip x at 1 for auto {
  random-stream drift stable("verse").fork("drift")
  notes a.notes |> shift(drift.next(0ms..=30ms)) |> transpose(drift.next(-2..=2))
}

Operators that use seeds (all in the operator catalog, all with seed=, all with the same model): humanize(timing=, velocity=, seed=), randomize(velocity=lo..hi, pitch=lo..=hi, seed=), thin(0.25, seed=, per=note|bar), scramble(seed=), and the generator walk(root, scale, steps=, step=, octave=, range=, seed=).

Helpers that keep notes out of a range or a set: clamp(lo..=hi) (cap at a ceiling and a floor), fold(lo..=hi) (move by octaves into the range, keeps the note name), snap(root, scale) (to the nearest scale tone), keep(root, scale) and avoid(root, scale) (drop notes inside / outside the scale). Generators: chords("Am F C G", length=1bar, octave=4) and scale(root, kind, steps=8, step=0.5beat, octave=4).

4. Declared or implicit stable names?

Implicit on first use (chosen). A name is only a label of a branch in the key tree, so nothing has to exist before it is used, and a name used in two clips is the same namespace by construction. The risk is a typo that silently starts a new namespace; the editor answers that with a warning when a name is used once and is within two edits of a name used elsewhere ("did you mean ..."), with a quick fix. A declared registry would add ceremony for every name and would not stop a typo in the declaration. Inspect: hover shows the key and the namespaces list; ample seeds and the "Where does the randomness come from?" item of the roll list every use with its derived key and how many values were drawn.

5. Copy and duplicate

Stable names are song-global. When a clip that uses stable(...) is copied the editor asks, with the impact in words:

  1. Reuse - keep the names: the copy plays exactly the same random choices (use it when the copy should match).
  2. Fork - append .fork("copy-n") to every stable seed of the copy: still derived from the same parents, but its own deterministic branch (use it for a variation that stays related).
  3. Independent - new song-global names (pulse_2, pulse_3, ...), one consistent mapping per copy: a fully separate family.

Explicit seeds (seed=123456) are copied as they are (they have no name to fork); the dialog says so.

6. Edge cases

  • Detach / bake / editable: a baked or detached clip is plain notes; the randomness is frozen into them. Re-baking re-runs the same derivation, so it gives the same notes unless a seed, the master-seed (for stable) or the pipeline changed, and then the bake is stale (AMP2030) and says why.
  • Master-seed change: all stable results change; explicit seeds do not; bakes that use stable become stale.
  • random-seed(): never hidden. Until it is replaced by a number the pipeline refuses to build (AMP2039), with a fix that picks one (OS randomness, once) and writes it into the song. From then on it is an ordinary explicit seed.
