30. Fix stale     |> bake old {…}  ⚠ stale: its recipe changed   💡 Re-bake · Detach · Use live expression

17. Design decisions and the naming rules

Decided after a critical read of the draft; each point says what was kept and why.

  1. "Total" is the wrong word. With bounded loops, recursion guarded by stack depth and fuel, and limits that end an evaluation with an error, the language terminates (always a value or a diagnosed failure), but it is not total in the technical sense. The word is now "bounded, resource-safe".
  2. Effects. The effect axis is pure/dynamic only. Seeded randomness is reproducible, so it is a dependency (with master-seed, tempo, clock, os-random), not an effect. seed=7 and stable("x") both "use randomness"; only the second depends on the master-seed. Dependencies are inferred transitively per helper and exposed to tooling (HelperInfo.Dependencies). Effects are always inferred; the declaration is a required permission (point 6).
  3. Length / Time. Two dimensions, stored in their own base unit (beats and seconds); conversion needs the tempo and the recipe records the tempo when, and only when, a time in seconds is converted. The earlier wording ("Length is tempo independent") was too simple.
  4. Float to Int is an error (page section 3). There was no compatibility reason for the implicit rounding; it contradicted "a fix never changes the music silently".
  5. Identity. Build identity is content-addressed (resolved values), bake identity is dependency-addressed (recipe). Not one or the other: they answer different questions (section 8 and the two-identities note).
  6. Dynamic helpers are explicit. A helper whose body (or callee) is dynamic and that is not declared dynamic is an error with the fix Mark helper dynamic. dynamic over-declaration (declared dynamic, nothing dynamic inside) is allowed: it is an upper-bound assertion, useful while a helper is being written. The status of a song never trusts the declaration: it uses the inferred effect.
  7. Names. Helpers, functions and built-ins are lowerCamelCase (canonVoice, randomSeed, currentTime); types, conversions and constructors are TitleCase (Notes, Int, Round, Note); blocks and resources keep their kebab-case. A kebab-case helper name is a lint (AMP2076 family: helper-naming, fix: the camelCase spelling); random-seed() stays as a deprecated alias of randomSeed() with a warning.
  8. Hyphens in expressions. In an expression, a-b is never silently one name and never silently a subtraction. Resolution: if only the symbol a-b exists (a block, a constant ...) it is that symbol; if only a and b exist it is an error with the fix a - b; if both exist it is ambiguous (AMP2074) with the fixes a - b and [a-b]; if neither exists it is unknown. [name-with-hyphens] is the escaped symbol (it is also how a block with a hyphen is referenced when ambiguity exists: [lead-main].notes). It collides with the list literal only for a one-element list of an unspaced subtraction: [a-b] is always the symbol; write [a - b] or [a-b,] for the list. Name positions (block headers, from lines) keep working without brackets.
  9. Records and generics. Wording fixed: no user-defined records or generics; Note, List<T>, Range<T> are built in.
  10. emit and return. Kept the rule (a bare return is the early exit); the merge semantics are written down in section 4. build { } was a leftover of an earlier draft and is not part of the language.
  11. Module hashing. Per-helper semantic hash plus the hashes of what it references; the module is provenance only (section 2).
  12. environment() stays, behind the capability model of page 16 (off by default, forbiddable by the server, never re-enabled below a forbidden scope).
  13. Limits. Reworded: every potentially unbounded construct has a finite effective limit; the effective limit and where it comes from are part of the document (Document.Limits) and shown in hover.
  14. Two concrete problems (pickRegister returning an Octave used as a GM program; a helper called stretch-by that shifts) were real: the first is now a type error (values keep the musical type they were made as), the second was a name; it is delayBy.

Conditions: true-ish values, !, &&, || and cond ? a : b (E1)

A condition (if, while, !, &&, || and the condition of ?:) reads a value with one rule, truthiness:

Value Counts as true when
Bool it is true
Int, Float it is not 0
a quantity (a length, a time, an interval, a gain, a percent) its number is not 0 (0ms and 0% are false)
String, a symbol (a bare word) it is not empty
List it has items
Range it is not empty (3..3 is empty, 3..=3 is not)
Notes it has at least one note
a single Note, a seed, a random stream, a time of day always true

!a is not truthy(a). a && b and a || b give true or false (never one of the operands), and stop at the first operand that decides (the other side is not worked out). c ? x : y works out only the branch that is taken; the two branches may have different types (the type of the expression is the union, the hover shows it), it is right associative (a ? b : c ? d : e) and a branch is a whole pipeline (a ? b : c |> d pipes the second branch). Write parentheses to pipe the whole conditional: (a ? b : c) |> d. A condition that is not a Bool is allowed (that is the point of the rule); to be strict write the comparison (n != 0, len(list) > 0).

15. The musical type model (design, with the first part being built)

Status: the parts M1-M4 below (typed catalogue, static checker, spans, typed completion) are built; the helper language of page 14 builds on them. Page 14 section 3 is the general type system, this page is the musical vocabulary on top of it.

1. Goal and non-goals

Three things, nothing more: (1) find mistakes early (walk(123, "minor", steps="sixteen", step=7) is wrong before anything runs), (2) give completion, hover and fixes the exact set of valid values, (3) make musical intent explicit without a heavier syntax. A type is only worth having if it buys one of these.

2. Opinion: the minimal strong model

Concept Decision Why
PitchClass (C, C#, Db ... B) a type (a closed vocabulary of 12 classes, spelling remembered for display) needed by walk/scale/snap/keep/avoid/chords; 123 and "C" must be rejected
Root, NoteName not types, the parameter name says "root" a second name for the same vocabulary only adds noise to hovers
Pitch (C5, F#3, 60) a type = pitch class + octave = MIDI 0..127; bare Int accepted with an info + fix where(pitch=...), clamp, fold, euclid(pitch=)
Octave refinement alias Int 0..=9, not a value kind the range check and the completion (2..6 first) are the benefit; no operations of its own
Velocity refinement alias Int 1..=127 same
Count refinement alias Int 1.. (steps, hits, times, voices) catches 0, negatives and "sixteen"
ScaleMode (major, minor, dorian ...) a type, a closed enum from spec/scales.json a bare word, never a string
Scale (root + mode as one value) not yet root and mode stay two parameters (backwards compatible); a Scale value earns its place when helpers pass keys around: planned, not built
Chord, Chords (List<Chord>) types; a chord token (Cm, Ab, G7, F#m7b5, C/E) is parsed once; chords("Cm Ab") keeps working (a string literal is parsed against the expected type) helpers need not pass strings around, and the checker can underline the one bad chord
Interval a quantity of pitch distance, stored as an exact rational number of semitones, with units st, oct, cents see 3
Duration = Length | Time, Length, Time as page 14 see 4
Probability refinement of Float 0..=1; 25% converts to 0.25 thin, chance
Range<T> typed range (1..=4 is Range<Int>, 0ms..=40ms is Range<Duration>, -5..=5 is Range<Interval>) random, randomize, where, selectors
RandomSource = Seed | StableSeed | RandomStream as page 13/14 seed=
Notes, Note as page 14

Overkill, left out on purpose: separate Semitones/Cents types (they are units of Interval), Frequency, Tempo, TimeSignature (the meter is a setting of the composition line), Degree, Voicing, user generics. A union is only used where two members really are interchangeable (Duration, RandomSource, Number); there is no String | Int | Float anywhere in the musical API, and a String is never accepted where a vocabulary type is expected, except a quoted literal of that vocabulary (compatibility, with a warning and a fix).

Words are resolved by the expected type

A bare word in an argument is not a string: it is looked up in the vocabulary of the expected type. In a ScaleMode slot minor is a mode; in a PitchClass slot C is a pitch class; in a Chords slot Cm is a chord. A variable of the right type wins over a vocabulary member with the same name (and a lint warns about the shadowing). That gives exact completion (walk(C, | offers modes only), exact errors with nearest suggestions (mnor → minor) and no magic identifiers.

3. Interval

transpose(+7) today means semitones. I would not fix it to Int: an Interval is an exact rational number of semitones with units st (semitones, default), oct (12 st) and cents (1/100 st): +7st, -1oct, 50cents. Bare numbers keep working in an Interval slot and mean semitones (silently: transpose(+12) is idiomatic; the hover shows +12 -> +12st; AMP2047 is reserved and unused). Note events have integer pitches, so an operator that needs a whole number of semitones (transpose) reports a fractional interval (+50cents) as an error for now (AMP2048 "microtonal needs pitch bend, which note events do not carry yet"): the type already allows microtonal values, only the consumer is restricted. Named intervals (P5, m3) can be added as vocabulary later without touching the model.

4. Durations, tempo, hashing

0.5beat, 2bars, 250ms, 1.5s are exact quantities (rational, not floats) with a dimension: Length (bars, beats, ticks: independent of tempo) and Time (s, ms: depends on tempo). Duration accepts both, so walk(..., step=0.5beat) and step=250ms are both valid. A Time value turns into beats with the song tempo with a fixed rule (round half to even); the recipe hash then contains the tempo (already so for seconds in page 12), and the hover says "depends on tempo". A bare number in a Duration slot is an error with the fix "add a unit" offering beat, bar, ms, s (S2: the choice changes the music). Where only a Length makes sense (bars(1..5) positions, quantize grid), a Time value gets the conversion fix with the value at the current tempo.

5. Spans: known, derived, unresolved

Every midi-clip value gets a span class that the checker computes without running the notes:

  • Known: plain literal or editable notes, a stored bake: the span is a constant.
  • Derived: built only from static quantities (generators with literal arguments, operators with literal arguments over known/derived inputs): the span follows by arithmetic, for example walk(... steps=16, step=0.5beat) is 8 beats and therefore 2 bars.
  • Unresolved until evaluation: depends on another block's evaluated notes, a file, a MIDI source, a dynamic call or a loop with a non-constant bound.

Hover shows the class and value (for auto · derived: 16 × 0.5 beat = 2 bars).

Downstream for auto: an instrument (gm, synth, piano, sampler, bass, guitar, delay-llama) may say for auto and then inherits the span of the notes that feed it (the longest, rounded up to whole bars). A fixed for N that differs from the statically known or derived span of its only source gets info AMP2049 ("the clip is 2 bars, this block says 4") with the fix Use auto span (S2: it can shorten a tail on purpose). A literal for is not nagged when the source is unresolved, and no aggressive warning is given when a derived span could simply have been written by hand.

6. The typed catalogue (before / after)

spec/note-ops.json gets a types section (vocabularies, refinements, units) and every parameter a type from this page. The C# checker, the web completion and the docs read the same file. Examples of the new signatures:

walk(PitchClass root, ScaleMode scale, Count steps = 16, Duration step = 0.5beat, Octave octave = 5,
     Count range = 2, Velocity velocity = 90, RandomSource seed) -> Notes
scale(PitchClass root, ScaleMode scale, Count steps = 8, Duration step = 0.5beat, Octave octave = 4, Velocity velocity = 90) -> Notes
chords(Chords chords, Length length = 1bar, Octave octave = 3, Velocity velocity = 80) -> Notes
euclid(Count hits, Count steps, Pitch pitch = 36, Duration step = 0.25beat, Velocity velocity = 90, Int rotate = 0) -> Notes
arp(Duration rate) -> Notes -> Notes              shift(Duration by) -> Notes -> Notes
transpose(Interval by) -> Notes -> Notes          stretch(Number factor) -> Notes -> Notes
humanize(Duration timing, Velocity velocity, RandomSource seed) -> Notes -> Notes
thin(Probability p, RandomSource seed, per = note|bar) -> Notes -> Notes
choose(List<T> options, RandomSource seed, Int round = 0) -> T        chance(Probability p, RandomSource seed, Int round = 0) -> Int
snap/keep/avoid(PitchClass root, ScaleMode scale) -> Notes -> Notes     clamp/fold(Range<Pitch> range) -> Notes -> Notes

Before and after:

# before: all of this is accepted by the parser and fails (or silently misbehaves) later
midi-clip m at 1 for 2 {
  notes walk(123, "minor", steps="sixteen", step=7, octave=5.5, seed=stable("melody"))
    |> transpose(+7.5)
    |> humanize(timing=20, velocity=300, seed=stable("melody"))
}
gm m-play at 1 for 4 { from m.notes -> notes }

# after: five precise diagnostics at the exact ranges, each with a fix
#  walk(123 ...)           AMP2044  123 is not a PitchClass (C, C#, Db ... B)              fix: C, D, E ...
#  "minor"                 AMP2045  a quoted word where ScaleMode is expected              fix: minor (S0)
#  steps="sixteen"         AMP2044  sixteen is not a Count (a whole number, 1 or more)
#  step=7                  AMP2046  a Duration needs a unit                                fix: 7beat / 7bar / 7ms / 7s (S2)
#  octave=5.5              AMP2050  an Octave is a whole number from 0 to 9                fix: Round(5.5) (S1) / 5 / 6
#  transpose(+7.5)         AMP2048  a fractional interval needs microtonal support         (hover: +7.5st = 750 cents)
#  velocity=300            AMP2044  300 is not a Velocity (1..=127)
#  timing=20               AMP2046  a Duration needs a unit                                fix: 20ms
#  gm m-play ... for 4     AMP2049  the clip is 2 bars (known), this block says 4          fix: Use auto span
midi-clip m at 1 for auto {
  notes walk(C, minor, steps=16, step=0.5beat, octave=5, seed=stable("melody"))
    |> transpose(+7st)
    |> humanize(timing=20ms, velocity=8, seed=stable("melody"))
}
gm m-play at 1 for auto { from m.notes -> notes }
# before: chord strings everywhere
notes chords("Cm Ab Bb Cm", length=1bar, octave=3, velocity=70)      # keeps working
# after: the same, parsed to typed Chords at check time; a helper can take them as a type
helper bed(Chords progression, Octave octave = 3) -> Notes { chords(progression, octave=octave, length=1bar) }   # helper phase
notes chords("Cm Ab Xq Cm")      # AMP2044  "Xq" is not a chord symbol: it must start with a root, underlined on that token only

7. IntelliSense that follows from the types

  • walk( offers the PitchClass vocabulary (and variables of that type); walk(C, offers ScaleMode only; step= offers duration units and snippets (0.5beat, 250ms, 1/3beat); octave= offers 2..6 first; seed= offers stable("…"), forks of known names, explicit numbers and streams of the clip.
  • After |> the left type decides (page 14), and each candidate shows its typed signature; hover on an argument shows its type, and "converted" when a bare number became an Interval or a Duration (for example +7 → +7st).
  • Signature help lists the real parameter types, defaults and the return type, marks the current parameter, and shows an info line when a conversion applies.

8. Plan and status

Chunk Content State
M1 types section and typed parameters in spec/note-ops.json (+ schema/validate-spec) built
M2 C# static checker (NoteTypes): arity, names, vocabulary, refinements, units, ranges, seeds, chord strings, diagnostics AMP2044–AMP2050, fixes, invalid-corpus cases, tests built
M3 span classes, for auto on instruments, AMP2049, Use auto span built
M4 web: typed catalogue module, typed completion, signature help, hover (JS reads the same spec) built
M5 Scale value, named intervals, microtonal pitch bend not built

16. Capabilities and the policy chain (design, with the first part being built)

Status: the effective-policy resolver, the settings syntax, the gating of the volatile built-ins and the diagnostics are built; network, filesystem, external-process and external-plugin are reserved names: the policy knows them, nothing in the language uses them yet (every future feature that touches the outside world must ask the policy first).

1. Why

AMPLE songs are programs. Part of the language reaches outside the song: the clock, OS randomness, the environment of the machine, and later the network, files, other processes and plugins. On a public playground or a shared server, the owner of the server must be able to say "none of that", and no song, no AI proposal and no later line of the same song may take it back. A capability is a permission, never a value.

2. The model

Capability Gates Default Notes
clock currentTime(), currentDate() on volatile; a dynamic helper is still required
os-random osRandom() on volatile
environment environment(name) off sensitive: the environment holds secrets; volatile
network (reserved) off
filesystem (reserved) off
external-process (reserved) off
external-plugin (reserved) off

Every capability has two independent bits at each level of the chain:

  • ceiling (server only): may this capability ever be used here? allow or forbid. Nobody below can change it.
  • setting (server default, project, song): on, off or unset (inherit).

The chain and the monotone rule

server ceiling + server default
   ↓ (project settings, when the host provides them)
project
   ↓ (settings { capabilities.environment off } lines, in source order)
song

Walk the settings of the chain in order, starting from the server default v:

  1. off at any level: v = off and the capability is locked off from here on.
  2. on at any level: if the ceiling forbids it, error ("disabled by server policy"); if the capability is locked off, error ("turned off earlier by …: a capability cannot be turned on again"); otherwise v = on.
  3. The effective value is ceiling ∧ v.

So a lower scope can only narrow: it can turn something off (for itself and everything below), it can turn on only what the scopes above allow and have not turned off. An explicit off in a song is a one-way door: a later on in the same song is a fatal configuration error (AMP2076); the capability stays off. off after on is fine (narrowing).

An unset capability that is off by default is not locked: the song may switch it on (when the ceiling allows). Only an explicit off locks.

Security settings are monotone, resources are not

Capabilities (and any future sandbox switch) follow the monotone rule: once forbidden above, never allowed below. Limits (limits.fuel, limits.stack-depth ...) follow a different rule on purpose: a song may ask for more or less than the default, up to the cap of the server (doc 14, section 6); only the cap is a hard ceiling. A resource is a quantity to be negotiated, a capability is an authority.

3. Syntax

settings {
  capabilities.environment on
  capabilities.network off
}

capabilities.<name> on|off; names are checked (unknown name → AMP2076 with did-you-mean). Several settings lines are read in order. A line the host injects above the song (a protected prologue) is read first, with the same semantics, but a host that needs enforcement must not rely on source text alone: it passes a server policy (ceiling and default) next to the song, because source text can be edited. Both are supported; the policy cannot be undone by any text.

Allow-lists (built for environment): capabilities.environment.allow "TZ, AMPLE_*" lists the names environment() may read (patterns: NAME, PREFIX*, *SUFFIX, *PART*, *). Every scope can add a list (server: ample serve --environment-allow TZ,AMPLE_*; project and song: the setting above) and a name must match every list, so a lower scope can only narrow, never widen. A name outside the lists is capability-denied at the call (AMP2077) with the lists named. Any other capability has no allow-list yet (capabilities.network.allow is the same idea for hosts, later).

The project layer is built: ProjectSettings.Capabilities in .ample/project.json ({ "environment": "off", "environment.allow": "AMPLE_*" }) is read when the project opens and sits between the server and the song for every parse.

4. Diagnostics and tooling

  • Using a gated feature while it is off is an error that says why, never "unknown function": AMP2077 "Capability environment is off by default: enable it with settings { capabilities.environment on }", "… is disabled by server policy", "… was permanently disabled by this song (line 3)". The same check runs statically on every helper body, so an unused helper with environment() is reported too.
  • Hover on a gated name shows the capability, its effective state and the decisive scope.
  • Completion keeps gated names but marks them: environment (off: disabled by server policy), sorted last. Hiding them would make "why is it missing" a mystery; showing them with the reason is the better UX.
  • The document exposes Capabilities (name, effective, deciding scope, reason) so the web editor, the LSP and Koda read one source.
  • Koda / AI proposals may not turn a capability on or remove an off line, and may not raise a limit above the caps; the assistant text says so, and the proposal check refuses a draft that widens the policy (a proposal is untrusted input).
  • A song whose policy denies a capability that one of its helpers needs is not silently degraded: the helper fails with AMP2077 and the clip shows the error.

5. What the parser, the evaluators and the server do

Layer Change
Parser reads capabilities.* settings in order (the settings dictionary alone loses the order), resolves the effective policy, reports AMP2076 (configuration) and, per helper, AMP2077 (denied use)
C# evaluator Context.Capabilities; currentTime, currentDate, osRandom, environment check it and fail with the reason; a denied call never reads anything
JS twin the same option, the same errors; environment reads an injected function (the browser has no environment: it returns "needs-server")
LSP / web hover, completion detail and the signature note use Document.Capabilities
Server passes the server policy (ceiling and default) into every parse; a public playground sets forbid for everything sensitive and ignores song text that tries otherwise; a future project policy file feeds the project level
Sandboxing capabilities are the language-level gate; OS-level isolation (process limits, no network namespace) stays the host's job: the policy is a contract for the evaluator, not a replacement for a sandbox

6. Open questions

  • Pattern allow-lists for network hosts and filesystem roots (the environment one is built).
  • A UI for the project layer (today it is the project file).
  • Whether clock and os-random should be forbiddable on a deterministic-only server (they can: ceiling forbid); a song using them then fails with AMP2077, which is the intended "fully reproducible only" mode.

17 - Notes: what every note needs, writing them as formulas, and proving nothing changed

Status: built. This page is the check that the built-in operators can write anything a note, and every setting of a note, needs; how the assistant finds the shortest way to write notes; and how "the result is the same" is proved instead of hoped for.

1. What a note is, and where each part can be written

Part of a note In the notes text How a formula makes or changes it
start, length bar:beat:length (beats are exact decimals, 6 places; in ticks when the clip or channel has ppq) shift, stretch, quantize, legato, humanize(timing=...), bars/beats/time/mask/cut/remove/replace, reverse, repeat, concat, merge; generators euclid, chords, scale, walk; the rhythm of a literal
pitch pitch transpose, snap/keep/avoid, clamp, fold, randomize(pitch=...), scramble, set(pitch=...) (a number, a note name like C4, or a list that cycles)
velocity velocity randomize(velocity=...), humanize(velocity=...), set(velocity=...)
channel, bank, program :channel:bank:program set(channel=, bank=, program=) (channel=-1 takes the routing away)
tie (a note over a bar line) ;tie=N on each piece written by the pipeline itself: a note that crosses a bar line is written as tied pieces, so it plays as one note
pan, fine tuning, release, cut, slide, portamento, bend ;pan= ;fine= ;rel= ;cut= ;slide= ;port= ;bend= set(pan=, fine=, rel=, cut=, slide=, port=, bend=) (rel=-1 takes the release away); a setting that is its default is left out
bend and controllers of a channel (CC 7, 11, 10, 64, pitch bend) <channel>.events row of a sequencer pattern (bar:tick:c|p:data1:data2) data, not formulas: they come from an import and are edited as data
clip: ppq, bend curve and bend_range parameters of the midi-clip auto(...) curves for bend

Not covered, by design: tempo-dependent meters (one meter for the whole song: meter on the composition line), tempo changes inside a song (an import puts the notes at their real time at the first tempo), and anything that is not a note (audio). A pipeline works in exact micro-beats; a tick of a MIDI file that is not a whole number of micro-beats is rounded, at most 0.5 micro-beat, far below one sample.

The check. NotePatternsTests writes random notes with every one of these settings in any mix (150 notes over 20 bars, over bar lines, with and without routing) and requires that NotePatterns.Find gives an expression that was evaluated and compared with the notes it came from and is the same. If a setting or a shape could not be written, that test would fail.

2. set(...)

notes |> set(pitch="38 50 45", velocity="105 82") gives the first note pitch 38 and velocity 105, the second 50 and 82, the third 45 and 105, and starts the lists again after the last value. The order of the notes is their start, then their pitch (before the change), so chords are handled in a fixed order. A single number sets every note. The keys are pitch velocity pan fine rel cut slide port bend channel bank program; every value is checked against the range of the setting (program must be from 0 to 127). Notes keep when they sound: set never moves or lengthens a note.

The shape that compresses best is a rhythm that repeats plus values that cycle:

1:0:0.5:38:100 1:0.75:0.25:50:100 1:1.5:0.5:45:100 |> bars(1..=1) |> repeat(32) |> set(pitch="38 50 45 50 43 55 45 55", velocity="105 82 91")

bars(1..=1) fixes the length of the rhythm at one bar, so repeat(32) puts the copies exactly one bar apart.

3. Formula rows in a sequencer

A row of a sequencer pattern that starts with = is a formula: a note pipeline that is worked out for that pattern (its bar 1 is the first bar of the pattern, the tempo of the song is used for lengths in seconds). A formula row has no helpers and no references to clips (only literals, generators and operators); long formulas that need helpers belong in a midi-clip. The sequencer, the build, the check of the assistant (AiService.ProblemsOf, which reports a bad row as AMP5380 with the reason) and ample_resolve_notes all read a row the same way (SequenceRows.TryRead); a new reader of rows must use it too (regression 2026-10-28, see AGENTS.md section 3). In the sequencer window a formula row shows ƒ formula and an Edit formula button; the roll opens only rows of notes.

4. Finding the shape (ample_find_patterns)

ample_find_patterns block=<midi-clip or sequencer> [channel=<name>] cuts the notes into windows of p bars (p from 1 to 16, and the whole length), keeps the periods where no note goes over the end of a window, and writes each as a pipeline: one segment per run of windows with the same rhythm, each rhythm |> bars(1..=p) |> repeat(m) |> set(...), joined with merge(... |> shift(n bars)). Only the settings that differ from the rhythm get a list, and a list is cut to its smallest cycle. Every candidate is evaluated and compared with the original notes (section 5); verified: true means every note, length and setting is the same. The shortest verified candidate comes first, and the answer says how much shorter it is. For a sequencer it gives a formula row per pattern and the channels that play exactly the same notes.

What it does not find: a motif that rises by a constant step, or is transposed per bar, or an arpeggio built from chords. Those need a helper (14-helpers-types-and-dynamic.md, a for loop with emit); the assistant writes it and proves it with ample_resolve_notes (its expression can call the helpers declared in the song). When nothing shorter exists the answer says so, and the notes stay: a performance that was played by a person (all the velocities different) is often not mathematical.

5. The same, exactly (ample_resolve_notes)

Notes of a clip, of a sequencer channel (over the whole playlist) or of a pipeline are read into one form (NoteSemantics): start and length in absolute micro-beats, every setting, the pieces of a tied note put together. Two lists are the same when every note of one has its note in the other with the same pitch, velocity, routing and settings, and its start and length differ by at most 2 micro-beats. The answer says what is missing, extra or changed. ample_import_score compress=true uses the same check before it writes a formula row.

6. A score in pieces, short

The import of a score writes patterns of bars_per_pattern bars; a pattern that says exactly what an earlier one says is not written again (the playlist plays the earlier one), a pattern that shares most rows with an earlier one is a variation (from=) that lists only what differs, and with compress=true a row is a verified formula when that is at least 40 percent shorter.

18 - Comments, doc comments and the hover

Status: built. What a comment can be, how a helper, a constant or a block says what it is for, and what the editor shows when a name is pointed at.

1. Comments

Form Meaning
# text a comment to the end of the line (a # right after a letter or digit is not a comment)
/* text */ a block comment: it can stand inside a line or cover many lines

A block comment is read as blanks (the lines, columns and offsets stay the same), so everything else in the file reads as it did. A /* inside a string, after a #, or right after a letter or digit (4/*2 is a division) starts nothing. A comment that is never closed is AMP1116 (it would swallow the rest of the file). The document keeps the comments: the editors and the edits see the original text; # ample-ignore CODE works as before.

Limits, by design: a block comment cannot be nested, and tools that read the raw text without the parser (the replace and rename edits) still see code that is commented out with /* */ as code.

2. Doc comments

A doc comment is /** ... */, or lines that start with ##, directly above (no blank line) a helper, a let constant, a type alias or a block:

/**
 * Moves a voice up and delays it.
 * @param {Interval|Int} by how far up, in semitones
 * @param Notes source the notes to copy
 * @param delay when the copy starts
 * @return {Notes} the copy, shifted
 * @example theme.notes |> canonVoice(+7st)
 */
helper canonVoice(Notes source, Interval by, Duration delay = 2bars) -> Notes { ... }

## The bass line of the chorus.
## @deprecated use bass2 instead
midi-clip bass at 1 for auto { ... }
Tag Meaning
text before the first tag the summary
@param [type] name text what a parameter means; the type is optional (below)
@return [type] text (or @returns) what the helper gives back
@example code an example (the lines that follow belong to it)
@deprecated [text] the name should not be used any more

Types and unions. A type may be written in braces ({Interval|Int}, {List<Int>}, {Int?}) or bare when it is a type of the language, a union or a generic (@param Notes source ...). A bare first word that is not a type (@param source the notes) is the name. The hover shows the declared type of a parameter and adds (documented as Interval|Int) when the comment gives another one, so a comment can say more than the declaration (a union the helper really accepts) without changing the song. The type is documentation, but it is checked against the declaration (section 3).

3. The checks: a doc comment must not lie

Only a helper that has a doc comment is checked, so a song without doc comments gets nothing new. The warnings are reported on the declaration of the helper (so # ample-ignore CODE on the line above silences one) and are part of the normal check, so the assistant sees them too. They do not stop a build.

Code Level What
AMP2090 warning a @param names a parameter the helper does not have (renamed or removed)
AMP2091 warning the type of a @param or @return is not the declared one: unions are compared as sets of members, a type alias (type Shift = Interval | Int) is written out first, Int? is Int, case is ignored; a wider or a narrower comment is a difference
AMP2092 warning a type in the comment does not exist (a typing mistake)
AMP2093 warning a call of a helper whose comment says @deprecated (with the reason)
AMP2094 info the comment describes some parameters but not all

The hover also says it: (documented as Interval|Int) next to a parameter and (declared Notes) after the returned value when the comment gives another type. A union inside the brackets of a generic (List<Int|Float>) is one type: it is split only at a | or , outside the brackets, the arguments are compared as types of their own (aliases and the order of a union included) and every name inside is checked for AMP2092. Quick fixes (on the warning, in the tip of the line and in the code actions): AMP2090 renames the @param to the parameter that is nearest (or removes the line when none is, which "Fix all" leaves alone because it removes text), AMP2091 writes the declared type in the comment, AMP2092 changes the typo to the nearest type, and AMP2094 adds the missing @param lines after the last one in the same style (* or ##). A fix only changes the comment, never the code. In the browser without the language server the warnings are shown but have no fix buttons.

4. The hover

Pointing at a name (a short rest of the pointer in the source editor, a tap on a touch screen) shows:

Name Shown
a helper of the song name(Type param = default, ...) -> Type, the doc comment (summary, deprecation, returns, examples), every parameter with its type, its default and its note, "Returns Type" when no comment says it, pure or dynamic, what it depends on, baked
a let, a var, a constant, a parameter or a loop variable (at its declaration and at every use) let name: Type, its value, Type with how it was found (a list of notes, a number with a unit, the call of transpose(), arithmetic on both sides, the declared type), and for a var that is assigned values of other types the Potential types (Int, Float); a parameter also shows its @param note
the let or var keyword what the keyword does and what it declares (Declares motif: Notes)
a constant, a type alias its type and its doc comment
a block name the doc comment above the block
a note operator (shift, humanize ...) the signature (with the receiver), what it does, every parameter with type, default and note, "Built in."
a function (Round, min, Note ...), a method (seed.fork) the same, from the builtins of the catalogue
currentTime, osRandom, environment the signature, that it is volatile and the state of the capability
a unit (2bars, 250ms, +7st) the unit and its meaning
a word of a helper body (for, emit, let, return ...) what it does

The text comes from the language server (textDocument/hover, markdown); when the server cannot be reached the browser builds the same text from the catalogue and the song (web/lib/doc-comments.mjs, the twin of Comments.cs and Queries.cs). The notes of the parameters of the built-in operators are the doc of the parameters in spec/note-ops.json (the catalogue is the one source; run node tools/gen-note-catalog.mjs after a change). A built-in function, method, unit or keyword is an entry of its builtins section; the evaluator does not read that list, it only feeds the hover.

The types of variables are worked out without running anything, from the value: notes literals, pipelines and operators (the return type of the catalogue), numbers (Int or Float, and with a unit Length, Time, Interval, Gain or Percent), strings, booleans, lists (List<Int | Float>), ranges, helper calls (the declared return type), the built-in functions, and arithmetic (/ gives a Float, a length times a number is a length, a length plus a time is a Duration). A declared type (let x: Type = ...) wins. A helper that does not write its return type gets it from its body: the types of every return (a union when they differ, Int | Float), Notes when it emits, and the type of its last expression; the hover shows -> Type and "worked out from what the body returns", and a call of that helper has that type for let x = helper(). (Three rounds are made, so a helper that calls another untyped helper gets its type too; a recursive helper must still say its type.) A call of a function that gives no type, or a word the language does not know, shows unknown. The same logic is in NoteLang.Variables.cs (server) and web/lib/variable-types.mjs (browser, without the language server).

Keeping the catalogue complete. When a built-in is added to the language (a function in NoteLang.Interp.cs, a unit, an operator), add its entry to spec/note-ops.json in the same change: an operator in operators, anything else in builtins. CommentsTests checks a sample of them.

19 - Components

Status: being built. A component is a reusable, typed block made of Notes code. It looks like a native block in the editor and the palette, and it stays transparent: its code is readable, its contract is typed, its versions are explicit, and a song always knows exactly which version of which code it used.

Two requirements shape the design:

  • R-A. A song never changes without its owner knowing because the code of a component changed. The semantic hash of every component a song uses is pinned in ample.lock; a different hash is AMP2203 until the change is accepted.
  • R-B. A build never starts over when nothing that matters changed. An instance becomes the notes it makes; the plan identity of everything downstream follows the resulting notes. A new description, a display name or a KODA fact never changes the semantic hash, so nothing is built again.

1. The declaration

/** Repeats the notes, one copy per step. */
#[Category("Notes")]
component alex.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  id "com.alex.notes.triple-notes"      # optional; the default is local:<name>; needed to seal and export
  current                                 # optional: this version is the default of its family

  input source: Notes {
    optional true
    fallback localNotes                   # the property that stands in when nothing is connected
  }

  property localNotes: Notes {
    editor jam                            # Jam edits it
  }

  #[MinValue(1), MaxValue(16), Step(1)]
  property copies: Int = 3

  property spacing: Duration = 1bar

  output notes: Notes

  process {
    let n = connected(source) ? source : localNotes
    for i in 0..copies {
      emit n |> shift(i * spacing)
    }
  }
}
  • Name. A path of one or more parts (alex.notes.tripleNotes). A name with one part may not be the name of a native block type (AMP2209); a namespace avoids it. The name is how source writes the component; the canonical id says what it is. Names can be remapped and reexported, the id never changes (the same component under two names is one component).
  • Header. component <name> [version <x.y.z>] [current] [id "..."], then {. The header may run over lines (version "1.0.0" on its own line is fine). version may also be written inside the body.
  • Ports. input <name>: <Type> and output <name>: <Type>, optionally with a body (optional [true], fallback <property>). In this version ports are Notes, and there is one output (AMP2219 otherwise); the model is Port<T>, so other types come later without a redesign.
  • Properties. property <name>: <Type> [= <default>] [{ editor jam }]. The types are the musical types of page 15 (and List, Range of them): there are no types of their own. A default is required except for Notes. A default must be a value of its type and inside its range (AMP2204).
  • Process. process { ... } is the body of a helper (page 14): the inputs and properties are its parameters in the order they are declared; emit, a return or the last expression give the output. connected(source) (or source.connected) says whether an optional input has a connection. All limits, capabilities and the pure or dynamic effect of helpers apply; a process that uses the clock, OS randomness or the environment needs requires clock (and the policy must allow it).
  • Inside a song or a file. A component is declared at the start of a line, in a song (.amplet) or in a .amplec file (a file of declarations: components, helpers, constants, types, import, reexport). Its lines are not song lines.
  • Doc comments (page 18) work above the component, the ports and the properties; @param per property, the hover shows the contract.

2. Attributes

#[Name(args), Name2] on its own line directly above a component, a port or a property. Only the built-in attributes exist (AMP2205 for anything else); each says where it may stand and on which types (AMP2206) and how many arguments of which kind it takes (AMP2207). To every tool that does not know attributes the line is a comment.

Attribute On Meaning
MinValue(n), MaxValue(n), Step(n) a property of an ordered type (Int, Float, Percent, Duration, Interval, Gain, ...) the range and the step of the editor; instances outside the range are AMP2218
Options("a", "b") a String property the allowed values, shown as a choice
Editor(jam) a Notes property Jam edits it (also editor jam in the body)
DisplayName(".."), Description("..") anything presentation
Category("..") the component the group of the palette
Tags("a", "b") the component words the Library search also finds (#a, #b); lower case, never part of the identity or the semantic hash
Experimental the component may still change in ways its version does not say
KodaFact("..") or KodaFact(text="..", appliesTo="copies") anything a fact for the assistant: advisory, it never changes the build

Prefer a type to an attribute when the type already says it (Percent instead of #[Unit("%")]).

3. Instances

An instance is a block whose type is the component:

alex.notes.tripleNotes introTriple stable at 2 for 3 {
  copies 3
  spacing 1bar
  from intro.notes -> source
}
  • The header is the usual type name [pinned@version] [at ...] {; pinned@<version> is a request for a version of the component (pinned@1.8 the 1.8 line, pinned@1.8.0 exactly, pinned@^1.2 compatible, pinned@~1.2 patch-level, pinned@4.0.0-beta.1 a pre-release by name); without it the instance follows the current version.
  • Default version: an explicit request, else the version marked current, else the highest release; a pre-release is never chosen unless it is the only one or is asked for by name. At most one current per component (AMP2214). Several versions of one component can coexist.
  • The property lines are checked against the contract (type, range: AMP2218); from lines connect the inputs; consumers read the output as from introTriple.notes -> x (the output name is whatever the component calls it).
  • What an instance makes. Before a song is built each instance becomes a midi-clip with the same name whose notes are the call of the process of its component. So the note flow, bakes, Jam, previews, the build and the plan identity work on an instance without any change, and three instances share one definition (one helper, three calls).
  • A component that comes from an imported file is added to the expanded text with its whole file (its helpers and constants come with it), once.

4. Hashes, pins and seals

Covers Used for
semantic hash canonical id, version, ports, property types and defaults, the constraint attributes, the process (comments out, whitespace collapsed), the hashes of every helper and constant it uses, requires, the migrations pinning in ample.lock (R-A), deciding that a rebuild is needed (R-B)
payload hash everything above and the documentation, the presentation attributes, ui, deprecated, KODA facts what a seal and a signature protect
  • Pins (R-A). The lock file has a component section: <canonical id>@<version> with the semantic hash. The first use pins; a different hash later is AMP2203 with the fix "accept the change" (it re-pins). An unsealed component that changed shows an info in the build log, once per build.
  • Seal. seal { payload sha256:.. semantic sha256:.. [signed-by ".." key .. signature ..] } is written by the engine, never by hand. A sealed version is immutable: if the component changes afterwards the seal no longer matches (AMP2210) and the component counts as unsealed. The way forward is a new version.
  • Unsealed is not an error (AMP2211 is an info): it builds, it just never counts as trusted.
  • Same id + same version + same payload in two places is one component (deduplicated); same id + same version + another payload is AMP2212.
  • A signature is the publisher's attestation over the payload hash (ECDSA P-256, the keys of the user).

5. Namespaces, imports, reexports

Namespaces are logical paths, independent of files. One file can hold components in several namespaces; several files can add to one namespace. import "file.amplec" [as alias] makes the components of a file available (the alias replaces the first segment of their names: fx1.notes.tripleNotes; the Library tab and ample_component_library propose one when a name is taken) (found like modules: project, linked folders, packs, the user library); reexport <path> as <path> offers a symbol (or a namespace with .*) of an import again, keeping its canonical id, version and provenance. Cycles are errors (AMP2217). The same exported path for two different canonical ids is AMP2213 and needs an explicit alias; the last import never wins.

6. Deprecation and migration

component alex.fx.canonMaker version 3.2.0 {
  deprecated {
    message "Use 4.x; the routing changed."
    replacement alex.fx.canonMaker@^4
  }

  migrate 3.2.0 -> 4.0.0 {
    impact musicalChange                 # none | equivalent | musicalChange | destructive
    message "The result may sound wider."
    rename interval -> transposeBy       # rename a property (copy a -> b keeps both)
    set spread = old.spread * 2          # a typed expression over the old values
    drop legacyStereo                    # remove a property
    port source -> input                 # rename an input (its from lines follow)
  }
  ...
}

A deprecated version warns (AMP2220) and never stops a build; a migration is a small, pure, bounded, typed program over the state of an instance (its properties, connections and local notes). An impactful migration (musicalChange, destructive) is never applied without an explicit acknowledgement; the preview shows the changed properties, ports, the resulting notes, span, event count and semantic hash. Chains (1 -> 2 -> 3) are followed and their impacts combined; a replacement can be another component.

Expressions in set are bounded (400 characters, 32 levels) and typed: numbers with an optional unit (2bars), old.<property> for the value before the step, + - * /, brackets and min, max, clamp, round, abs. Units must agree for + and -. A property of the old version that the new one does not have, and that no drop removed, is removed anyway and makes the migration destructive. A migration without an impact line counts as musicalChange. A chain (1 -> 2 -> 3) is found by a search over the migrations; migrate com.other@1.0.0 -> 1.0.0 replaces another component. ample components migrate <song> <block> <target> [--apply --acknowledge] and /api/components/migrate-preview / /migrate show and make it.

7. Embedding and extraction

A song can carry its components: embedded module <name> { ... } holds complete component declarations with their seals and keeps the module boundary, so an embedded component is the same object as an imported one with the same id, version and payload hash. Actions: embed the dependencies of the selected instances, embed a whole module, use the template source (only when id, version and payload match exactly: a semantic no-op), extract a component or module to a .amplec, detach a sealed embedded component for editing (it becomes unsealed).

8. Diagnostics

AMP2200 to AMP2228 (see the catalogue): 2200 syntax, 2201 names, 2202 types, 2203 changed since pinned, 2204 defaults, 2205 to 2207 attributes, 2208 output and process, 2209 native name, 2210 seal void, 2211 unsealed, 2212 to 2214 conflicts, 2215 version, 2216 to 2217 import and reexport, 2218 instance, 2219 not supported yet, 2220 deprecated, 2221 migration syntax, 2222 migration available, 2223 version syntax, 2224 id, 2225 attributes without a target, 2226 fallback, 2227 capabilities, 2228 ui.

Friendly name. #[DisplayName("Triple notes")] above the declaration is the friendly name: the card, the palette and the panel show it; the full name (alex.notes.tripleNotes), the canonical id and the version are on hover and in the properties of the block, both visible.

9. Audio components

A component with an Audio port is an audio component: the same declaration, imports, versions, seal, embedding, migration and palette, and a process that is a graph of audio processors instead of Notes code.

component alex.fx.wetDry version 1.0.0 {
  input audio: Audio
  property echo: Duration = 0.5beat
  property feedback: Percent = 35%
  property dryLevel: Gain = -3dB
  output audio: Audio
  process {
    let dry = audio
    let wet = audio |> delay(time=echo, feedback=feedback) |> reverb(size=50%)
    emit mix(dry |> gain(dryLevel), wet |> gain(-8dB))
  }
}
  • Audio is a lazy graph, never a buffer: audio |> delay(...) describes a node, the build renders the blocks it becomes. A component boundary is an abstraction boundary, not a file boundary. Rendering granularity stays the block (each processor has its own take in the cache).
  • The processors are the effect blocks (one definition, two surfaces): every template with an audio in and out (delay, reverb, chorus, compressor, eq, filter, limiter, phaser, tremolo, pan, ...). gain(x) is the volume block, mix(a, b, ...) is a bus. A second audio input is given by name: compressor(threshold=-12dB, key=sidechain).
  • Arguments are named and typed by the unit of the block parameter: a time for ms (250ms, 0.25beat, 1bar; beats become ms with the song tempo), a Percent for %, a gain for dB, a frequency for Hz. Arithmetic over the properties is allowed (space * 0.5). A Bool property can be given to enabled (bypass). A Notes operation on Audio (AMP2234), a wrong unit (AMP2232), an unknown parameter (AMP2235) and an unknown name (AMP2231) are errors at the line.
  • A name is defined before it is used, so a graph cannot loop; feedback exists only through the feedback parameter of a processor. At most 64 processors and 8 outputs (AMP2233). Several outputs: emit audio |> ... -> name.
  • Notes in, sound out (a component with an instrument inside): a Notes input is a value of its own kind and an instrument turns it into audio: emit notes |> piano() |> delay(time=250ms) |> reverb(size=room). The instruments are the blocks that read notes and give audio: piano, bass, guitar, synth, gm, sampler and delay-llama (drums read a trigger and are not offered). Their parameters are named arguments like those of an effect (piano(...), delay-llama(...)). The instance is wired like any block (from melody.notes -> notes), takes the placement of the instance (at 1 for 2) onto the instrument block it becomes, or, when it has none, the placement of the clip it reads, and the next block reads its sound (from voice.audio -> in). Notes are not audio: notes straight to an output, an effect on notes, an instrument on audio and notes in a mix are AMP2232. A Notes output next to Audio ports is refused (AMP2230): the process makes audio. An unconnected Notes input says so (AMP2218) unless it is optional.
  • An instance is wired like any block (from vocals.audio -> audio; the next block reads from vocalFx.audio -> in) and becomes ordinary blocks named <instance>__<processor><n> (delay1, reverb1): provenance for diagnostics, logs and the takes. Node ids are the processor name and its number in the source.
  • Hashes: the semantic hash contains the process, the contract and processor=<block>@<version> for every processor used, so a new version of an effect block is a changed hash; one function (ComponentHashing.DependenciesOf) serves seal, check, catalog and build. Documentation and presentation are not in it.
  • Latency and preview are derived, never claimed: the longest path of processor latencies (a template that really delays its signal declares latencyMs; no built-in does, the limiter looks ahead over a whole file without delaying it) and the browser preview (every processor must have one). ample components graph <song> <block> and GET /api/components/graph show the graph; the board menu has "Show internal graph".
  • Migration: port input.audio -> input.signal renames an input (the from lines of the instance follow) and port output.a -> output.b an output (the consumers follow); an audible change is declared musicalChange and must be acknowledged.
  • Nested components: an audio process can call another audio component as a processor, with its properties as named arguments: audio |> alex.fx.dreamEcho(feedback=20%). A second audio input is given by name (key=other). The called component is built with those values and spliced into the graph (nodes dreamEcho1_delay1, ...), so the engine still sees ordinary blocks. Its semantic hash is part of the hash of the caller (component=name@version:hash): a change in the nested code is a change in the caller and breaks its seal. At most four deep; a component never calls itself.
  • Notes components call Notes components too (2026-10-29): in the process of a Notes component, another Notes component is called like a function: emit alex.notes.echoNotes(alex.notes.octaveLayers(source, layers=2), plays=3, interval=2). The first unnamed value is the first input; every other input and every property is given by name (plays=3), and what is left out takes the default of the called component (an input without a default and not optional must be given, AMP2248; a name the called component does not have is AMP2248 too). The call is rewritten to the call of the helper that the called process is, so it is evaluated by the same helper system, and the hash of the caller contains the hash of what it calls (change the called component and the seal of the caller breaks). A component file can import the files of the components it calls (import "components/echo-notes.amplec" at the top of the file); the song does not see those, they travel along. Demo: demo-projects/components/12-nested-notes.amplet. The call can also be a pipe step: source |> alex.notes.octaveLayers(layers=2) |> alex.notes.echoNotes(plays=3) (what is before the pipe is the first input). In a mixed component a Notes call can stand before the instrument: emit notes |> alex.notes.octaveLayers(layers=2) |> piano() makes a midi-clip block (named after the instance and the call) whose notes are the call, and the instrument reads that clip; such a component has no live preview (the call is not evaluated in the browser). A file that imports with an alias (import "components/up.amplec" as p) calls the component by the alias; the registry writes the declared name into what the expansion adds, so two files that use the same alias for different components do not clash.
  • Pin the version of what you call (2026-10-29): a call takes the default version of the called component (the one marked current). Write the version after the name to keep the one you tested: alex.notes.up@1.2.0(source), @1.2 or @^1.2 (the same requests as an instance alex.notes.up@1.2 name { ... }), in Notes calls and in audio calls (audio |> alex.fx.dreamEcho@1.0.0(feedback=20%)). A request that no version matches is AMP2248. A component that is not sealed and calls a family with more than one version without a pin gets an info, AMP2249 (a sealed one breaks its seal when the default changes, because the hash contains what it calls).
  • Where a call is read (2026-10-29): only in code, not in the strings and comments of a process (a bracket that never closes in a comment hides nothing); a dotted name that looks like a component and is none in sight is AMP2248 ("is its file imported?"), not a syntax error. A file of components opened on its own (the editor, ample check file.amplec) reads its own imports, so a call of an imported component checks without a false error. A Notes component can have String and Bool properties; chords("Am F", 1bar, 3, 70) takes length, octave and velocity in that order without names.
  • Circles (2026-10-29): a component never calls itself, directly or through other components, in both kinds. When A calls B and B calls A the check says so and names the circle (alex.notes.ping -> alex.notes.pong -> alex.notes.ping): AMP2247, on every component of the circle (for audio components at the call that closes it). The calls inside a circle are left out of the helper, so a circle is reported, never run. Chains are at most four deep (AMP2233).
  • Latency of branches that meet is aligned: the shorter branch gets a shift block (align1, ...). Between the tracks of a song the same alignment is optional: settings { audio.latencyCompensation on } puts a shift in front of the earlier inputs of a mixer, bus, send or vocoder and a cut in front of the master (AMP2250); it is off by default, so a song without it keeps its plan ids. A pass-through (emit audio) is allowed.
  • Limits of this version: no external plugins, seeds only through processors that have a seed parameter.

10. Layout and live preview

A component can design its own controls: knobs, sliders, switches, choices and an xy pad, in rows and groups. The layout is presentation only: it is part of the payload hash (a seal protects it) and never of the semantic hash, so changing it never changes what the component makes (R-A) and rebuilds nothing (R-B). The ranges are different: MinValue, MaxValue and Step constrain the value, so they are semantic.

#[MinValue(0%), MaxValue(90%)]
property feedback: Percent = 30%
#[MinValue(0%), MaxValue(100%)]
property room: Percent = 40%
property delayTime: Duration = 0.25beat

ui {
  row {
    knob feedback label "Echo" size l
    knob room size l
  }
  field delayTime
  meter audio
  card {                       // the compact face on the board card
    knob feedback size s
  }
  preview live                 // opt in to the live preview
}
  • Widgets (a closed set, no scripts): knob, slider (a number property, with its range from MinValue/MaxValue/Step, else what the type usually means), toggle (Bool), choice (Options or Bool), xy x=a y=b (two number properties, one write for both), readout (a value), meter (an audio output: its level while the live preview plays), jam (a Notes property), curve and field (the standard field of the panel; a curve has no editor yet). Options: size s|m|l, label "text", tint <colour>. A tint colours a widget or a group (group "Echo" tint blue { ... }): a name (accent, green, yellow, orange, red, pink, purple, blue, teal, gray) or a text such as "#ff8800"; #[Tint(red)] on a property is the shortcut without a block; anything else is AMP2246. A property can have a friendly name: #[DisplayName("How many")] is the label in the panel, on the knob and in the rows, and the tooltip shows both (How many (copies)); label in the layout overrides it. The curve widget draws a text property that holds points, x:y pairs from 0 to 1 ("0:0 0.5:1 1:0"): double click adds a point, right click removes one, a drag moves it, and the value is written in that format (it is a value of the component; the process language does not read curves yet).
  • Containers: row, column, group "Title" { ... }, and card { ... } at the top level. At most 4 deep and 64 items (AMP2243).
  • Without a block the layout is made from the properties: a plain field each. #[Widget(knob)] and #[Group("Envelope")] on a property are the shortcut for simple cases; #[LivePreview] on the component is the shortcut for preview live. Properties that the layout does not show keep their standard rows.
  • Where it shows: the properties panel (the whole layout), the board card (the card block; the card gets taller and a knob on it never moves the block) and a window (the ⤢ button).
  • Dragging is a preview: while a widget moves nothing is written; on release one setParameter is (one undo step). An xy pad writes both properties in one step.
  • Checks: AMP2240 (not a word of the layout), AMP2241 (no such property or output), AMP2242 (a widget that does not fit the type), AMP2243 (too big or too deep), AMP2244 (the same property twice), AMP2245 (a live preview that cannot be).
  • A Bool or String property written on an instance is checked as such (true or false, any text); only numbers go through the number evaluator.

Live preview (opt-in, advisory): an audio component that says preview live gets a Live switch. The sound that feeds the block loops in the browser through a real-time chain made of the same live effects the built-in blocks use (eq, filter, compressor, distortion, delay, reverb, chorus, gain; a mix is a sum), and the sound changes while a knob moves. The server stays the only evaluator of the process (units, beats to milliseconds, arithmetic over properties): the browser sends the values of the knobs to POST /api/components/graph-values and sets its chain from the answer. Capability is derived, never claimed: a component can run live when every processor has "livePreview": true in its template and none has a second audio input (a sidechain key); otherwise the switch is off and says which processor stops it (AMP2245). The preview is approximate (Web Audio is not the engine); it never writes a take, never touches a plan id and never builds: the committed build is the truth. It needs the source built first (it says so instead of building by itself). A component with one instrument inside (Notes in, sound out) loops the sound the server rendered for that instrument (its take, so the instrument stays deterministic) and runs the effects after it live; with more than one instrument the switch stays off ("more than one instrument"). The Delay Llama is the exception that sings in the browser itself (the live llama worklet of Jam): a component with a Delay Llama inside needs no build, the notes are those of the midi-clip that feeds it (looped), and its own settings (vowel, size, unison, vibrato, ...) change the voice while a knob moves.

11. Not in this version

A Notes output next to Audio ports, a live preview of Notes components, of the instrument itself while its own parameters move, and of processors without a real-time chain (a limiter, a sidechain key), a meter on an input, native code, a package registry, a trust store, several implementations of one version, user-defined attributes and types.

99 Maintaining this specification

The language specification must be kept true for as long as AMPLE exists. It is the one place where parser, linter, language server, formatter, help generator and UI agree on what the language is.

The rules

  1. The spec is normative. ample/docs/ pages explain; this folder and ample/spec/ define. On conflict, the spec wins and the other page is fixed.
  2. A language change is five edits in one change:
    • the data in ample/spec/ (template, diagnostic, lint rule, grammar, tokens);
    • the prose page in this folder;
    • a conformance case in ample/spec-tests/ (a valid case for new syntax, an invalid case with expected diagnostics for a new code);
    • an updated example (in the page, tagged ```amplet run once the help generator executes them, chunk 12);
    • a line in CHANGELOG.md, with a migration note if it breaks anything.
  3. CI enforces it: node ample/tools/validate-spec.mjs (schemas, unique ids, grammar equals prose, links, every static diagnostic and lint rule has a failing example) and, from chunk 12, ample docs check (the generated help.html is up to date and all examples compile or fail as stated). A change that breaks either is not done.
  4. The help is generated, never edited by hand. It is built from this folder and ample/spec/ (chunk 12).
  5. Codes and ids are never reused. Retire, do not delete.
  6. Provisional is allowed, silent is not. A not-yet-decided detail is marked provisional in the data and listed in ../open-questions.md; it is never guessed in code.
  7. Corpus before code. When the implementation and the corpus disagree, decide which is right, fix the spec and the corpus first, then the code. Never edit the corpus just to make a test pass.

Review points

  • Whenever a chunk that touches the language is marked done, the agent re-runs validate-spec and reads README.md for staleness.
  • At each milestone (M1 to M5 in the plan) the owner reviews the spec index and the changelog.
  • Before 1.0: a full read-through against the working product, with every difference fixed on the side that is wrong.

Where the corpus came from

The first corpus (spec version 0.1) was generated by ample/tools/gen-corpus.mjs from the clickable sketch's mock parser, because that was the only executable reference of the mock syntax. Expected diagnostics therefore describe the mock; chunk 20's real parser must match them, and from then on the corpus is edited by hand. The templates, codes and lint rules were seeded by ample/tools/extract-spec-from-sketch.mjs and are hand-maintained now.

Language changelog

Note pipelines and note bake (2026-10-26, draft)

  • Musical types (docs/language/15-musical-types.md): every note operator parameter has a type (PitchClass, ScaleMode, Count, Octave, Velocity, Pitch, Probability, Interval, Duration, Window, Range, RandomSource); the typed catalogue is spec/note-ops.json v2. New spellings +7st, -1oct, 50cents, 25% and note names (C2) mean the same as the plain numbers (same recipe). New codes AMP2044 (wrong type), AMP2045 (quoted word), AMP2046 (missing unit), AMP2048 (fractional interval), AMP2049 (fixed span differs from the notes), AMP2050 (not whole), AMP2051 (unit of the wrong kind); AMP2047 is reserved. An instrument may say for auto and follows the notes that feed it.
  • Seeds and randomness (docs/language/13-randomness.md): stable("name") namespaces derived by hashing from the master-seed, .fork(...), explicit seeds, random-seed() that must be picked, addressed draws, random, choose, chance, declared random-stream clip lines with name.next(), the seeded operators humanize, randomize, thin, scramble and the generator walk, the generators chords and scale, the helpers clamp, fold, snap, keep and avoid; new codes AMP2038-AMP2043. Humanize now draws per note (addressed) instead of in order, so it gives other numbers than the first draft.
  • More operators (reverse, stretch, legato, quantize, seeded humanize, repeat, arp, where, euclid as a source), named arguments, MIDI file blocks as a source, the limit of the song (settings notes.maxEvents) under the limit of the server, and AMP2037 (the pipeline may be too large).
  • A midi-clip notes value may be a pipeline expression (notes take.notes |> bars(1..=4) |> transpose(+12)), with editable { } literals and bake name { } stages that store signed notes (inline or in a file). A part may be written for auto (the length of the notes). Plain literals are unchanged; new codes AMP1111, AMP2023-AMP2036, AMP5701. See docs/language/12-note-pipelines.md.

Piano-roll ties (2026-10-18)

  • Compact notes accept ;tie=0..2000000 to join bar-split sustains while keeping instrument routing inherited. Legacy nine-field ties remain valid; duplicate or conflicting tie identities are rejected. Expanded tie-id also works without explicit channel/bank/program.
  • The built-in midi-clip renderer is version 4 so cached note output includes the new tie semantics.

Render stream extension (implementation in progress; verification paused)

  • Added the render port type, render outputs on audio sources, and render_in inputs on built-in audio effects. Effects may use their existing audio input or the render recipe input; both may be connected when one or both connections are disabled.
  • Added AMP2020 for connecting both effect input modes while both are active. Source variants now retain ordered render recipes, materialize at audio boundaries, and record effect parameters and seeds in the plan. Full build, cache, UI and conformance acceptance remains in progress; testing is paused at the owner's request.
  • Added docs/examples/16-audio-vs-render/, a self-contained song with matching EQ/reverb chains on ordinary audio and render paths, mixed for direct comparison.

Added in MIDI M03 (2026-10-04)

  • midi-clip is version 1.1 and accepts optional structured polyphonic notes as bar:beat:length:pitch:velocity entries. Beat values use integer microbeats internally with up to six decimal places in source; ties crossing bars are split. Existing chord and melody songs are unchanged.
  • Added static diagnostic AMP2012 for malformed structured MIDI note entries. Migration: none; the new parameter defaults to empty.

Added in MIDI M13 (2026-10-04)

  • midi-clip retains imported note onset and duration in source PPQ ticks, including output metadata, while preserving readable beat fields.

Added in MIDI M15 (2026-10-04)

  • The MIDI file template exposes note, typed sequence and audio outputs. The midi-render template accepts sequence or note input and provides a SoundFont-backed audio conversion path.

Added in MIDI M02 (2026-10-04)

  • Added the midi source template for bounded .mid/.midi project files, deterministic track selection and notes:midi rendering, with a text warnings output.
  • Added build diagnostics AMP5501–AMP5503 for invalid assets, unsupported exact note timing and missing track indices.

0.1 draft (2026-10-03)

  • Added mood-scene (a stable style:data source) and ace-music (a live ACE-Step block with optional lyrics:text, optional melody:midi, optional style:data and audio:audio). ai-voice remains a live ACE-Step block with required lyrics and a vocal-only contract.
  • Template parameters can now describe modalEditor and multiline property editing behavior. The display label and short documentation are also template data.
  • Migration: existing ai-voice voice values retain their parameter name, but the UI calls it Vocal direction. Existing inline lyrics text values still render only when the linked file has no content; move new work into the Lyrics editor file.

0.1 draft (2026-10-02)

  • First written specification: lexical rules, grammar, error recovery, types and ports, template rules, seeds and determinism, references, diagnostics and lint, formatting, versioning, maintenance.
  • Data seeded from the clickable sketch: 14 templates, 31 static diagnostic codes (AMP1xxx, AMP2xxx, AMP5001, AMP5002), 9 lint rules, plus the runtime notices AMP5101 and AMP5102 (regeneration safety).
  • Conformance corpus: 15 valid, 42 invalid (one per code and lint rule), 8 recovery, 10 format pairs, 7 round trip.
  • Known gaps: the statement-style syntax of ../examples/, include and imports, .amplelrc, inner graphs of groups, defining new block types (all in ../open-questions.md).

Added in chunk 94 (2026-10-03)

  • New statement use <module>[@version] as <name> { ... } and the module file format (module, param, input, output); new static code AMP1110 and runtime codes AMP5320 to AMP5328; keyword use. Nothing that parsed before changes meaning (a block type called use did not exist). Migration: none.

Added after chunk 98 (2026-10-03)

  • drums is now 1.3 (S07): optional choke parameter (open:hat,pedal; rules separated by ;) cuts a voice when a closing voice is hit, with a 7 ms fade. Sample folders may hold a set.json with gain (dB) and tune (semitones) for the whole set. Songs that say drums ... stable@1.2 stay valid (the class is stable, not pinned). Migration: none.
  • Sampler velocity layers (S05): sample files name_v<L>_r<R>.wav are layer L, round robin R; accents, strokes and note velocity choose the layer. melody notes take an optional third field, the MIDI velocity (c4:1:110, default 96, unchanged output). Round robins (S06) are chosen per hit from a separate seeded stream (no change to humanize bytes). Built-in drums, bass, piano and guitar renderers are version 2. Migration: none, folders without layer files sound the same.
  • Template parameters can say how the property panel edits them: kind (text, number, choice, combo, seed, sampleset, file, pattern, channels) with options, min, max, step, unit, placeholder, accept and count. Parameters no longer start with made-up text; an empty value shows a placeholder. Migration: none, old values keep their meaning.
  • Six audio effect templates (category Effects, stable@1.0): eq, distortion, delay, reverb, compressor and filter. Each has one required in:audio, one out:audio and an enabled on|off bypass. Integer arithmetic only, so they are bit-reproducible. Migration: none.
  • midi-clip has an optional melody parameter (note name, octave, length in beats; r is a rest). When it is set, the clip plays the melody instead of the chords. Notes now carry beat and beats; the built-in piano plays them at that place and length (notes without them still last the whole bar). Migration: none.
  • lyrics is now 1.1: the legacy inline text parameter is gone. The words live in the lyrics file, which the lyrics editor creates and names (lyrics/<block name>.lyr) the first time you open it. Migration: move old inline text into a lyrics file ([bar N] words per line) and set file; songs that still say text get AMP2003.
  • piano is now 2.1 and bass 1.2: set can name a sample folder of the project (note-named WAV files, like the guitar), and both have a gain in dB. The built-in sounds are unchanged. Migration: none.
  • ai-voice is now 0.10: the optional parameter sing (bars) says how long the voice sings. ACE fills all the time it is given, so a voice longer than its words repeats the last sounds; with sing the voice is made that long and the rest of the block stays silent (short fade at the end). Empty means the whole block, as before. Migration: none.
  • ai-voice sing also takes the word auto: the voice is as long as the linked lyrics file needs (from the start of the block to the end of the last timed line; the last line gets as many bars as the one before it). The build replaces the word by the number, so the plan holds the real length.
  • The lyrics file can hold section tags as lines of their own ([Verse], [Chorus], [Outro]). They have no bar, are not timed, are passed to ACE with the words and show as heading rows in the lyrics editor. Migration: none (such lines used to be reported as unreadable).
  • ai-voice is now 0.11: the optional parameter fit (off or stretch). ACE tends to sing a little faster than the music and then runs out; stretch slows the voice down without changing its pitch so it ends where the lyrics end (at most 1.6 times as long). The factor is written into the take (voiceStretch). Default off. Migration: none.
  • ai-voice 0.12 and ace-music 0.2: steps is empty by default, which takes the number of steps the chosen ACE model wants (turbo 8, sft and base 50). A block that says steps itself keeps that number. The model is a plugin setting (synthModel). Migration: none.
  • New statement settings { plugin.name value ... } for the plugin settings of one song (new static code AMP1112 for a malformed line). The settings of a song are part of the plan of the blocks of that plugin, so choosing another ACE model or isolation gives a new take instead of the cached one. The plugin settings that were stored once per project (.ample/plugin-settings.json) are now only the defaults for new songs: a build reads the settings of the song, not those of the project. Migration: a song that relied on project-level settings needs a settings line (the plugin settings screen has "Use the project defaults" and "Apply and back" writes it).
  • Plugins can report progress with sub-steps (ctx.progress(fraction, step, stepFraction)), shown as bars in the node editor; the server sends the event build.block. No change to songs.
  • A song that lacks a setting its plugin marks as required fails its blocks with AMP5370, which names the setting and the project default; the node menu offers "Use the project default" (writes it into the song's settings line and builds again). New songs are made with + New song (POST /api/songs) and start with the project defaults in their settings line. No change to existing songs.
  • New effect block duck (stable@1.0, category Effects): the sound dips at every hit of a 16-step pattern (default every beat) by depth dB and comes back over release ms, like a sidechain pumping effect. Integer gain, deterministic. Migration: none.
  • ai-voice sing auto also looks at the words: the length is the smaller of the lyrics timeline and an estimate from the text (about four syllables a second plus a breath per line), so a short text is no longer stretched over a long block. Voices with sing auto get a new take once.
  • ACE plugin 0.5.1: a voice or music block that sits later in the song (at 5 for 4) is now made as long as its own bars and placed where the block starts; before, the sound began at the start of the song. Voice takes are made again once.
  • ACE plugin 0.6.0: the setting backend (server, cli, server-then-cli) with aceBinFolder and cliLmModel. A plugin can mark settings every song must state itself (x-songRequired); a song that does not gets the editor warning AMP2013 with a quick fix (the project default) and AMP5370 when it is built. The example songs now state acestep.backend server. Migration: songs that use ai-voice or ace-music need settings { acestep.backend server } (the quick fix writes it).

2026-10-04

  • Added the midi file block with project-contained inputs, deterministic track selection, canonical notes output and unsupported-event warnings.

Creates intended backing music or a full song. Lyrics are optional: without them it makes instrumental music.
