AMP5458 Unknown or expired assistant task token

error runtime since 1.0

An assistant tool received a task token that is not active or no longer belongs to a running task. Start or resume the intended task and use the token it provides.

AMP5459 Server setting cannot be widened through the API

error runtime since 1.0

A project may turn off capabilities, but it cannot widen server policy or select the Codex program. Ask the administrator to change those settings.

AMP5460 Assistant edit request is invalid or ambiguous

error runtime since 1.0

The requested file edit could not be applied safely because its operation is incomplete, its target is missing, or its match is ambiguous. Read the file again and provide a more precise edit, including an occurrence when needed.

AMP5461 FFmpeg is required for FLAC output

error runtime since 1.0

Install FFmpeg or set AMPLE_FFMPEG to its executable path before exporting FLAC audio.

AMP5462 Proposal could not be measured

error runtime since 1.0

AMPLE could not prepare the proposal for measurement. Review the reported error and retry after resolving the setup problem.

AMP5463 Proposal needs offered audio files

error runtime since 1.0

The proposal refers to audio files offered to the assistant. Include those files in the proposal or revise it so the song does not depend on unavailable audio.

AMP5464 Koda is busy

error runtime since 1.0

Koda does one thing at a time. A second question while the first one is still being worked on is refused; stop the first one or wait for it.

AMP5470 File exceeds the 60 MB limit

error runtime since 1.0

This operation accepts files up to 60 MB. Choose a smaller file.

AMP5506 A controller of a midi-clip is not a value it can play

error runtime since 1.0

A named controller of a midi-clip takes a number in its range (modwheel and the sends 0 to 100 percent, volume and expression 0 down to -96 dB, pan -100 to 100, sustain on or off) or a curve such as auto(1:0, 2:100); cc takes controller=value entries with controllers and values 0 to 127. The build stops at the clip.

Wrong

example: AMP5506
midi-clip lead { notes 1:0:1:60:100  volume loud  cc "74:20" }

Right

midi-clip lead { notes 1:0:1:60:100  volume -6  cc "74=20" }

AMP5505 MIDI to audio converter has no input

error runtime since 1.0

Connect a MIDI sequence or MIDI notes to the converter before building it.

Wrong

example: AMP5505
midi-render audio { }

Right

midi-render audio { from notes.notes -> notes }

AMP5530 Effect preview range is invalid or too long

error runtime since 1.0

Choose a non-negative preview interval no longer than 30 seconds.

AMP5600 Not enough free disk space to store a take

error runtime since 1.0

The drive that holds the takebank is full, or has less free space than the render needs. Free space on the drive, clean up takes in the Storage panel (ample storage clean), or move the takebank to another drive (ample storage move).

AMP5601 The takebank cannot be written

error runtime since 1.0

A take could not be stored: the folder is read-only, the file is in use or the drive is not reachable. Check the data folder of the project (.ample/data or the configured data path).

AMP5602 Clean-up refused

error runtime since 1.0

The clean-up was not run: it needs the exact acceptance text, or the plan changed since the dry run. Run the dry run again and accept it.

AMP5603 The take data folder is not reachable

error runtime since 1.0

The configured data path of the takebank is not there (an unplugged drive, a renamed folder). Connect the drive or change the data path; builds render again what is missing.

AMP5604 Not enough disk space for this build

error runtime since 1.0

The estimate of this build is larger than the free space of the drive that holds the takebank. Free space, clean up takes, move the takebank, or build a smaller part.

AMP5605 Unknown final

error runtime since 1.0

The song has no final with that name. List the finals of the song and use one of them.

AMP5606 The clean-up cannot tell what is protected

error runtime since 1.0

A source, a history revision, a working file or the storage options could not be read, so the clean-up cannot be sure which takes are in use. Nothing was removed. Close the file, repair it and run the dry run again.

AMP5610 A place that can never be written

error runtime since 1.0

The assistant asked to write somewhere that is never open (the project own .ample folder or a system folder), or the path is not a full path. Remarks go to ample_findings inside the project.

AMP5611 No permission to write there

error runtime since 1.0

The assistant tried ample_write_outside without a permission for that path. It asks first with ample_request_access; the person decides.

AMP1111 Note pipeline syntax

error static since 1.0

The notes of a midi-clip are written as a pipeline, but the text is not valid: a bracket is not closed, an operator has no arguments, or a step is missing.

Wrong

example: AMP1111
notes take.notes |> bars(1..

Right

notes take.notes |> bars(1..5)

AMP2023 Unknown note operator

error static since 1.0

A pipeline step names an operator that does not exist. The message suggests the nearest one and the editors offer to replace it.

Wrong

example: AMP2023
notes take.notes |> transpos(12)

Right

notes take.notes |> transpose(12)

AMP2024 Note operator argument

error static since 1.0

An operator got an argument it cannot use: a wrong number of arguments, a wrong kind, a missing or wrong unit.

Wrong

example: AMP2024
notes take.notes |> shift(2)

Right

notes take.notes |> shift(2beats)

AMP2025 Range is reversed

error static since 1.0

The end of a range is before its start.

Wrong

example: AMP2025
notes take.notes |> bars(4..2)

Right

notes take.notes |> bars(2..4)

AMP2026 Fractional bar position

warning static since 1.0

A bar position with a fraction is allowed (1.5 is the middle of bar 1), but it is often a slip; there is no automatic fix.

Wrong

example: AMP2026
notes take.notes |> bars(1..4.5)

Right

notes take.notes |> bars(1..5)

AMP2027 Notes before the beginning

warning runtime since 1.0

A shift moved notes before the start of the value; they are dropped.

Wrong

example: AMP2027
notes take.notes |> shift(-1beat)

Right

notes take.notes |> shift(+1beat)

AMP2028 Unknown note source

error static since 1.0

A pipeline reads the notes of a block that does not exist or has no notes to read (only a midi-clip with notes can be read).

Wrong

example: AMP2028
notes nobody.notes |> transpose(1)

Right

notes melody.notes |> transpose(1)

AMP2029 Note sources read each other

error static since 1.0

Two clips read each other through their note pipelines, so neither can be worked out.

Wrong

example: AMP2029
notes b.notes   (in a)  and  notes a.notes   (in b)

Right

notes 1:0:1:60:100   (in b)

AMP2030 Stale note bake

warning static since 1.0

What a bake stage is made of has changed since it was baked (the pipeline before it, a clip it reads, or the tempo). The build keeps using the stored notes; bake again or detach the stage.

Wrong

example: AMP2030
a bake stage whose input-hash no longer matches

Right

bake the stage again

AMP2031 Baked notes were edited by hand

warning static since 1.0

The notes stored in a bake stage no longer match their notes-hash: they were edited by hand. With strict on the stage this is an error. Bake again to go back, or accept the change.

Wrong

example: AMP2031
a bake stage whose notes were edited

Right

bake the stage again, or accept the edit

AMP2033 Bake file cannot be read

error static since 1.0

A bake stage keeps its notes in a file of the project, and that file is missing or cannot be read.

Wrong

example: AMP2033
bake lead { file "bakes/missing.notes" }

Right

bake lead { file "bakes/lead.notes" }

AMP2034 Bake stage has no notes yet

info static since 1.0

A bake stage without notes does nothing yet. Bake it to store the notes of the pipeline up to that point.

Wrong

example: AMP2034
|> bake lowered

Right

|> bake lowered { notes ... }

AMP2036 Length auto needs valid notes

warning static since 1.0

A part written as "for auto" takes the length of the notes of the clip; while the notes have problems the length is taken as one bar.

Wrong

example: AMP2036
at 1 for auto  (notes with an error)

Right

at 1 for auto  (valid notes)

AMP5701 Note pipeline too large

error runtime since 1.0

A note pipeline made more notes than the limit allows. Make the pipeline smaller; a project may raise its own limit up to the limit of the server.

Wrong

example: AMP5701
a pipeline that merges a clip with itself many times

Right

a smaller pipeline

AMP2037 Note pipeline may be too large

warning static since 1.0

Worked out without running it, the pipeline can make more notes than the limit allows (a repeat multiplies, a concat adds). Make it smaller, or raise the limit of the song with settings { notes.maxEvents 500000 }; the limit of the server (2000000) cannot be passed.

Wrong

example: AMP2037
notes a.notes |> repeat(1024) |> repeat(1024)

Right

notes a.notes |> repeat(16)

AMP2038 Wrong seed

error static since 1.0

A seed is a whole number, stable("name"), or one of those followed by .fork("label") (a name in quotes or a whole number). Anything else, or a stable(...) without exactly one name, is refused.

Wrong

example: AMP2038
humanize(seed=0.5)

Right

humanize(seed=stable("verse").fork("timing"))

AMP2039 random-seed() has not been picked

error static since 1.0

random-seed() asks AMPLE to choose a seed from OS randomness once. Until a number has been written into the song the result could not be reproduced, so the pipeline refuses to build; the fix picks the number and writes it into the song.

Wrong

example: AMP2039
humanize(seed=random-seed())

Right

humanize(seed=4503599627370496)

AMP2040 Random-stream problem

error static since 1.0

A random-stream has to be declared in the clip (random-stream name seed) before name.next() is read; a stream is not a seed, a plain seed has no next(), and a name may be declared only once per clip.

Wrong

example: AMP2040
transpose(drift.next(-2..=2))   (no random-stream drift)

Right

random-stream drift stable("x").fork("drift")   transpose(drift.next(-2..=2))

AMP2041 Stable name looks like a typo

warning static since 1.0

A stable name used only once that is within two edits of a name used elsewhere starts a new random family and silently changes the music. The fix uses the name that is used more often.

Wrong

example: AMP2041
seed=stable("verce")   (and "verse" elsewhere)

Right

seed=stable("verse")

AMP2042 Same seed used twice

info static since 1.0

The same seed used twice by the same operator in one clip gives identical random offsets, so the two results are correlated. Give the second its own fork if they should differ.

Wrong

example: AMP2042
humanize(seed=stable("a")) |> humanize(seed=stable("a"))

Right

humanize(seed=stable("a")) |> humanize(seed=stable("a").fork("second"))

AMP2043 Random-stream never read

info static since 1.0

A random-stream was declared in the clip but its next() is never called.

Wrong

example: AMP2043
random-stream drift stable("x")   (no drift.next())

Right

remove the line, or read it with drift.next()

AMP2044 Argument of the wrong type

error static since 1.0

An argument is not a value of the type the operator expects: a pitch class (C, C#, Db ... B), a scale (minor, dorian ...), a count, an octave, a velocity, a pitch, a probability or a chord symbol. The catalogue (spec/note-ops.json) says what each argument is.

Wrong

example: AMP2044
walk(123, minor, seed=1)

Right

walk(C, minor, seed=1)

AMP2045 Quoted word

warning static since 1.0

A pitch class, scale or mode is a bare word, not a string. A quoted word of the right vocabulary is still understood; the fix removes the quotes.

Wrong

example: AMP2045
walk(C, "minor", seed=1)

Right

walk(C, minor, seed=1)

AMP2046 Missing unit

error static since 1.0

A duration needs a unit (bar, beat, tick, ms or s): a bare number does not say what it counts, and the choice changes the music, so no unit is chosen for you.

Wrong

example: AMP2046
a.notes |> shift(2)

Right

a.notes |> shift(2beat)

AMP2047 Reserved

info static since 1.0

Reserved: a bare number in an Interval slot (transpose(+7)) means semitones and is accepted silently; this code is not used.

AMP2048 Fractional interval

error static since 1.0

An interval that is not a whole number of semitones (50cents) is a valid Interval, but note events carry whole pitches only (microtonal pitch bend is not supported by this operator yet).

Wrong

example: AMP2048
a.notes |> transpose(+50cents)

Right

a.notes |> transpose(+1st)

AMP2049 Fixed span differs from the notes

info static since 1.0

A block says for N, but the only notes that feed it have a statically known or derived span of another length. The fix writes for auto, so the block follows the notes.

Wrong

example: AMP2049
gm play at 1 for 4 { from melody.notes -> notes }   (melody is 2 bars)

Right

gm play at 1 for auto { from melody.notes -> notes }

AMP2050 Not a whole number

error static since 1.0

A count, octave, velocity or pitch is a whole number. The fix offers the value rounded half to even; Floor, Ceil or Truncate change the music differently and are your choice.

Wrong

example: AMP2050
walk(C, minor, octave=4.5, seed=1)

Right

walk(C, minor, octave=4, seed=1)

AMP2051 Unit of the wrong kind

error static since 1.0

A unit does not belong to the type that is expected: pitch distances use st, oct or cents; lengths use bar, beat or tick; times use ms or s.

Wrong

example: AMP2051
a.notes |> shift(3st)

Right

a.notes |> shift(3beat)

AMP2052 Lossy number conversion

error static since 1.0

A decimal number that is not whole cannot become a whole number by itself: rounding is a musical choice. Say how with Round, Floor, Ceil or Truncate (the fix offers Round, which rounds half to even). A whole decimal such as 4.0 is accepted.

Wrong

example: AMP2052
twice(2.5)

Right

twice(Round(2.5))

AMP2053 Conversion failed

error static since 1.0

Int(x) and Float(x) only convert what is exactly representable; Round, Floor, Ceil and Truncate say how a decimal becomes a whole number.

Wrong

example: AMP2053
Int(2.5)

Right

Round(2.5)

AMP2054 emit and return mixed

error static since 1.0

emit builds Notes (each emit merges into the result): a helper uses emit, or return with a value, not both, and an emitting helper returns Notes.

Wrong

example: AMP2054
helper h(Notes n) -> Notes { emit n  return n }

Right

helper h(Notes n) -> Notes { emit n }

AMP2055 Stable name shared by every call

info static since 1.0

A stable name inside a helper is the same namespace on every call, so two calls draw the same random numbers. Pass the seed in as a RandomSource parameter and fork it per call.

Wrong

example: AMP2055
helper soft(Notes n) -> Notes { n |> thin(0.5, seed=stable("hat")) }

Right

helper soft(Notes n, RandomSource seed) -> Notes { n |> thin(0.5, seed=seed) }

AMP2056 While loop reached its max

error static since 1.0

A while loop always has a max. Reaching it with the condition still true is an error (a silently truncated result changes the music); write max N stop when stopping there is intended.

Wrong

example: AMP2056
while count(r) < 100 max 2 { ... }

Right

while count(r) < 100 max 2 stop { ... }

AMP2058 Code after return

info static since 1.0

The statements after a return in the same block are never run.

Wrong

example: AMP2058
return n
  n |> reverse()

Right

return n

AMP2060 Helper uses a dynamic value but is not declared dynamic

error static since 1.0

A helper that reads the clock, OS randomness or the environment, or calls a dynamic helper, must say so: dynamic helper. The word is a permission, the effect itself is always inferred, so a missing mark can never make a song look reproducible. The fix marks the helper.

Wrong

example: AMP2060
helper nudge(...) { ... currentTime() ... }

Right

dynamic helper nudge(...) { ... currentTime() ... }

AMP2061 Unknown helper or operator

error static since 1.0

There is no helper, operator or built-in with this name. The fix offers the nearest name.

Wrong

example: AMP2061
trnspose(1)

Right

transpose(1)

AMP2062 Helper name with other casing

warning static since 1.0

Names are compared ignoring case, so the call works, but it is written differently from its declaration. The fix writes the declared spelling.

Wrong

example: AMP2062
canonvoice(...)

Right

CanonVoice(...)

AMP2064 Name declared twice

error static since 1.0

Two declarations have the same name (names are compared ignoring case), or a helper has the name of a built-in.

Wrong

example: AMP2064
helper twice(...)  helper Twice(...)

Right

helper twice(...)

AMP2065 Recursive helper without a return type

error static since 1.0

A helper that calls itself must say what it returns (-> Type): the types of a recursion cannot be inferred.

Wrong

example: AMP2065
helper down(Int n) { return down(n - 1) }

Right

helper down(Int n) -> Int { ... }

AMP2066 Unknown type

error static since 1.0

A parameter or return type is not a type. The fix offers the nearest type.

Wrong

example: AMP2066
helper f(Fnt x)

Right

helper f(Int x)

AMP2067 Variable misuse

error static since 1.0

A variable that was made with let cannot be changed (use var), a name must be defined before it is assigned, a name is defined once per block, a constant cannot be defined in terms of itself, and a division by zero has no value.

Wrong

example: AMP2067
let x = 1  x = 2

Right

var x = 1  x = 2

AMP2069 Stale value bake

warning static since 1.0

A baked value (bake expression as value @hash) no longer matches what its expression is made of: a helper, a block or the tempo changed. The fix bakes it again.

Wrong

example: AMP2069
bake gain-for(a.notes) as 9 @00000000

Right

bake gain-for(a.notes) as 8 @<hash>

AMP2070 Baked value overridden on purpose

info runtime since 1.0

A baked value with override keeps its own number while the expression resolves to something else; the message says what the expression gives now.

Wrong

example: AMP2070
bake f() as -2dB @hash override

Right

bake f() as -2dB @hash override

AMP2071 Limit above the cap of the server

warning static since 1.0

A song may lower a limit or raise it up to the cap of the server, never above it; the cap is used.

Wrong

example: AMP2071
settings { limits.fuel 999999999999 }

Right

settings { limits.fuel 5000000 }

AMP2072 Baked value changed by hand

warning runtime since 1.0

The number of a baked value was changed while the hash still matches the expression: write override to keep it on purpose, or bake it again.

Wrong

example: AMP2072
bake f() as 9 @<hash>

Right

bake f() as 9 @<hash> override

AMP5702 The clip cannot be baked

error runtime since 1.0

Baking turns the notes of a clip into plain notes. It needs a clip that has notes, notes that are a pipeline (not plain text), and an editable piece with the number that was asked.

Wrong

example: AMP5702
bake on a clip without notes, or on notes that are not a pipeline, or on piece 9 of a clip that has 2 pieces.

Right

notes clip.notes |> bake name, on a clip that has a pipeline.

AMP5710 Loop limit

error runtime since 1.0

A loop would run more often than limits.loop-iterations allows (the song can raise it up to the cap of the server).

Wrong

example: AMP5710
repeat 100000000 { ... }

Right

repeat 100 { ... }

AMP5711 Fuel exhausted

error runtime since 1.0

Helper code used more evaluation steps than limits.fuel allows. Fuel is counted in abstract steps, so every evaluator stops at the same place.

Wrong

example: AMP5711
a huge loop

Right

a smaller loop, or settings { limits.fuel N }

AMP5712 Stack depth

error runtime since 1.0

Helpers call each other deeper than limits.stack-depth allows.

Wrong

example: AMP5712
a recursion without an end

Right

a recursion with a base case

AMP2082 Name is not defined

warning static since 1.0

A word in a helper that is not a parameter, a variable, a constant or a word of the language (a scale, a pitch class, true, false, a member of a type) is a symbol, and that is rarely meant: a misspelled name, or a variable used before it is declared. In arithmetic it is an error. This is found in every branch, also in the ones that never run.

Wrong

example: AMP2082
let a = b + 1
  let b = 2

Right

let b = 2
  let a = b + 1

AMP2083 A path without a value

warning static since 1.0

A helper that says what it returns can end without a value on some path (an if without an else, a loop at the end): calling it then fails. Every path ends with return VALUE or an expression.

Wrong

example: AMP2083
if p == 0 { return 1 }

Right

if p == 0 { return 1 } else { return 2 }

AMP2084 Unused variable

info static since 1.0

A variable made with let or var in a helper is never read.

Wrong

example: AMP2084
let unused = 5
  return 1

Right

return 1

AMP2085 A statement that does nothing

info static since 1.0

A statement that is only a name, a number or a calculation, and is not the last one of its block, has no effect: its value is thrown away.

Wrong

example: AMP2085
p
  return 1

Right

return 1

AMP2086 Helper never called

info static since 1.0

A helper of a song that no clip, property or other helper calls. Silence it with # ample-ignore AMP2086 on the line above when it is meant to stay.

Wrong

example: AMP2086
helper old(Int p) -> Int { return p }

Right

remove it, or call it

AMP2087 Helper not available

info static since 1.0

A call of a helper whose declaration has a syntax error. The error is on the declaration; the calls follow when it is fixed (this note replaces a second, confusing unknown-operator error).

Wrong

example: AMP2087
helper f(Int p) -> Int { retrun 1 }
notes ... f(1)

Right

helper f(Int p) -> Int { return 1 }

AMP2088 The kit has no sample for this voice

error static since 1.0

A pattern of a drums block asks for a voice (kick, snare, tom ...) that the sample folder of its kit has no WAV file for. When the block is built that is AMP5350 and the block fails, and so does everything that needs it. This check looks at the folder before anything is rendered. Use a voice the kit has, map the voice to a sample of another kit (map tom=other-kit/tom) or give the block a fallback kit that has it.

Wrong

example: AMP2088
pattern kick:x... tom:..x.

Right

pattern kick:x... snare:..x.

AMP2089 The music that feeds this block is longer than the block

warning static since 1.0

A block that has no length of its own (no at ... for ... and no bars) covers 8 bars. When the notes or the MIDI that feed it are longer, everything after bar 8 is cut off: it is not rendered and not heard. Give the block a length, or write for auto so that it follows the music that feeds it.

Wrong

example: AMP2089
midi-render gm {
  from song.sequence -> sequence
}

Right

midi-render gm at 1 for auto {
  from song.sequence -> sequence
}

AMP5713 Memory limit

error runtime since 1.0

The notes made by helper code together take more memory than limits.memory allows (an estimate of 64 bytes per note, counted at every pipeline result and helper result, so every evaluator stops at the same place).

Wrong

example: AMP5713
repeating a long clip thousands of times

Right

a shorter result, or settings { limits.memory 256 } (never above the cap of the server)

AMP2073 Property depends on a volatile value

info runtime since 1.0

A block property expression reads the clock, OS randomness, the environment or a dynamic helper: its value can differ between builds, and the song is not reproducible (status dynamic) until the value is baked: property bake expression as value.

Wrong

example: AMP2073
gain wobble()

Right

gain bake wobble() as 2dB

AMP2074 A name with hyphens that was meant as a subtraction

error static since 1.0

A hyphen belongs to a name (canon-voice), so a-b is one name. When every part of it is a variable, a constant or a number the author most likely meant a subtraction: write spaces around the minus.

Wrong

example: AMP2074
a-b

Right

a - b

AMP2075 Not available

error runtime since 1.0

environment() is not part of the language: reading the environment of the machine would put its secrets into songs and takes. A capability-based replacement may come later.

Wrong

example: AMP2075
environment("HOME")

Right

(not available)

AMP2076 Capability setting

error static since 1.0

A capabilities.<name> setting names a capability that does not exist, has a value other than on or off, switches on a capability that the server or the project forbids, or switches on a capability that was turned off earlier (an explicit off is permanent and the capability stays off).

Wrong

example: AMP2076
settings { capabilities.environment off }
settings { capabilities.environment on }

Right

settings { capabilities.environment off }

AMP2077 Capability denied

error static since 1.0

The code reads the clock, OS randomness or the environment (or, later, the network, files, processes or plugins) while that capability is off: by default, by the server, by the project or by this song. The message says which.

Wrong

example: AMP2077
environment("AMPLE_KEY")   (capability environment is off by default)

Right

settings { capabilities.environment on }

AMP2078 Helper name

warning static since 1.0

Helpers and functions are written in lowerCamelCase (canonVoice); blocks and resources keep their kebab-case. Rename the helper with F2 so every call follows.

Wrong

example: AMP2078
helper canon-voice(...)

Right

helper canonVoice(...)

AMP2079 Old spelling

warning static since 1.0

random-seed() is spelled randomSeed() (helpers, functions and built-ins are lowerCamelCase). The old spelling still works for now.

Wrong

example: AMP2079
seed=random-seed()

Right

seed=randomSeed()

AMP2200 Component declaration cannot be read

error static since 1.0

A component is declared as component <name> version <x.y.z> { ... } with input, output, property, process, ui, requires, deprecated, migrate and seal lines inside. This line or block does not follow that form.

Wrong

example: AMP2200
component koda.notes.tripleNotes {
  input source Notes
}

Right

component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

AMP2201 Name used twice in a component

error static since 1.0

Inputs and properties are the parameters of the process, so they share one list of names, and a name may not be a word of the component language.

Wrong

example: AMP2201
component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property source: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

Right

component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

AMP2202 Type a component cannot use

error static since 1.0

The ports and properties of a component use the types of the musical type model (Notes, Int, Float, Bool, Duration, Interval, Percent, ...) and List or Range of those. There are no types of its own for components.

Wrong

example: AMP2202
component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property copies: Whatever = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

Right

component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

AMP2203 Component changed since it was pinned

warning runtime since 1.0

ample.lock pins the semantic hash of every component a song uses. The component has another hash now, so the song may sound different. Review it, then accept the change (the editor offers it) or run ample lock update.

Wrong

example: AMP2203
component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

Right

component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

AMP2204 Default of a property does not fit

error static since 1.0

A property needs a default that is a value of its type and inside its range (only a Notes property may start empty).

Wrong

example: AMP2204
component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = sunny
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

Right

component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

AMP2205 Unknown attribute

error static since 1.0

Only the built-in attributes exist: MinValue, MaxValue, Step, Options, Editor, DisplayName, Description, Category, Experimental and KodaFact. Attributes of your own are not allowed.

Wrong

example: AMP2205
#[MinValu(1)]
component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

Right

component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

AMP2206 Attribute not valid here

error static since 1.0

An attribute says where it may stand and on which types: MinValue, MaxValue and Step go on ordered types (Int, Float, Percent, Duration ...), Options on a String, Editor on Notes. A type that already says it is better than an attribute.

Wrong

example: AMP2206
#[MinValue(0)]
property enabled: Bool = true

Right

property enabled: Bool = true

AMP2207 Attribute arguments wrong

error static since 1.0

An attribute takes a fixed number of arguments of one kind (a number, a text in quotes or a name), MinValue may not be above MaxValue and Step must be more than 0.

Wrong

example: AMP2207
#[MinValue(10), MaxValue(1)]
property copies: Int = 3

Right

property copies: Int = 3

AMP2208 Component without output or process

error static since 1.0

A component has one output and a process that says what it makes.

  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

Right

  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

AMP2209 Component takes a native name

error static since 1.0

The names of the native block types are reserved: a component never shadows one. Give it a namespace.

Wrong

  output notes: Notes

  property copies: Int = 3

AMP2210 Seal does not match

warning runtime since 1.0

The component was changed after it was sealed. A sealed version is immutable, so the seal is void: the component counts as unsealed. Make a new version (unseal, change the version, seal again).

Wrong

example: AMP2210
component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

Right

  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

AMP2211 Component is not sealed

info runtime since 1.0

An unsealed component is a development object: it builds, but nothing about it is trusted and its results are always worked out again. Seal a version to make it immutable.

Wrong

example: AMP2211
component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

Right

  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

AMP2212 Same component and version with another content

error runtime since 1.0

Two files declare the same canonical id and version with a different sealed content. That is a hard conflict: one of them is a different component that must have another id or version.

Wrong

example: AMP2212
component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

Right

  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source
  }
}

AMP2213 Same name for different components

error runtime since 1.0

Two different components (different canonical ids) are exported under the same path. Remap one with import ... as or give it another path.

Wrong

example: AMP2213
component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes

  output notes: Notes

error runtime since 1.0

At most one version of a component is marked current: it is the default over a higher release.

error static since 1.0

The properties of an instance must have the type of the property, stay inside its range, and the inputs that are not optional must be connected.

error static since 1.0

A migration is written migrate <from> -> <to> { ... } with an impact (none, equivalent, musicalChange or destructive) and statements that rename, copy, set, drop or relink.

}

info runtime since 1.0

The version of this instance has an automatic migration to a newer one. Nothing is changed until you preview and accept it.

Wrong

component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes

error static since 1.0

A version is major.minor.patch, with an optional pre-release (4.0.0-beta.1); a request may start with ^ or ~ and may leave out minor and patch.

  property copies: Int = 3

AMP2224 Canonical id not valid

error static since 1.0

A canonical id is lower-case letters, digits, dots and hyphens with at least one dot (com.koda.effects.canon-maker). It is required before a component is sealed and exported.

  output notes: Notes

Right

AMP2225 Attributes without a declaration

warning static since 1.0

Attributes are only read directly above a component declaration (or inside a component above a port or property).

Right

component koda.notes.tripleNotes version 1.0.0 {

  output notes: Notes

AMP2226 Fallback of an input is not notes

error static since 1.0

The fallback of an input is a property of type Notes of the same component: the notes that stand in when nothing is connected.

}

Right

  input source: Notes {

  }
}

error static since 1.0

A component says which capabilities it needs (requires clock). A process that reads the clock, OS randomness or the environment without saying so is refused; the policy of the song and the server decides whether it may.

  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes

  output notes: Notes

warning static since 1.0

The declarative ui of a component binds to properties and ports of that component.

Wrong

example: AMP2228

  input source: Notes
  property copies: Int = 3
  output notes: Notes

  }

AMP2230 Audio component contract not valid

error static since 1.0

A component that has Audio ports makes audio: Notes may go in (an instrument turns them into sound) but a Notes output next to Audio ports is not offered, and an Audio input has no fallback.

Wrong

example: AMP2230
component koda.fx.mixed version 1.0.0 {
  input audio: Audio
  output notes: Notes
  output audio: Audio
  process {
    emit audio
  }
}

Right

component koda.fx.dreamEcho version 1.0.0 {
  input audio: Audio
  property feedback: Percent = 30%
  property delayTime: Duration = 0.25beat
  output audio: Audio
  process {
    emit audio
      |> delay(time=delayTime, feedback=feedback)
  }
}

AMP2231 Unknown name in an audio process

error static since 1.0

A name in the process must be an input, or a let defined before it is used. Names are read top to bottom, so an audio graph can never loop back on itself.

Wrong

example: AMP2231
component koda.fx.dreamEcho version 1.0.0 {
  input audio: Audio
  property feedback: Percent = 30%
  property delayTime: Duration = 0.25beat
  output audio: Audio
  process {
    emit signal
      |> delay(time=delayTime, feedback=feedback)
  }
}

Right

component koda.fx.dreamEcho version 1.0.0 {
  input audio: Audio
  property feedback: Percent = 30%
  property delayTime: Duration = 0.25beat
  output audio: Audio
  process {
    emit audio
      |> delay(time=delayTime, feedback=feedback)
  }
}

AMP2232 Wrong type in an audio process

error static since 1.0

A processor takes Audio and gives Audio, and each argument has the unit of its parameter (a time for time, a Percent for a percentage, a Gain for dB, a frequency for Hz). Notes cannot go into an audio processor and the other way round.

Wrong

example: AMP2232
component koda.fx.dreamEcho version 1.0.0 {
  input audio: Audio
  property feedback: Percent = 30%
  property delayTime: Duration = 0.25beat
  output audio: Audio
  process {
    emit audio
      |> delay(time=feedback, feedback=feedback)
  }
}

Right

component koda.fx.dreamEcho version 1.0.0 {
  input audio: Audio
  property feedback: Percent = 30%
  property delayTime: Duration = 0.25beat
  output audio: Audio
  process {
    emit audio
      |> delay(time=delayTime, feedback=feedback)
  }
}

AMP2233 Audio graph too big or without output

error static since 1.0

An audio component has at most 64 processor nodes and 8 outputs, and every output must be given by an emit.

Wrong

example: AMP2233
component koda.fx.dreamEcho version 1.0.0 {
  input audio: Audio
  property feedback: Percent = 30%
  property delayTime: Duration = 0.25beat
  output audio: Audio
  process {
    let unused = audio
      |> delay(time=delayTime, feedback=feedback)
  }
}

Right

component koda.fx.dreamEcho version 1.0.0 {
  input audio: Audio
  property feedback: Percent = 30%
  property delayTime: Duration = 0.25beat
  output audio: Audio
  process {
    emit audio
      |> delay(time=delayTime, feedback=feedback)
  }
}

AMP2234 Unknown audio processor

error static since 1.0

The name is not a processor (an effect block with an audio in and an audio out, gain, pan or mix). A Notes operation cannot be used on Audio.

Wrong

  input audio: Audio
  property feedback: Percent = 30%
  property delayTime: Duration = 0.25beat
  output audio: Audio

}

Right

  property feedback: Percent = 30%
  property delayTime: Duration = 0.25beat

error static since 1.0

The argument is not a parameter of that processor. The hover of the processor lists them.

Wrong

AMP2236 Audio graph limit or note

warning static since 1.0

A note about an audio graph that does not stop the build: a processor without client preview, or a block that declares a delay (latency). The branches of one component are lined up inside it; to line the component up with the other tracks of the song too, write settings { audio.latencyCompensation on } (see AMP2250).

  input audio: Audio
  property feedback: Percent = 30%
  property delayTime: Duration = 0.25beat
  output audio: Audio
  process {
    emit audio
      |> delay(time=delayTime, feedback=feedback)
  }
}

Right

  input audio: Audio
  property feedback: Percent = 30%
  property delayTime: Duration = 0.25beat
  output audio: Audio
  process {
    emit audio
      |> delay(time=delayTime, feedback=feedback)
  }
}

error static since 1.0

A word of the ui block that is not a widget, a container or preview. The message lists the words.

A widget names a property (or, for a meter, an output) that the component does not have. A near name is suggested.

A knob, slider or xy needs a number property, a toggle a Bool, a choice a property with Options, a jam a Notes property. Use field for any type.

AMP2246 Not a colour

error static since 1.0

A tint (in a ui block or as #[Tint(...)]) is a colour name (accent, green, yellow, orange, red, pink, purple, blue, teal, gray) or a text such as "#ff8800".

AMP2247 Components call each other in a circle

error static since 1.0

A component never calls itself, directly or through other components: when A calls B and B calls A there is no end. Notes components call each other like a function (emit koda.notes.up(source, semitones=7)), audio components call each other as a processor (audio |> koda.fx.dreamEcho(feedback=20%)). The message names the circle (A -> B -> A). Break it by moving what both need into a third component that neither of them calls back.

Wrong

example: AMP2247
component koda.notes.ping version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit koda.notes.pong(source)
  }
}

component koda.notes.pong version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit koda.notes.ping(source)
  }
}

Right

component koda.notes.ping version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit koda.notes.pong(source)
  }
}

component koda.notes.pong version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source |> transpose(12)
  }
}

AMP2248 A call of a component does not fit

error static since 1.0

When a Notes component calls another Notes component, the first unnamed value is its first input and everything else is given by name: the other inputs and the properties (a property left out takes its default). This is reported for a name that the called component does not have, for a value that is not an input and for an input that is not given.

Wrong

example: AMP2248
component koda.notes.up version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  #[MinValue(0), MaxValue(12)]
  property semitones: Int = 2
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source |> transpose(semitones)
  }
}

component koda.notes.twice version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit koda.notes.up(source, octaves=2)
  }
}

Right

component koda.notes.up version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  #[MinValue(0), MaxValue(12)]
  property semitones: Int = 2
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source |> transpose(semitones)
  }
}

component koda.notes.twice version 1.0.0 {
  input source: Notes
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit koda.notes.up(source, semitones=7)
  }
}

AMP2249 A call names no version

info static since 1.0

A component that calls another component without a version gets the default version of it (the one marked current). When the called component gets a newer default, the caller makes something else, and a caller that is not sealed does not notice. Write the version in the call, koda.notes.up@2.0.0(source) (or @2.0, @^2.0), to keep the one you tested. A sealed component records what it calls in its hash and breaks its seal instead, so this is only said for components that are not sealed.

Wrong

example: AMP2249
component koda.notes.up version 1.0.0 {
  id "com.koda.test.up"
  input source: Notes
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source |> transpose(2)
  }
}

component koda.notes.up version 2.0.0 current {
  id "com.koda.test.up"
  input source: Notes
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source |> transpose(3)
  }
}

component koda.notes.twice version 1.0.0 {
  id "com.koda.test.twice"
  input source: Notes
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source |> merge(koda.notes.up(source))
  }
}

Right

component koda.notes.up version 1.0.0 {
  id "com.koda.test.up"
  input source: Notes
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source |> transpose(2)
  }
}

component koda.notes.up version 2.0.0 current {
  id "com.koda.test.up"
  input source: Notes
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source |> transpose(3)
  }
}

component koda.notes.twice version 1.0.0 {
  id "com.koda.test.twice"
  input source: Notes
  output notes: Notes
  process {
    emit source |> merge(koda.notes.up@2.0.0(source))
  }
}

AMP2250 Latency compensation is on

info static since 1.0

The song says settings { audio.latencyCompensation on }, so AMPLE put a shift block in front of every input of a mixer, bus, send or vocoder that arrives earlier than the latest input, and a cut block in front of the master that takes the remaining delay off the start. Only blocks whose template declares a latency (latencyMs) count; no built-in block does today, because the renderers look ahead over a whole file without delaying it. The setting is off by default: a song without it keeps its plan ids.

Wrong

example: AMP2250
composition "p" { ample 1  tempo 120  master-seed 1 }

midi-clip a at 1 for 1 {
  notes 1:0:1:60:100
}

synth s at 1 for 1 {
  from a.notes -> notes
}

master out {
  from s.audio -> audio
}

Right

composition "p" { ample 1  tempo 120  master-seed 1 }
settings { audio.latencyCompensation on }

midi-clip a at 1 for 1 {
  notes 1:0:1:60:100
}

synth s at 1 for 1 {
  from a.notes -> notes
}

master out {
  from s.audio -> audio
}

AMP5940 --bind needs an IP address

error runtime since 1.0

The address after --bind must be an IP address such as 127.0.0.1 or ::1, not a host name. Behind a reverse proxy on the same machine use 127.0.0.1 together with --allow-all, so only the proxy can reach the port.

AMP5941 Build parallelism out of range

error runtime since 1.0

A project may ask for fewer blocks rendered at the same time than the server allows (1 up to the limit of the server, which is at most the number of cores), or null to follow the server. More than the server allows is refused.

AMP1121 Section outside the bars

error static since 1.1

A section of the view block starts at bar 1 or later, lasts at least one bar and ends by bar 256 (the same limit as a part of a block).

Wrong

example: AMP1121
view {
  section "Drop" at 0 for 8
}

Right

view {
  section "Drop" at 1 for 8
}

AMP1122 Sections overlap

error static since 1.1

Two sections of the view block cover the same bar. Sections lie one after the other.

Wrong

example: AMP1122
view {
  section "A" at 1 for 8
  section "B" at 5 for 8
}

Right

view {
  section "A" at 1 for 8
  section "B" at 9 for 8
}

AMP1123 Two sections with one name

warning static since 1.1

Two sections of the view block have the same name. It does no harm, but they are hard to tell apart.

Wrong

example: AMP1123
view {
  section "A" at 1 for 8
  section "A" at 9 for 8
}

Right

view {
  section "A" at 1 for 8
  section "B" at 9 for 8
}

Lint rules

Lint rules find things that compile but are probably not what you meant. Set a level per rule with lint { L004 error }; silence a rule for the next block with # ample-ignore L004.

RuleNameDefaultFinds
L001unused-outputinfoA block has outputs that nothing reads.
L002missing-inputwarningA required input has no source.
L003lock-and-refreshwarningA block is locked and also marked always-refetch.
L004overlapping-partswarningTwo parts of the same block overlap in time.
L005dynamic-not-fixedoffA dynamic block is neither baked nor locked, so results can change between builds.
L006pinned-outdatedwarningA pinned block uses an older version than its template.
L007no-path-to-masterwarningA block that makes audio never reaches the master.
L008name-case-clashwarningTwo block names differ only by upper or lower case.
L009custom-seedinfoA block uses custom seeds instead of derived ones.
L010older-port-nameerrorA connection uses an older internal port name (in, out, mix, in3, render_in) instead of the name of the stream it carries (audio, notes, render, audio1); v1 only reads the stream names. ample migrate renames them.
L011pre-release-headererrorA block header uses the pre-release form class@version (stable@1.1, live@0.4); v1 leaves the class and the number out and only a pinned block states pinned@<version>. ample migrate converts the song.
L012clip-controller-ignoredwarningA midi-clip sets controllers that only the gm block (and midi-render) plays (modwheel, sustain, reverb_send, chorus_send, cc), and its notes reach another instrument, which plays only volume, expression and pan.
L013clip-controller-valueerrorA controller of a midi-clip is not a value it can play (a number outside its range, a word, or a cc that is not controller=value entries); the build would stop with AMP5506.

Command line reference

Ample.Cli

Reproducible song programming.

  • --help, -h, /h, -?, /?: Show help and usage information

Ample.Cli add

Creates a song, lyrics, chords, MIDI clip, module, sample folder, note or folder with a valid skeleton.

  • --folder: A project folder instead of the default one of the kind.
  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --list: Lists the kinds and their default folders.
  • <kind>: What to create: song, lyrics, chords, midi, module, component, samples, note, sequence, folder.
  • <name>: The name (letters, digits, spaces, _ and -); the extension is added.

Ample.Cli analyze

Analyses a take and keeps the result next to the project (computed once per audio, analyser, version and options; the take never changes).

  • --with: The analyser: tempo, key, loudness, spectrum, pitch or melody (an analysis plugin offers its own).
  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --options: Options as JSON, for example {"tempo":120} for melody.
  • --plugin: Use this analysis plugin instead of a built-in analyser.
  • --allow-gpu: Allow a plugin that needs the GPU to run (it is never started without this).
  • --allow-network: Allow a plugin that needs the network to run (it is never started without this).
  • --list: List the analysers and exit.
  • <take>: The take id (or the start of one).

Ample.Cli auth

Sign-in settings for `ample serve --login`.

Ample.Cli auth set-password

Stores the user and password for `ample serve --login` (only a salted hash is kept; the password is asked for without echo).

  • --user: The user name.
  • --home: The AMPLE user data folder (default: AMPLE_HOME or the local application data folder).

Ample.Cli backup

Incremental, verifiable backups of a project into a folder you choose.

Ample.Cli backup create

Makes a backup (only what changed since the last one is stored).

  • --target: The folder that holds the backups.
  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --no-takes: Leave out the takes and their data.

Ample.Cli backup list

Lists the backups, newest first.

  • --target: The folder that holds the backups.

Ample.Cli backup policy

Chooses where backups go and whether one is made before every dangerous act.

  • --target: The folder that holds the backups.
  • --auto: on or off: make a backup before every dangerous act.
  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).

Ample.Cli backup prune

Removes old backups (a dangerous act: run it without --accept for the dry run). The last good backup is always kept.

  • --target: The folder that holds the backups.
  • --keep: Keep the newest N backups.
  • --daily: Also keep the newest of each of the last D days.
  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --accept: The words the dry run asked you to type; without it nothing is removed.
  • --reason: Why (kept in the black box).

Ample.Cli backup verify

Rehashes every stored file of a backup; exit code 1 when anything is missing or damaged.

  • --target: The folder that holds the backups.
  • <backup>: A backup id (or a unique start of it); default: latest.

Ample.Cli bake

Renders a block at full quality and marks it baked in the song source.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the folder above the song that has .ample).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder with spec/ (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <song>: The .amplet song file.
  • <block>: The block to bake.

Ample.Cli bake-notes

Bakes the note pipeline of a midi-clip: stores its notes, signed, in a bake stage (or in a file).

  • --stage: The bake stage to bake (default: the last one; a stage called baked is added when there is none).
  • --file: Keep the notes in this project file instead of in the stage.
  • --detach: Turn the pipeline into plain notes instead of baking it.
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <song>: The .amplet file.
  • <block>: The midi-clip whose note pipeline is baked.

Ample.Cli blackbox

AMPLE Redux recovery archive (legacy command name).

Ample.Cli blackbox compact

Explicitly thins old AMPLE Redux records to hourly summaries and applies the size budget.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).

Ample.Cli blackbox export

Writes all records to a file as text.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • <file>: Output file.

Ample.Cli blackbox restore

Restores a file from the pre-image of a record, as a new command (the history stays).

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • <seq>: A record number.

Ample.Cli blackbox show

Shows one record in full, including its pre-image.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • <seq>: A record number.

Ample.Cli blackbox simulate-crash

For tests: writes the start of a file write to the black box and stops, as a crash would (the next health check finds it).

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • <file>: A project file (relative path).

Ample.Cli blackbox tail

Shows the last records of the black box.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • -n: How many records.

Ample.Cli blackbox verify

Checks the checksums and the hash chain; exit code 1 when a record was changed or damaged.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).

Ample.Cli build

Renders the song; blocks whose plan is unchanged come from the cache.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the folder above the song that has .ample).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder with spec/ (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • --block: Build only this block and what it needs.
  • --preview: Preview: low quality, optionally a range, for example 5:4 (four bars from bar 5), or just 'all'.
  • --out: Write the master here: a WAV file, or mp3 / flac when the name ends so (needs ffmpeg on the PATH; default: out/<song>.wav in the project). With --block: write that block's sound here.
  • <song>: The .amplet song file.

Ample.Cli check

Validates a song file; exit code 1 when there are errors.

  • --format: Output format: text or json.
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <file>: The .amplet file.

Ample.Cli check quality

Measures takes (clipping, true peak, loudness, silence, DC offset, sample rate) against the rules of spec/quality-rules.json and the project policy. Advisory: the exit code is 1 only when a rule the policy requires fails.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --take: A take id (or the start of one). Default: the newest take of every block that has audio.

Ample.Cli checkpoint

Takes a snapshot of the sources (nothing happens when nothing changed).

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • -m: Message.

Ample.Cli choose

Selects a take for a block (it is used when the block is baked).

  • --project: The project folder (default: found above the song).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder with spec/.
  • <song>: The .amplet song file.
  • <block>: The block.
  • <take>: A take id or unique prefix.

Ample.Cli cleanup

Removes unreachable history content. Without --accept you see the dry run.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --accept: The exact acceptance text for a dangerous act.
  • --reason: Why (recorded in the black box).

Ample.Cli components

Reusable typed blocks of Notes code: list what a song can see, check a file of components, seal a version, make a new one.

Ample.Cli components check

Reads a file of components and prints the problems of its components (contract, attributes, defaults, process).

  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <file>: A .amplec or .amplet file.

Ample.Cli components detach

Detaches a sealed embedded component for editing: removes its seal, so it builds as a development version.

  • --version: The version of the component (needed when the file has several).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <song>: The .amplet file.
  • <name>: The component (as declared).

Ample.Cli components embed

Embeds components (with their dependency closure) in the song, inside an embedded module that keeps their module boundary.

  • --module: The name of the embedded module (default: the file the first component comes from).
  • --whole: Embed everything of the files the components come from.
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <song>: The .amplet file.
  • <components>: The components to embed (their dependencies come with them).

Ample.Cli components extract

Extracts an embedded component to a new .amplec file and makes the song import it. Identity, version and seal are kept.

  • --version: The version of the component (needed when the file has several).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <song>: The .amplet file.
  • <name>: The component (as declared).
  • <file>: The new .amplec file, relative to the song (also the path the song imports it by).

Ample.Cli components graph

Prints the internal graph of an instance of an Audio component: its processors with parameters and links, the latency and what the browser can preview.

  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <song>: The .amplet file.
  • <block>: The instance of an Audio component.

Ample.Cli components list

Lists the components a song can see (its own and the imported ones) with every version, its seal and signature.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the folder of the song).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <song>: The .amplet file.

Ample.Cli components migrate

Shows (and with --apply makes) the migration of one instance to another version: the chain, the impact and the changed properties. An impactful migration is never applied without --acknowledge.

  • --apply: Write the migrated song (without it only the preview is printed).
  • --acknowledge: Accept an impact of musicalChange or destructive (needed with --apply).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <song>: The .amplet file.
  • <block>: The instance (block name).
  • <target>: The version to migrate to (4.0.0), or id@version for another component.

Ample.Cli components new-version

Makes a working copy of a version with a new version number, without its seal; the original is untouched.

  • --from: The version to copy (needed when the file has several).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <file>: The file that holds the component.
  • <name>: The component.
  • <new-version>: The version of the copy (1.2.1).

Ample.Cli components seal

Seals a version: writes the seal block (payload and semantic hash, optionally a signature). A sealed version is immutable.

  • --version: The version of the component (needed when the file has several).
  • --sign: Sign the seal with the active key of the library (the passphrase comes from AMPLE_VAULT_PASSPHRASE).
  • --signed-by: The name written next to the signature (default: the user name).
  • --home: The library folder that holds the keys (default: the user library).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <file>: The .amplec or .amplet file that holds the component.
  • <name>: The component (its name as declared).

Ample.Cli components unseal

Removes the seal of a version, so that it can be changed again. Anything that pinned its hash sees the change (AMP2203).

  • --version: The version of the component (needed when the file has several).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <file>: The file that holds the component.
  • <name>: The component.

Ample.Cli components use-template

Uses the template source again for an embedded component. Only when id, version and payload are exactly the same.

  • --version: The version of the component (needed when the file has several).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <song>: The .amplet file.
  • <name>: The component (as declared).

Ample.Cli credits

Writes the credit sheet of the project: what made each block (from the plans of the takes), the modules and library assets in use with their licences, and the people in .ample/credits.json. Advisory, not legal advice.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --format: md or json.
  • --out: Write the sheet to this file instead of the screen.
  • --write: Also keep the sheet in .ample/credits/ so that backups and exports carry it.
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).

Ample.Cli docs

Builds and checks the generated help.

Ample.Cli docs build

Generates the offline help.html from the spec, docs and command tree.

  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • --out: Output file for the help page (default: docs/help/help.html in the AMPLE folder).

Ample.Cli docs check

Fails when the committed help.html is out of date or a source has problems (dead links, failing examples).

  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).

Ample.Cli doctor

Checks a project folder without changing it; exit code 1 when there are errors.

  • --env: Also check what the tools and the assistant need around the program (libraries, ffmpeg, Python, the sound font, disk space); what is missing goes to the project log with how to fix it.
  • --sound: Build this song (a path in the project) and report the sound of its blocks: silent, very quiet, clipping, not heard, and the loudness of the master, with suggested gains.
  • --root: The AMPLE folder with spec/ (default: found from the current folder upwards); used with --sound.
  • --json: With --sound: write the findings as JSON.
  • --fix: With --sound: put the suggested effect blocks (normalize for a very quiet block, a lower volume for a clipping one) into the song; the journal keeps the old text.
  • <folder>: The project folder.

Ample.Cli drop

Drops (archives) a line. Without --accept you see the dry run.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --accept: The exact acceptance text for a dangerous act.
  • --reason: Why (recorded in the black box).
  • <name>: A line, tag or node name.

Ample.Cli encrypt

Optional encryption at rest of the black box and of backups (off by default). The passphrase comes from AMPLE_PASSPHRASE.

Ample.Cli encrypt disable

Switches encryption off again (a dangerous act: run it without --accept for the dry run).

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --accept: The words the dry run asked you to type; without it nothing changes.
  • --reason: Why (kept in the black box).

Ample.Cli encrypt enable

Switches encryption on (a dangerous act: run it without --accept for the dry run). The new passphrase is read from AMPLE_PASSPHRASE.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --accept: The words the dry run asked you to type; without it nothing changes.
  • --reason: Why (kept in the black box).

Ample.Cli encrypt passphrase

Changes the passphrase (nothing is re-encrypted). The old one is read from AMPLE_PASSPHRASE, the new one from AMPLE_NEW_PASSPHRASE.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).

Ample.Cli encrypt recovery-kit

Writes the recovery kit of an encrypted project.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --out: The file to write the recovery kit to (it contains the key: keep it offline).

Ample.Cli encrypt status

Says whether the project is encrypted.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).

Ample.Cli explain

Says what each kind of edit does to a block at its freeze level.

  • --project: The project folder (default: found above the song).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder with spec/.
  • <song>: The .amplet song file.
  • <block>: The block.

Ample.Cli export

Writes the project (without secrets) into one archive that any zip tool can read.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --no-takes: Leave out the takes and their data.
  • <file>: The archive to write (for example song.ample).

Ample.Cli fmt

Rewrites a song file into the canonical form.

  • --check: Do not write; exit code 1 when the file is not formatted.
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <file>: The .amplet file.

Ample.Cli follow-suggest

Looks at a recording and suggests the settings of a follow block (band, baseline, attack, release); write them in the block to keep them.

  • <file>: A .wav file (a recording with passing cars, a drum loop, ...).

Ample.Cli fork

Creates a new line (default: at the current line's head).

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --from: A line, tag or node.
  • <name>: A line, tag or node name.

Ample.Cli go

Switches the working files to a line (unsaved work is checkpointed first).

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • <name>: A line, tag or node name.

Ample.Cli help

Shows help topics in the terminal (the same sources as help.html).

  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <topic>: A page id or part of a title; without it the topics are listed.

Ample.Cli history

Shows the lines and the newest snapshots of the current line.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).

Ample.Cli import

Imports an archive into a new folder after checking every hash.

  • --new-id: Give the imported project a new id (default: it keeps its id).
  • <file>: The archive.
  • <folder>: A new folder to import into.

Ample.Cli instances

Lists running AMPLE server instances.

  • --json: Write active instances as JSON.
  • --clean: Remove stale registry records before listing.
  • --home: The AMPLE home folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data folder).

Ample.Cli keys

The signing keys of the user (ECDSA P-256). The private key is sealed with the passphrase of the vault.

Ample.Cli keys export

Prints the public key (PEM) for someone who verifies your signatures.

  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).
  • <key>: The key id.

Ample.Cli keys generate

Makes a signing key.

  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).

Ample.Cli keys list

Lists the keys.

  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).

Ample.Cli keys rotate

Retires the active key (it keeps verifying old signatures, but cannot sign any more) and makes a new one.

  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).

Ample.Cli library

Linked folders (catalogs), the assets in them, and what a project uses.

Ample.Cli library add

Copies a file into a writable linked folder and scans it. A read-only folder is refused.

  • --into: The linked folder (id or name); it must be read-write.
  • --as: Path inside the folder (default: the file name).
  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).
  • <file>: The file to copy into a writable linked folder.

Ample.Cli library link

Links a folder and scans it.

  • --name: A name (default: the folder name).
  • --read-write: Allow AMPLE to write into it (a marker file with the catalog id is written). Default: read-only.
  • --for-project: Link it for the project only.
  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).
  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • <path>: The folder to link (you choose it; nothing is found automatically).

Ample.Cli library list

Lists the linked folders with their state, and the assets.

  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).

Ample.Cli library relocate

Points a linked folder at its new place (checked by its marker, fingerprint or files). No song changes.

  • --force: Link it even if it does not look like the same catalog.
  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).
  • <folder>: A linked folder (id or name).
  • <new-path>: Where the folder is now.

Ample.Cli library scan

Scans a linked folder incrementally (unchanged files are not read).

  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).
  • <folder>: A linked folder (id or name).

Ample.Cli library verify

Hashes the assets again and compares them with the catalog; exit code 1 when anything is not ok.

  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).
  • <folder>: A linked folder (id or name); default: all.

Ample.Cli lint

Shows only the lint rules (L001 and up) for a song file; exit code 1 when a rule is set to error.

  • --format: Output format: text or json.
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <file>: The .amplet file.

Ample.Cli lite-worker

Builds one Remix request that arrives on the standard input (started by the server, not by people).

  • --root: The AMPLE folder.
  • --work: The private folder of this build.

Ample.Cli lock

ample.lock: the assets, packs and plugins a project depends on, pinned by hash.

Ample.Cli lock update

Works out what the songs use and writes ample.lock (accepts changed assets).

  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).
  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).

Ample.Cli lock verify

Compares ample.lock with the catalog; exit code 1 when anything is not ok.

  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).
  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).

Ample.Cli lsp

Runs the language server (Language Server Protocol 3.17) on stdin and stdout. Editors start this; nothing else is printed.

  • --root: The AMPLE folder with spec/ (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • --help-base: Where diagnostic codes link to (default /help).

Ample.Cli mcp

Runs an MCP server on stdio with task-scoped AMPLE context and constrained actions, including approved visible-browser actions (started by an AI agent, not by hand). The token of the task comes from the environment variable AMPLE_CONTEXT_TOKEN.

  • --url: The address of the running AMPLE server.

Ample.Cli midi

MIDI file conversion commands.

Ample.Cli midi convert

Converts an SMF file into a project module.

  • --project: Project folder (default: current folder).
  • --output: Generated module name in modules/ (letters, digits, _ and -).
  • <file>: Input .mid or .midi file.

Ample.Cli midi soundfont-check

Checks GM preset and percussion coverage in an SF2 bank.

  • --file: Project-relative SF2 file or pack:musescore-general.

Ample.Cli midi verify-conversion

Checks that a MIDI file parses and converts to a valid module without writing project files.

  • <file>: Input .mid or .midi file to parse and convert in memory.

Ample.Cli migrate

Moves a song to the current AMPLE version: shows the steps and the changed lines first, writes only with --write.

  • --write: Write the migrated song (without it the command only shows what would change).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <file>: The .amplet file.

Ample.Cli modules

Reusable modules: groups of blocks with parameters, inputs and outputs, used with 'use' in a song.

Ample.Cli modules add

Checks a module file and copies it into the project's modules/ folder.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • <file>: The module file to copy into the project.

Ample.Cli modules expand

Prints the song with every use replaced by the blocks of its module, and the problems found.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <file>: The .amplet file.

Ample.Cli modules list

Lists the modules of the project's modules/ folder.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).

Ample.Cli mv

Moves or renames a project file or folder and, by default, updates every path in the songs and modules that points at it.

  • --no-refactor: Move only the file; paths in songs and modules that point at it are not changed (they may break).
  • --dry-run: Print the changes without making them.
  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • <from>: The project file or folder to move or rename (project-relative).
  • <to>: Its new project-relative path.

Ample.Cli new

Creates a project folder with the mandatory .ample structure.

  • --name: Project name (default: the folder name).
  • --seed: Master seed (default: derived from the project id).
  • <folder>: The project folder.

Ample.Cli open

Attaches to or starts the server for a project.

  • --last: Open the most recently used project.
  • --visible: Show a console window for the server.
  • --no-open: Start or attach without opening a browser.
  • --song: Song path to open when song deep links are supported.
  • --agent: Self-reported agent name; requires --reason.
  • --reason: Why the agent is opening this project.
  • --home: The AMPLE user data folder (default: AMPLE_HOME or the local application data folder).
  • <target>: A project folder, .amplet song or .module file.

Ample.Cli packs

Lists and links the user-level installed audio packs.

Ample.Cli packs link

Creates a junction to an existing audio-packs folder; it never copies packs.

  • --home: The AMPLE user folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).
  • <folder>: Existing audio-packs folder to link into the user-level AMPLE home.

Ample.Cli packs list

Lists the pack folders in lookup order.

  • --home: The AMPLE user folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).

Ample.Cli packs where

Shows where an installed pack file is found.

  • --home: The AMPLE user folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).
  • <asset>: A path below an installed pack (default: the MuseScore General SoundFont).

Ample.Cli peek

Looks at a line, tag or node without changing anything.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --file: Print this file of the peeked state.
  • <name>: A line, tag or node name.

Ample.Cli plan

Plan commands.

Ample.Cli plan show

Prints the plan (the complete recipe) a take was made from.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • <take>: A take id or a unique prefix.

Ample.Cli play

Builds a preview and writes the WAV (no player is started).

  • --project: The project folder (default: the folder above the song that has .ample).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder with spec/ (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • --out: Write the master here: a WAV file, or mp3 / flac when the name ends so (needs ffmpeg on the PATH; default: out/<song>.wav in the project). With --block: write that block's sound here.
  • <song>: The .amplet song file.

Ample.Cli plugins

Plugins.

Ample.Cli plugins describe

Shows a plugin's manifest and settings schema.

  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • --folder: An extra folder with plugins.
  • <plugin>: A plugin id.

Ample.Cli plugins list

Lists the plugins that are found.

  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • --folder: An extra folder with plugins.

Ample.Cli plugins run

Starts a plugin, does the handshake and asks it to describe itself (a self-test; no render).

  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • --folder: An extra folder with plugins.
  • <plugin>: A plugin id.

Ample.Cli plugins validate

Checks a plugin manifest; exit code 1 when it has problems.

  • <folder>: A plugin folder (with plugin.json).

Ample.Cli project

Project commands.

Ample.Cli project info

Prints a project summary without taking the writer lock.

  • <folder>: The project folder.

Ample.Cli project open

Opens a project for writing (takes the instance lock), prints a summary and releases it.

  • <folder>: The project folder.

Ample.Cli promote

Shows what promoting a line into another would change; --yes does it.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --source: Source line.
  • --to: Target line.
  • --yes: Do it (without it you only see the preview).

Ample.Cli recover

Lists commands that were interrupted (no outcome record) with what they were about to overwrite.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).

Ample.Cli regen

Regenerates a block safely: the selected take is kept, the new result is verified, and a difference becomes a decision whose default is to restore the previous take.

  • --project: The project folder (default: found above the song).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder with spec/.
  • --seed: Seed for the regeneration (default: derived).
  • --decide: Answer an open regeneration decision (its id).
  • --keep-variant: With --decide: keep the new take as a variant (default: restore the previous take).
  • <song>: The .amplet song file.
  • <block>: The block.

Ample.Cli restore

Restores a backup into a new folder, or in place as a dangerous act.

  • --target: The folder that holds the backups.
  • --in-place: Put the backup into an existing project (a dangerous act: run it without --accept for the dry run).
  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --accept: The words the dry run asked you to type.
  • --reason: Why (kept in the black box).
  • <backup>: A backup id (or a unique start of it), or latest.
  • <folder>: A new folder to restore into (not with --in-place).

Ample.Cli seed

Shows or changes the seed of a block. Seeds are locked by default.

  • --project: The project folder (default: found above the song).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder with spec/.
  • --unlock: Unlock the seed (changing it probably makes reproduction impossible).
  • --lock: Lock the seed.
  • --set: Set the seed (needs it to be unlocked).
  • --randomize: Give the seed a new derived value (needs it to be unlocked).
  • --reason: Why (recorded in the history).
  • <song>: The .amplet song file.
  • <block>: The block.

Ample.Cli seeds

Lists the stable random namespaces of a song with how often each is used and the seeds of every note pipeline; with --pick it writes a number for every random-seed().

  • --pick: Replace every random-seed() by a number chosen once from OS randomness.
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • <song>: The .amplet file.

Ample.Cli serve

Starts the local server with the web UI, the API and the help (127.0.0.1 only).

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder (default: found from the current folder upwards).
  • --home: The AMPLE user data folder (default: AMPLE_HOME or the local application data folder).
  • --port: Port on 127.0.0.1 (default: a free one).
  • --max-upload-mb: Maximum project file upload size in MiB (1 to 512).
