  • --forbid-capabilities: Comma-separated capabilities that no project, song or proposal can ever use on this server (clock, os-random, environment, network, filesystem, external-process, external-plugin). A public playground forbids the sensitive ones.
  • --environment-allow: Comma-separated names (patterns like TZ, LANG*, *_HOME) that environment() may read on this server; every other name is refused.
  • --no-browser: Do not open the browser.
  • --visible: Keep the server in a visible console window.
  • --no-token-output: Do not print the private token launch URL.
  • --allow-lan: Accept other host names. Only on a trusted network: the session token is the only protection.
  • --login: Also accept a sign-in with the user and password set by `ample auth set-password` (page: /login). The launch token keeps working.
  • --allow-all: Listen on every address and accept any host name (for a tunnel). Only together with --login.
  • --bind: The IP address to listen on (default: 0.0.0.0 with --allow-lan or --allow-all, else 127.0.0.1). Behind a reverse proxy on the same machine use 127.0.0.1 together with --allow-all.
  • --parallelism: How many blocks a build may render at the same time on this server: at most the number of cores of the machine, which is also the default (one per core). A project can ask for fewer, never for more. The environment variable AMPLE_PARALLELISM does the same.
  • --lite-only: The public Remix: only the Remix page, its API and its language server exist (everything else is a 404), no sign-in or token is asked, the limits of the public profile hold and every build runs in a process of its own. Listens on 127.0.0.1 only: put a reverse proxy in front.
  • --log-file: Write server output to this rolling log file.
  • --started-by: Start source for launcher integration.
  • --agent-name: Self-reported agent name for launcher integration.
  • --agent-reason: Reason for an agent-started server.
  • --openapi: Write the OpenAPI document to this file and exit (no project needed).

Ample.Cli sign

Signs the newest record of the black box (or a file) with your signing key. The passphrase of the key is read from AMPLE_VAULT_PASSPHRASE.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).
  • --file: Sign this file (an export) instead of the black box; the signature goes next to it as <file>.sig.

Ample.Cli storage

What the takebank uses, what could be given back, the clean-up and the storage options.

Ample.Cli storage clean

A dry run of a clean-up (what would go, what stays protected); with --accept <fingerprint> it runs.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --accept: The fingerprint printed by the dry run; with it the clean-up is run.

Ample.Cli storage compress

Compresses the plain WAV takes of the project in place (lossless: the takes and their ids do not change).

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).

Ample.Cli storage move

Moves the take data to another folder or drive (progress is shown; a stopped move continues when run again).

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • <path>: The folder for the take data (for example D:\ample-takes\song), or - to move it back into the project.

Ample.Cli storage settings

Shows or changes the storage options of the project.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --soft-limit-gb: The size above which a clean-up is suggested (0: off).
  • --keep-superseded: How many older takes of a block stay besides the current one.
  • --archive-path: Move reclaimed data here instead of deleting it (empty: delete).

Ample.Cli storage show

Shows the size of the takebank, what is protected and what could be given back.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).

Ample.Cli tag

Creates a locked tag.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --from: A line, tag or node.
  • --reason: Why (recorded in the black box).
  • <name>: A line, tag or node name.

Ample.Cli takes

Takebank commands.

Ample.Cli takes list

Lists the takes of a project, newest first.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).

Ample.Cli takes show

Shows one take with its plan id and data.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • <take>: A take id or a unique prefix.

Ample.Cli takes verify

Rehashes the data of a take (or of all takes); exit code 1 on missing, truncated or damaged data.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • <take>: A take id or prefix; without it every take is verified.

Ample.Cli variants

Makes several takes of a block to choose from (the same request gives the same variants) and lists them.

  • --project: The project folder (default: found above the song).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder with spec/.
  • --count: How many.
  • --kind: variant, resing (new voice, same melody) or rewrite (new melody).
  • <song>: The .amplet song file.
  • <block>: The block.

Ample.Cli vault

Secrets (API keys, tokens) kept outside every project. Plugins get only the secrets their manifest names.

Ample.Cli vault list

Lists the names of the secrets (never the values).

  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).

Ample.Cli vault remove

Removes a secret.

  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).
  • <name>: The name of the secret.

Ample.Cli vault set

Stores a secret. The value is read from standard input; the passphrase of the vault from AMPLE_VAULT_PASSPHRASE (a new vault is made when there is none).

  • --home: The library folder (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).
  • <name>: The name of the secret (letters, digits, _ - .).

Ample.Cli verify

Checks the hash chain of the black box and every signature of the project (or the signature of a file). Exit code 1 when anything is wrong.

  • --project: The project folder (default: the current folder).
  • --file: Check the signature of this file (<file>.sig) instead of the project.
  • --trust: Only accept signatures of this key id.

Ample.Cli verify-reproduction

Re-renders the selected take's own plan only to check reproduction; never replaces anything.

  • --project: The project folder (default: found above the song).
  • --root: The AMPLE folder with spec/.
  • <song>: The .amplet song file.
  • <block>: The block.

API reference

The API of ample serve: loopback only, every call carries the session token in X-Ample-Token, every error is RFC 9457 problem details with the AMP code. Generated from docs/api/openapi.json.

acts

MethodPathWhat it does
POST/api/acts/cleanupDry run of the history cleanup; returns a token and what to type. Read only.
POST/api/acts/confirmSecond step: confirm a dry run with the token, the typed acceptance and a reason. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/acts/drop-lineDry run of dropping a line; returns a token and what to type. Read only.
POST/api/acts/master-seedDry run of changing the master seed; returns a token and what to type. Read only.
POST/api/acts/prune-backupsDry run of pruning old backups (the last good one stays); returns a token and what to type. Read only.
POST/api/acts/replace-takeDry run of replacing the selected take with a regenerated one. Read only.
POST/api/acts/restore-in-placeDry run of restoring a backup into this project; returns a token and what to type. Read only.
POST/api/acts/retagDry run of moving or removing a tag. Read only.
POST/api/acts/unlink-mountDry run of unlinking a folder from the library (no file is touched); returns a token and what to type. Read only.

ai

MethodPathWhat it does
POST/api/ai/attachmentKeeps an audio file the user offers to Codex (WAV bytes in the body, or mp3/ogg/flac with ?extension=; name= is the file name). Nothing of it is in the project: it is only offered to a task (offered: [id]) and comes along into the project only when the user chooses so at Accept. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/attachment/{id}/audioAn offered audio file, to listen to before it is given to Codex or taken along. Read only.
POST/api/ai/browser/inputA click, scroll, typing or key of the person into the assistant's browser window while it waits for a person (type click|move|scroll|type|key, x, y, dy, text). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/browser/viewThe assistant's browser window as a picture (JPEG, base64) while it waits for a person (sign-in, a human check); active=false otherwise. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/accessFor an AI task: asks the person to allow writing to a place outside the project (path, why, minutes, kind write or passthrough). The call waits for the answer: allow for that long, always for the project, or deny. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/analyzeRead-only context for an AI task: the reference analysers (tempo, key, loudness, spectrum, pitch) on the built audio of a block. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/analyze-audioFor an AI task: a deterministic look at one audio file (a project file or workspace/<path>): length, level, brightness, pitch of a single note, likely key, tempo and whether it loops in whole bars. Read-only, no AI. Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/answerFor an AI task that answers a question from Koda: delivers the answer as a title, a short answer and the details (markdown) the user can unfold. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/context/arrangementFor an AI task: the arrangement of the song before the task and now (where the blocks sit in bars and seconds, the slice of the master), what changed, and with measure=true the real length, peak and silence of the built master of the proposal next to the current project. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/arrangement-lintFor an AI task: which blocks of a song play in which bars, the density per bar and what looks wrong (silent bars, harmony without a bass, nothing that builds). Reads only the placements. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/beatsThe beats catalogue (original CC0 grooves) for an AI task, small by default: overview=true, a search with genre, family, mood, form, bpm, novelty, energy, text, limit and offset, similar=<id>, id=<id> with parts, or queries=[...] for several searches in one call. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/blockRead-only context for an AI task: one block with what feeds it and what it feeds. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/blocktypesRead-only context for an AI task: the block types. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/browser-clickFor an AI task: clicks a numbered element from the latest browser-read result; purchase actions are blocked. Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/browser-jsFor an AI task: executes owner-authorized JavaScript in the visible page; may change page state or trigger actions and can bypass the numbered-click purchase block. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/context/browser-media-muteFor an AI task: mutes or unmutes HTML audio and video elements on the current page; does not control browser tab/system audio. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/browser-mouse-moveFor an AI task: moves the pointer inside the visible page viewport for hovering; does not click. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/browser-network-statsFor an AI task: returns aggregate console error and network resource counts without message text, URLs, headers or bodies. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/browser-openFor an AI task: after explicit task approval, opens a URL in the visible persistent Chromium window. The owner enters credentials manually. Purchase actions are unavailable. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/browser-readFor an AI task: reads the visible page title and text, returning visible links, buttons and text fields with indexes for browser-click and browser-type. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/browser-screenshotFor an AI task: captures the visible page screenshot and returns it for visual inspection, without saving it as a download. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/browser-showFor an AI task: after explicit browser approval, makes its isolated headless Chromium window visible for owner inspection or manual interaction. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/browser-typeFor an AI task: fills a numbered non-credential text field from the latest browser-read result; password, username and account fields are never filled. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/changes-sinceFor a resumed AI task: how the project changed since the working copy was based on it (overview), the diff of one file, or import=true to bring the project's version of a file into the copy. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/checkFor an AI task: the errors and warnings that the proposal introduced (the ones the song did not have before); none means it can be handed in. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/component-libraryFor an AI task: searches the library of the proposal (query words, tag, imported=yes|no): every component of every .amplec file with description, tags, kind, seal, whether the song imports it, the import line to write and the block type to use (an alias when the name is taken). Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/componentsFor an AI task: the components a song of the proposal can see, every version with its seal, signature and deprecation, the contract of the default version and the problems of putting them together. Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/copy-fileCopy a text file within an AI staged proposal to a new path, without overwriting; the source stays. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/context/docsRead-only context for an AI task: the reference documents (list, one, or a search). Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/editFor an AI task: structured edits (replace, insert, delete_lines, set_param, add_block, remove_block, connect, disconnect, create) of a file of the temporary copy, all or nothing; the answer lists the new errors and warnings and the diff. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/context/faerRead-only context for an AI task: independent project Faer routes, aggregate capability readiness and installed ACE model filenames, roles and sizes, without credentials or job content. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/fetchFor an AI task: AMPLE downloads a public web address for Codex (which has no network). A link from the user's request is fetched at once, another link needs the user's approval. Public addresses only, images, text, audio, JSON, XML or PDF, at most 10 MB. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/fetch-sampleFor an AI task: fetches a real sample for the proposal. AMPLE reads the page itself and only a CC0 or public-domain licence on freesound.org, archive.org or opengameart.org lets the audio file (wav, mp3, ogg, flac, aif) through, at most 25 MB, into assets/web of the working copy; the answer has a ready SOURCE.md text. no approval is asked because the licence is checked here. browser=true does the same with the signed-in browser of AMPLE for a sound that needs a sign-in (it needs the browser permission of the task). Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/fileRead-only context for an AI task: a text file of the project (a PDF: its text), in a window; an offset reads on past a truncated one. Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/find-patternsFor an AI task: finds a shorter way to write the notes of a midi-clip or a sequencer channel: a rhythm that repeats with pitches, velocities and other settings that cycle, as a note pipeline that was evaluated and compared with the original. Read-only. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/find-samplesFor an AI task: finds real samples by itself. AMPLE reads the CC0 search of Freesound (and the public-domain search of the Internet Archive) without a sign-in, reads every candidate page and checks its licence, and answers with candidates ready for fetch-sample (page and file). text=words (for example dj scratch), source=freesound|archive|all, limit up to 8. Read-only; nothing is downloaded. Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/findingsFor an AI task: writes the model's remarks (what is missing, what could be better) to notes/ai-findings/ inside the project; no permission is needed. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/context/generateFor an AI task: deterministic pattern generators (euclid, groove, arpeggio, bassline, fill) from a small query with a seed. Read-only, no AI. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/historyFor an AI task: what the user asked before in this project and what came out (newest first; id= for one request in full with its changes). Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/humFor an AI task: the melody found in a hummed recording that the user attached (notes, key, the notes text of a midi-clip), at the tempo of the song or the one asked for. Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/import-scoreFor an AI task: turns a MIDI or MusicXML score of the project into a new sequence file in the proposal (one channel per part, patterns of a number of bars, a playlist). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/context/install-packFor an AI task: downloads a .zip sample-pack archive from a public web address and installs it into the user's library (packs/<name>@<version>), available to every project afterward. Always needs the user's approval, even when the link was given in the request. At most 200 MB; the archive must contain a pack.json. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/listenFor an AI task: builds the proposal in a temporary project and measures a block (or the master) with analysers (default loudness and spectrum), next to the same block of the real project when it is built. Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/listenFor an AI task: like GET listen, with a trial: edits (the format of the edit tool) that are applied only in the temporary project of this call, to hear a variant without changing the proposal. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/context/lookupFor an AI task: more about units, a parameter (unit, range, what a change reaches), the impact of a block (what is rendered again) or a word (block types, parameters and documents), for the song as the task has it now. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/memoryFor an AI task: the notes kept for later tasks outside the song, scope=project or scope=song (the song of the task). Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/memoryFor an AI task: adds a dated note to (mode=append, the default) or rewrites (mode=replace) the memory of the project or of the song; it is kept in the .ample folder, never in the song. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/context/mix-hintsFor an AI task: mix starting points (volume, pan, filter, EQ, compression, sends) per instrument and genre as AMPLE block parameters. Read-only. Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/moveFor an AI task: proposes moving a project file or folder with the references following. With confirm ask the owner is asked now and the call waits for the answer; with propose the move is listed with the proposal and ticked at Accept. Nothing is moved before Accept. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/context/move-fileMove a text file within an AI staged proposal without overwriting; workspace/filename recovers a misplaced root song. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/context/obsoleteFor an AI task: marks one previously presented sample obsolete with a reason; it remains in the output until the user dismisses it. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/context/offeredFor an AI task: the audio files the user offered (length, level, pitch, the path the song uses for them, whether the proposal uses them). Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/presentFor an AI task: shows the user a piece of sound (the render of a block, whole or a slice, from the proposal or the current project) in the task window. Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/presentPresents a clip with optional temporary structured trial edits; reports rendered settings and identical audio. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/projectRead-only context for an AI task: what the project is, its linked sample-pack catalogs, and a searchable, filterable, paged list of its files. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/project-logFor an AI task: the project log, what is missing for the tools of the project and how to put it right. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/redux-searchFor an AI task: read-only search of the task's AMPLE Redux archive; scope=project expands to this project's journal. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/request-assetFor an AI task: asks the user to let Codex read a large or non-text source asset; AMPLE copies it into the working folder of the task when it is allowed. The answer comes when the user has decided. Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/resolve-notesFor an AI task: the notes of a midi-clip, of a sequencer channel or of a note pipeline (expression) in one form (count, bars, signature, first notes), and with compare_block / compare_channel / compare_expression whether the two are exactly the same (every note, length and setting). Read-only. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/revisionFor an AI task: what one revision of the project history changed against the one before it, or the diff of one file of it. Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/sample-set-addAdd one audio file as a WAV to a sample set folder of an AI staged proposal, optionally with its loop points and the set's envelope; never overwrites. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/context/sample-sourcesFor an AI task: where real, legal samples can be found (a DJ scratch, a vinyl crackle, a foley sound) and how they come into a project: the rules (CC0 or public domain by default, the source written down, nothing bought or downloaded without the owner) and the places with their licence. text=words puts the places that fit first. Read-only, no AI. Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/skip-buildFor an AI task: honor the user's explicit no-build or no-render request while still validating source changes. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/context/songRead-only context for an AI task: a song with its blocks and problems. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/thoughtFor an AI task: shows the user what the AI is thinking about right now (a short note that replaces the previous one). Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/variantsFor an AI task: offers 2 to 6 alternatives that are all part of the proposal (name, summary, the blocks that belong to each, the block to listen to), so the user can compare, hear and keep one. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/context/web-readFor an AI task: reads a public HTML URL supplied by the user or returned by this task's approved search, without cookies or JavaScript and without another approval; redirects are public-address-only and response size is capped at 2 MB. Read only.
GET/api/ai/context/web-searchFor an AI task: calls the selected search provider after task approval; DuckDuckGo is its free official Instant Answer API (not full results), Brave is an API-key search plan. Brave usage is a local estimate and identical results have a brief in-memory cache. No search-result HTML scraping fallback. Read only.
POST/api/ai/context/write-outsideFor an AI task: AMPLE's own pass-through write to a place outside the project; it only works inside a permission the person gave (see access). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/device/cancelStops a device flow that is waiting. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/device/startStarts the Codex device flow for this project (its own Codex home) and returns the address and the code to enter. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/device/statusThe state of the device flow: waiting, linked, failed or cancelled. Read only.
GET/api/ai/grantsThe permissions that last for the project (writing outside it and visible browser access) and the project log. Read only.
POST/api/ai/grants/revokeTakes back a permission that lasts for the project. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/historyThe earlier AI requests of this project (newest first), optionally for one song (song=) or containing a word (query=), so a new request can continue one (continueFrom). Read only.
POST/api/ai/humKeeps a hummed recording (WAV bytes) so that it can be attached to an AI task or message (hums: [id]); the answer holds its id and the melody found in it (tempo, grid, key and bar as for /api/hum/transcribe). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/hum/{id}/audioThe kept hummed recording, to play it again. Read only.
GET/api/ai/modelsThe models Codex offers and the current account's usage limits. Read only.
GET/api/ai/policyWhat this server allows projects to use of Codex. Read only.
POST/api/ai/policyChanges what this server allows projects to use of Codex (capabilities only: they say what a project MAY choose). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/sessionsLists the saved assistant sessions for this project. Read only.
POST/api/ai/sessionsCreates a named assistant session; optional conversation archiving is off by default. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
DELETE/api/ai/sessions/{id}Deletes an assistant session that has no active or unapplied proposal. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
PATCH/api/ai/sessions/{id}Renames a saved assistant session or changes its optional conversation archive. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/settingsChanges the AI settings of the project: the assistant (none, codex-server, codex-device) and the execution mode (manual, auto, unsafe). What the server does not allow cannot be chosen; the first use and the first unsafe use need an acknowledgement. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/statusWhere the AI assistant stands: what the server allows, what the project chose, whether Codex is installed and (with auth=true) whether it is signed in. Read only.
GET/api/ai/tasksThe AI tasks of this project, newest first. Read only.
POST/api/ai/tasksAsks Codex for a proposal: it works in a temporary copy of the files in scope; the project is not changed. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/tasks/{id}One AI task: the log (since=N: only the entries after number N; details=1 adds the input and output of every tool call, which is large), the approvals Codex waits for, and the proposal with its diff, diagnostics and build status. Read only.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/acceptApplies the proposal: a checkpoint first, then the other files; the new text of the song is returned for the editor. Refused when the project changed since the task began, and when it does not build unless anyway is true. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/accept-selectedAccepts selected proposal files without starting another Codex turn. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/accept-selected-continueAccepts selected proposal files after checking them, then continues the same Codex conversation with the remaining proposal. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/answerAnswers an approval request of Codex: accept, acceptForSession, accept30, acceptForProject, decline or cancel. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/archiveArchives the conversation of a task: its Codex session ends and nothing in the project changes. While the working copy and the thread are kept it can be resumed from the Assistant list (see resume in the session list). Stop (interrupt) only stops the turn. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/assistantChanges the model and/or the reasoning effort of a running task (as Codex itself can); the next turn uses them and Codex is told. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/tasks/{id}/audioProposal audio with byte ranges; peaks=N returns a bounded waveform summary instead of audio. Read only.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/buildBuilds the proposal in its temporary project so it can be listened to: the whole song, or with block one block and what it needs. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/cancelStops a task. Nothing in the project changes. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/tasks/{id}/clip/{clip}A clip of sound that Codex presented to the user, to listen to; ?format=wav or ?format=mp3 (encoded by ffmpeg) downloads it as a file. Read only.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/clips/{clipId}/obsoleteMarks one presented sample obsolete with a reason. It stays visible until the user dismisses it. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/compactAsks Codex to compact its conversation now (between turns); the task shows that it is compacting while it happens. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/continueContinues only unfinished work using delivered clips and original quantity limits; rejects duplicate running requests. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/interruptStops the turn Codex is working on and keeps the conversation open: the next message goes on in the same session (unlike cancel, which ends the task). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/tasks/{id}/log/{seq}The input and output of one tool call in the log of a task (the log itself leaves them out because they are large). Read only.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/messageGoes on with a proposal before it is accepted: while Codex works the message steers it, afterwards it asks for a change on top of the proposal as it is now. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/rebaseBrings a proposal up to date with a project that changed in the meantime, where the changes do not overlap. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/rejectThrows the proposal away; the project stays as it is. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/resumeResumes an interrupted or ended assistant conversation; with fresh=true a new Codex session starts in the same working copy and is told what was asked and what is already changed. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/ai/tasks/{id}/textThe proposed text of a file of the proposal (as it would be after Accept). Read only.
POST/api/ai/tasks/{id}/undoPuts back the files (other than the open song) that an accepted proposal changed. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/ai/unlinkRemoves the Codex identity of this project (its login and its Codex home); the Codex of the user is not touched. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/koda/login/cancelStops the device flow of Koda that is waiting. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/koda/login/startStarts the Codex device flow for Koda's own home: an address and a code to enter. The same account as the assistant may be linked a second time. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/koda/statusKoda, the helper: whether Koda has a login of their own (lane own) or shares the lane of the assistant (lane shared), and a device flow that is waiting. Read only.
POST/api/koda/unlinkRemoves Koda's own login; Koda then shares the lane of the assistant. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.

analysis

MethodPathWhat it does
POST/api/audio/transcriptionsRuns a local analysis plugin on bounded WAV audio and keeps its aligned stems and transcription artifacts in the project analysis cache. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/audio/transcriptions/{id}Returns local transcription provenance and URLs for its aligned audio and MIDI artifacts. Read only.
GET/api/audio/transcriptions/{id}/peaksReturns a bounded waveform summary for a 16-bit source or stem WAV. Read only.
GET/api/audio/transcriptions/{id}/{role}Streams one completed local transcription source, stem or MIDI artifact with byte ranges. Read only.

audio

MethodPathWhat it does
POST/api/hum/save-midiWrites the notes found in a hum (notes: start and duration in seconds, pitch, strength) as a .mid file in a folder of the project, at the tempo given; the name is made unique. The answer holds the path. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/hum/transcribeFinds the melody in a hummed or sung line (WAV bytes in the body, 16 bit PCM): the notes, the key and the notes text of a midi-clip, snapped to tempo (default 120), grid (beats, default 0.25), key (auto or like 'A minor') and start bar. An attempt: listen to it and correct it. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.

backup

MethodPathWhat it does
GET/api/backupWhat the project remembers about its backups (target, last backup, age, whether one is made before dangerous acts) and the backups in that target. Read only.
POST/api/backup/createMakes a backup (into the remembered target, or the target given). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/backup/policyChooses the target and whether a backup is made before every dangerous act (takes effect the next time the server starts). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/backup/verifyRehashes a backup (default: the latest in the remembered target). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/exportWrites the project into an archive file (no secrets, a consistent copy of the database). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.

build

MethodPathWhat it does
POST/api/buildBuilds a song (the cache decides what is rendered); progress goes to the event stream. An optional override { block, name, value } builds with that one parameter replaced, without changing the song, and without events (a draft, for listening to an edit before it is applied). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/build/estimateHow big and how long the build of a song would be (an educated guess that learns from earlier builds), and whether it fits on the drive of the takebank. Nothing is rendered or stored. Read only.
GET/api/build/statusWhich blocks of a song already have a take (a dry run of the build: nothing is rendered or stored). A block is cached (with its take), stale (no take yet), waiting (an input has none) or disabled. Read only.
POST/api/build/textBuilds song text that is not a file of the project (the source of a template, to listen to it) as a draft: nothing is changed or announced. only builds up to one block and gives its take. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/sound-checkThe sound of the built takes of a song: silent, very quiet, clipping and unheard blocks, the master loudness and values that are cut, each with a fix when there is one (nothing is rendered). Read only.
POST/api/sound-check/fixPuts the fix of a sound finding into the song: a normalize block (fix normalize) or a volume block with a lower gain (fix volume:-3) after the block; what read the block now reads the effect. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.

components

MethodPathWhat it does
GET/api/componentsThe components a song can see (its own and the imported ones) with every version, its seal and signature, the problems of putting them together, and the .amplec files that can be imported. Read only.
POST/api/components/check-textThe problems of the text of a component file (text): the diagnostics of the parser as the language server gives them (0-based ranges). Nothing is read or written; used while a .amplec file is typed. Read only.
POST/api/components/completeThe suggestions at a place in the text of a component file (text, line and character, 0-based): attributes, statements, types, the words of the ui block, processors after |>. Nothing is read or written; used by Ctrl+Space in the editor of a .amplec file. Read only.
POST/api/components/detachDetaches a sealed embedded component for editing: its seal is removed and it builds as a development version. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/components/embedEmbeds the dependency closure of some instances (blocks), the named components (components) or whole source modules (whole) in the song, inside an embedded module; the song gets the new text back. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/components/embed-previewSays what embedding components in a song would do (path, blocks or components, whole): the closure of definitions that would be written, the ones that are there already and the ones with other code. Read only.
POST/api/components/extractExtracts an embedded component to a new .amplec file of the project (file) and makes the song import it; identity, version and seal are kept. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/components/filesThe .amplec files of the project. Read only.
GET/api/components/graphThe internal graph of an instance of an Audio component (path of the song, block): its processors with parameters and links, the blocks they become, the latency and whether the browser can preview it. Read only.
POST/api/components/graph-valuesThe internal graph of an Audio instance with property values that are not in the song yet (path, block, values: name to text): the same answer as the graph route, for a knob that is being moved. Nothing is written or built; the live preview sets its real-time chain from it. Read only.
POST/api/components/importWhat adding a component file to a song does (path of the song, file, name, add): the import line and optionally an instance, the new text and the conflicts (AMP2212 to AMP2214). Nothing is written; the client applies the text. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/components/libraryThe library of the project (path of the song, refresh=true to read every file again): every component of every .amplec file with friendly name, description, tags, kind, versions and seal, whether the song imports it, and how many files were read now and how many came from the cache. Read only.
POST/api/components/migrateMigrates an instance to a version. A migration with an impact above equivalent is applied only with acknowledge true; the song gets the new text back. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/components/migrate-previewSays what migrating an instance (block) to a version (target: 4.0.0, or id@version for another component) would do: the chain, the impact, the changed properties and ports, the notes before and after. Nothing is changed. Read only.
POST/api/components/new-versionMakes a working copy of a version with a new version number (newVersion), without its seal; the original stays as it is. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/components/sealSeals a version of a component (path of the song or file of the project, name, version): the hashes are written as a seal block. A song gets the new text back (nothing is written); a .amplec file is written through the command bus. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/components/unsealRemoves the seal of a version of a component, so that it can be changed again. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/components/use-templateUses the template source again for an embedded component, only when id, version and payload are exactly the same; otherwise it is refused. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.

control

MethodPathWhat it does
GET/api/control/blockEverything the controls need for one block: freeze level, seed with its history, selected take, variants, the explainer and open regeneration decisions. Read only.
POST/api/control/decideAnswers an open regeneration decision: restore (default) or keep-variant. Replacing needs the two-step act. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/control/regenerateRegenerates a block safely: the selected take stays; a different result becomes an open decision (default: restore). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/control/seedA seed with its lock state and history. Read only.
POST/api/control/seedUnlocks, locks, sets or randomizes a seed (a locked seed refuses changes). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/control/selectSelects a take for a block. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/control/variantsMakes one or more individually indexable takes of a block. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/control/variants/discardDiscards a variant (the take stays in the bank until cleanup). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/control/variants/keepKeeps a variant (it stays selectable). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/control/variants/previewPreviews the deterministic field changes for a variant request without rendering. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/control/verify-reproductionRenders with the reference take's seed and current software/settings, compares output bytes and warns on recipe or version changes. Keeps the reference take selected. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.

documents

MethodPathWhat it does
GET/api/docOpens a song: text, version, diagnostics and blocks. Read only.
PUT/api/docApplies new text to the working copy (not saved) with optimistic concurrency by version. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/doc/bake-clock-asBakes the clock values of the last build of a song (or of one block: block) into a NEW song file of the project and leaves the open song as it is: the open song stays dynamic and can be the seed of several baked songs. An existing name is refused. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/doc/completeCompletions at a position. Read only.
GET/api/doc/diskCompares the working copy of a song with its file on disk. state: same, reloaded or merged (already dealt with), conflict (regions lists the stretches both sides share and the ones to choose from: base, mine, theirs = the file) or gone. Read only.
POST/api/doc/editApplies a graph edit (set parameter, add or remove block, connect, disconnect, rename, flag) as a text edit. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/doc/expandedReturns the module-expanded graph for nested module navigation without changing the open song. Read only.
GET/api/doc/hoverHover text at a position. Read only.
GET/api/doc/inputsThe files each block reads while it builds (sample folders, lyrics, MIDI and audio files, SoundFonts, modules) as one stamp per block, a hash of all of them, and the blocks whose seed follows the master seed. The web UI compares it to know that a build is out of date after such a file changed, although the song text did not. Read only.
POST/api/doc/layoutsSets the place of many blocks in one request (Auto format, align, distribute): items is a list of block, x, y. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/doc/parseParses text that is not open (for example an older state read with peek) and returns the same view as a document, without opening or changing anything. Read only.
POST/api/doc/resolveAnswers a conflict between the working copy and the file on disk: text is the composed result (per region the file's lines, the working copy's, both, or your own), diskSha the one the conflict reported. The file becomes the saved base, the working copy the text; save it as usual. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/doc/revertThrows the changes of the working copy away: the song goes back to the text of the saved file. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/doc/saveWrites the working copy to the file through the command bus (AMPLE Redux keeps the old text). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/doc/save-asWrites the working copy of a song to a new song file of the project (an existing name is refused); the open song stays as it is. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
GET/api/doc/symbolsThe outline of a song. Read only.
GET/api/docsThe song files of the project. Read only.
POST/api/gm/auditionRenders a bounded temporary GM note preview without creating a take; channel -1 auditions all note channels. Read only.
POST/api/midi/clip-notesThe notes a midi-clip block plays (from its chords, melody or notes), written as compact notes text, so the piano roll can make a clip with chords or a melody editable; nothing is changed or built. Read only.
GET/api/midi/downloadRe-encodes a project MIDI source as a downloadable Standard MIDI File while retaining its parsed events. Read only.
GET/api/midi/infoReturns a bounded, payload-free summary of a project MIDI file. Read only.
POST/api/midi/module-downloadExports edited notes from a generated MIDI module and merges them with retained source events. Read only.
GET/api/midi/notesThe paired notes of a project MIDI file (all tracks or one), as ticks of the file, for the read-only piano roll and for making an editable copy; bounded. Read only.
POST/api/midi/uploadValidates and imports bounded MIDI bytes into assets/midi through the project command bus. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/notes/bakeBakes the note pipeline of a midi-clip up to a stage (or detaches it into plain notes) and returns the new text of the song and, for a bake into a file, that file; nothing is written. Read only.
POST/api/notes/duplicateCopies a midi-clip under a new name and lets the copy reuse, fork or leave the stable random namespaces of the original (mode reuse, fork or independent); returns the new text of the song, nothing is written. Read only.
POST/api/notes/editableRewrites one hand-written editable piece of a midi-clip's note pipeline (the roll writes here) and returns the new text of the song; nothing is written. Read only.
POST/api/notes/provenanceWhere the randomness of a midi-clip comes from: every use of a seed with its derived key and the values drawn, its random-streams, and the stable names of the song with their use counts. Read only.
POST/api/notes/random-seedReplaces every random-seed() of the song by a whole number chosen once from OS randomness (so the song stays reproducible) and returns the new text; nothing is written. Read only.
GET/api/templatesThe block templates, port types and classes of the language (the palette is generated from this). Read only.

effects

MethodPathWhat it does
POST/api/effects/impulseReturns the bounded WAV impulse response selected by a convolution block for approximate local preview. Read only.
POST/api/effects/previewApplies a built-in integer effect to a bounded input range without creating a take or changing project state. Read only.

events

MethodPathWhat it does
GET/api/eventsServer-sent events: build.progress, build.done, doc.changed, history.changed, files.changed. Read only.

finals

MethodPathWhat it does
GET/api/finalsThe finals of a song (a song without any has one implicit final, full) and what their last render made. Read only.
POST/api/finalsAdds a final to a song or changes its definition: the first bar, how many bars, a fade in (beats), a fade out (bars) and the format. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/finals/deleteRemoves a final from a song (an exported file stays). Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.
POST/api/finals/renderRenders one final on purpose: the estimate and the disk check, the build, then the kept bars with their fades exported to renders/. Changes state: journaled in AMPLE Redux as a command.

game

MethodPathWhat it does
GET/api/game/manifestThe manifest of a built game score (query id= the score name, variant= optional): tempo, loop, stems with hashes, states, transitions and provenance. Read only.

AMPLE overview

Status (2026-10-11): this is AMPLE's design and knowledge base, not a statement that every described idea is implemented. Each feature page carries its own built/planned status; use the build plan for chunk status. The rationale below is historical. Mock examples and proposed CLI sessions are labelled on their pages.

Origin: two favourite songs, "Always" and "Serendipity", could not be reproduced because their seeds were never stored; AMPLE is built so that this cannot happen again (the "Always rule" in Decisions).

The original goal was a clean, standalone tool (C#) for writing songs as text: instrument tracks (textual MIDI) and AI voices/samples on one timeline, reproducible by default, with a web UI (plain HTML/JS/CSS on a local server, also on Windows). It does not depend on the prompt bridge or prompt-music; those (and the ACE-Step findings in Prompt bridge) are only background knowledge.

Building it: the build plan is in ../plan/ (chunks prefixed with their priority, lowest first). The language specification is in language/ (normative, kept maintained); the generated help.html comes from chunk 12.

Pages

Page What it covers
Decisions What was decided so far, grouped by topic, and what the design is based on. Start here.
Mono and stereo The channels parameter (auto, mono, stereo), the song default on the master block and the stereo meter.
Piano roll Piano-roll tools, gestures, note properties, MIDI expression, accessibility and remaining engine gaps (PR01-PR22).
Project layout (as built) What a project folder contains and how it is protected: .ample/, format versions and upgrades, the one-writer lock, atomic writes, safe paths, and the new/open/doctor commands.
Takebank and plans (as built) Immutable takes and the plans they were made from: the Always rule enforced in the API, the database and the files, canonical plan ids, content-addressed data, attempts, verification, orphans.
Storage: overview, protection and clean-up What the takebank uses, which takes are never removed, the clean-up with dry run, impact and progress, the soft limit and the per-project options.
Finals Several deliverables of one song (full, edit, teaser), each rendered on purpose with an estimate first and exported with its own cut and fades.
Game score Layers and music states of a song as loopable stems plus a manifest, so a game can mix adaptive music live.
Game score: live audio server Design note: what AMPLE would need to produce the game's music live instead of as stems, and what stays stable on the game side.
Score import Turning a MIDI or MusicXML score into a sequence (parts, patterns, playlist, tempo) with ample_import_score.
Access outside the project How the assistant asks to write outside the project (what, why, how long), the pass-through commands, the emergency stop and the project log.
The language server (as built) ample lsp and the /lsp WebSocket: capabilities, transports, measured budgets, decisions and what is not done; the VS Code extension and the generated grammar.
The .ampletx package Portable single-file snapshots of a song (Full, Derived), the manifest, only what the build needs, the read-only viewer and the import.
The AI assistant (Codex) Codex proposes, AMPLE validates, you decide: server policy, project identity and mode, the proposal workspace, MCP context and skill.
AI browser tool Visible Playwright browsing with task/project approval, screenshots, pointer hover, page media mute, aggregate diagnostics and optional page JavaScript.
Saving mode How a coding agent works when asked to conserve usage: concise narration, safe batching of reads and edits, guarded edit scripts, focused verification.
The web UI (as built) What the web app does today (layout, palette, canvas, ports and links, groups, properties, undo, build), what is not yet there, honest differences from the sketch, how to run the browser tests.
Client-side preview analysis Block-by-block feasibility and requirements for browser-local previews, including server dependencies and explicit exclusions.
Extending the Studio UI AMPLE-only guide for new plugins and views, Studio components/tokens, preview honesty, and a quick migration check for concurrent work.
MIDI support Bounded SMF handling, note rendering, generated modules and nested module navigation.
AMPLE Lite The small code-first playground at /lite/: files, editor, demos, build and play, browser-local storage, Reset Lite, the safety boundary and the licences of its sounds.
Local server and API ample serve, the safety rules (loopback, host, origin, token), document concurrency, two-step dangerous acts, events.
Recording your voice The microphone recorder: record locally, listen, trim, set the latency, then upload one take as an import-audio block.
Instance registry Per-user server records, stale detection, protected launch URLs, ping and graceful shutdown.
Opening projects ample open, recent projects, detached server logs and the Windows launcher.
Plugins (as built) The plugin manifest, the JSON-RPC protocol version 1 and what the host guarantees: clean environment, job folder, timeouts, crash containment, one GPU job at a time.
Faer bridge (in progress) Optional per-project routing for ACE song and voice generation, voice cloning and stem separation to the authenticated Trooper.ai service; GPU acceptance checks remain.
Faer deployment notes Verified Trooper.ai setup findings, measured install steps, deployment choices and open validation checks.
FaerSpark The local ACE-Step server on demand: leases, start and stop, the "Faer, else local" route, and the model checks AMP5381, AMP5382 and AMP2014.
Play lights The Blocks view lights up while the song plays: which blocks are audible, where the signal flows, the motion per kind of block, when the lights are allowed.
Templates The Templates tab: the built-in beats with a wizard (preview, kit, chords and bass), suggestions without a model, and your own templates saved per project.
Koda, the small helper The eighth note of the logo as a helper: ask about a block, code or a field (Ctrl+K), answers from the template docs, drafts shown dashed on the board, hide / peek / mute, the two lanes beside the assistant.
ACE-Step model catalog for Codex Live Trooper model inventory shape, ACE model roles, recommendations, quantization trade-offs and exact-file selection rules for Codex.
ACE-Step plugin The plugin for an acestep.cpp server: the assumed server API (unverified), the rules it follows, the stand-in server and the manual test for the real server.
Regeneration safety The warning that AI regeneration is only guaranteed locally, and the safe regen flow: old take set aside, result verified, default "restore previous", crash-safe pending decision.
Determinism The four determinism levels, lock/freeze/pin/refresh, retries and checks, how reproducibility is verified.
Render recipes and reproduction checks The generation-input audit, saved recipes/provenance, CFG baselines and comparison of old takes with current software.
Modules Opt-in modules and plugins, the plugin contract, models, versions.
Bake Turning dynamic results into data blocks; recipe-exact versus data-exact.
Tech C# core, local server and web UI, stable PRNG, toolprints, project folder, build order.
Variants Making many takes of a block, scoring them 0-100, picking and locking one, keeping a shortlist for later.
AMPLE Redux journal The append-only recovery journal, durable AR references, recovery model and retention; the user-facing name is AMPLE Redux.
Controllability What the producer can pin, tweak and expect from an AI block: the freeze ladder (seeds, melody plan, take) and the "if I change X" table, with measured versus expected marked.
Library manager Everything a song uses (catalogs, packs, voices, plugins, templates, data), where it is used, replace with impact analysis, folders, global catalogs as linked folders.
Language support Diagnostics (codes, ranges, hints, quick fixes), the linter and its rules, CLI and language server, a generated language reference that cannot drift.
Source and views One song, three views: node editor, editable arrangement, source editor with validation; Apply versus Save; mock syntax and its checks.

How the blocks make a song

Status (2026-10-02): design sketch from a brainstorm. Nothing here is built; the clickable sketch only simulates it (its preview plays a stand-in synth, but it does follow the chords you type for piano and bass).

1. The idea in one sentence

The graph is a dependency graph of typed values on one shared timeline. A link does not carry sound first; it says "this block needs the result of that block". Building walks the graph from the sources to the master and each block produces its typed output, which is cached by hash.

2. Four kinds of values (the port colours)

Type What flows Example
midi (notes) events with a position on the timeline: bar.beat, length, pitch or chord, velocity chords produces Am F C G, one chord per bar, as note events
text words with timing hints lyrics: each line or word has a target time (bar, seconds, first 5 s checks)
data recorded facts, usually locked weather fetched once, frozen with lock (for example "rainy, 11 degrees")
audio a rendered signal placed on the timeline drum kit output, piano, a vocal take, the mix

3. The shared timeline is what keeps everything in sync

  • There is one tempo map (tempo, time signature, changes) and one bar grid. Bars and beats convert to seconds through that map.
  • Every block that makes something is anchored on the timeline: at bar 9 for 8 bars. The arrangement view shows exactly these anchors; the block graph shows how the blocks depend on each other. Same project, two views of the same text.
  • Notes and drum triggers are exact: they are events at known positions, so two blocks that read the same chords are in sync by construction, to the sample.

4. Walking through the example graph

  1. chords (stable, textual MIDI): Am F C G, 8 bars. Output notes = chord events (bar 1 Am, bar 2 F, ...). This is the harmonic spine.
  2. piano reads notes and plays voicings of each chord with its soundset (a sampler, pinned by hash). Output: audio, exact and repeatable.
  3. bass reads notes too and plays a pattern (for example the root on beats 1 and 3, a fill before a chord change). Same events, same timing, so it locks with the piano.
  4. drums have a trigger input that is optional: by default they play their pattern against the bar grid; connecting chords lets a pattern accent chord changes. Output: audio.
  5. lyrics produce timed words. weather produces data (mood words, tempo hint, season).
  6. chorus_vox (dynamic, an AI voice) takes lyrics, melody (the chords, which give key and progression, and optionally a melody line) and style (the weather data) and builds a recipe for the voice engine: caption/tags, lyrics, tempo, key, length, a seed derived from the master seed and the block name. The engine returns a take (audio) that is stored in the take bank by hash.
  7. mixer sums the audio inputs on the timeline at their anchors with gains and pans. master (EQ, compressor, limiter) shapes the sum; its output is the master audio you play or release.

5. Where "sync" is exact and where it is measured

Part How it syncs Honest note
Piano, bass, drums, any MIDI-driven sampler by construction: events on the shared grid exact, deterministic
Audio imports (a recorded loop) placed on the grid; optionally warped or trimmed with a stated policy exact placement, warping is a choice
AI voice measured, then checked: the take has its own length and timing the model does not obey a bar grid exactly; AMPLE places the take, measures word timing (opt-in plugin), compares with the lyric hints, and reports the error; variants let you pick the take that sits best; policies: warn (default), retry within a budget, pick best, nudge
Harmony between voice and band the voice is conditioned on key, tempo and chord progression following a given melody exactly is not proven yet; chords constrain the style, not every note

6. What a build does

  1. Order the needed blocks (sources first).
  2. For each block compute its cache key from template, version, parameters, node seed, baked flag and the keys of everything upstream. A matching cache means "will only be checked" (greyish green); no match means "must run" (grey).
  3. Run block by block: MIDI and sampler blocks are cheap and exact; dynamic blocks call plugins asynchronously with progress and store takes; each finished block lights up.
  4. Change the chords: the chords block, piano, bass, voice, mixer and master turn grey again, drums and lyrics stay cached.
  5. Preview of any block with an audio output builds what is missing first, then plays that block (for the mixer or master: everything upstream mixed together).

7. Where the song actually lives

The text (.amplet) is the song; the graph and the arrangement are views of it, and visual edits become patches to the text. A tiny excerpt of what the text could look like:

composition "my-song" { ample 1  tempo 92  master-seed 424242 }
midi chords   { chords "Am F C G"  bars 8 }
sampler piano using felt-piano   { from chords.notes }
sampler bass  using analog-808   { from chords.notes  pattern root-1-3 }
sampler drums using kit/tape     { pattern beat-A }
voice chorus_vox using anna      { lyrics chorus  melody chords.notes  style weather  at bar 9 for 8 bars }
mixer mix { drums, bass, piano, chorus_vox  gains 0 0 -2 0 }
master    { limiter -1 dB  target -14 LUFS }

8. What the sketch does and does not do

  • It follows the dependency graph, the cache colours and the progress per block.
  • Its preview sound is a stand-in synthesizer: piano and bass follow the chords you type in the chords block (one chord per bar, major or minor by name), drums play a fixed pattern, the voice is a seeded tone line. It is not the real engine and the voice is not a real take.
  • It does not measure word timing, place takes with warping, or apply the voice-engine recipe; those are designed in Variants, Bake, Modules and Tech.

One song, three views: node editor, arrangement, source

Status (2026-10-02): design sketch from a brainstorm. The syntax below is the MOCK syntax used by the clickable sketch (sketch/index.html); it is not a final language design, but it is real enough that the sketch parses, validates and applies it.

The song is text (song.amplet). The node editor, the arrangement and the source editor are three views of that text. Edit in any of them and the other two follow.

1. The three views

View Good for Writes to the text
Node editor (blocks) structure: what feeds what, parameters, groups, templates blocks, parameters, from ... lines, layout
Arrangement (timeline below) time: where each block sounds the at <bar> for <bars> [as <name>] part of the block header
Source (text) precision, bulk edits, copy and paste, reading everything

2. The arrangement is editable

  • Drag a bar to move it, drag its edges to resize (snaps to whole bars). Several parts per block are allowed (a piano with verse and chorus).
  • Double-click a bar: go to that block's source line. Double-click empty space on a track: a new 4-bar part. Right-click: go to source, select in the node editor, rename the part, duplicate, split, delete.
  • Blocks without a placement can be added with the dropdown above the timeline.
  • An edit changes the text (and the cache keys: a moved block is a changed block, so it and what depends on it turn grey for the next build) and shows the working copy as unsaved.

3. The source view

Switch the canvas area from Blocks to Source.

┌ files ────────────┬ song.amplet                     [Apply] [Revert] [Show block in node editor]   status ┐
│ ✎ song.amplet  ●  │  1  # song.amplet ...                                                                  │
│ ✎ lyrics/chorus   │  2  composition "my-song" { ample 1  tempo 92  master-seed 424242 }                                 │
│ ✎ chords/main     │ ... editor with line numbers; ● error and ▲ warning markers in the gutter              │
│ 🔒 ample.lock      ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                   │ problems: ● line 43: Unknown parameter "patern" for drums. Did you mean "pattern"?     │
└───────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  • Files on the left: song.amplet (the graph), plain text files the blocks refer to (lyrics, chords), and generated read-only files (ample.lock). Only song.amplet changes the node editor.
  • Live validation while typing (a short pause), with a problems list; click a problem to jump to the line.
  • A valid song edit syncs to the working copy (graph, arrangement and other views) after a short pause. Save makes the revision; Ctrl+Enter confirms the current buffer as applied.
  • Revert drops invalid or not-yet-synced edits and returns to the current working copy.
  • While the text cursor is inside a block in a valid song, the Properties panel shows that block. Source and property edits sync both ways; while the code has errors, the properties panel explains that sync is paused until the code is valid again.
  • Show block in the node editor jumps to the block under the cursor (needs a valid song).
  • Leaving the source view (to Blocks or the Branch manager) applies first; if there are errors the switch is refused with a message. A valid song switches back and every other view updates.
  • A project that opens with mistakes starts in the source view and stays there until the errors are fixed (or reverted). In the sketch, open always-remix in the Projects manager to see it.
  • Dirty non-song source files can be closed by saving, keeping a recovery draft, discarding or cancelling. Recovery drafts are offered when each file is next opened; a manual checkpoint saves pending source drafts first and stops if a file changed since its draft was made.
  • When safe saves are enabled, recovery saves in that manual checkpoint batch skip their individual auto-checkpoints; the final manual checkpoint remains the single snapshot for the batch.
  • File writes and recovery records are journaled in AMPLE Redux. Its current on-disk folder remains .ample/blackbox for compatibility; compaction is explicit and uses the project budget.

4. Mock syntax

composition "my-song" { ample 1  tempo 92  master-seed 424242 }
features { quality off  credits off  signing off  secrets on  lyrics on  git-mirror off  assist diff }

drums drums at 1 for 16 as "beat A" {
  kit kit/tape
  pattern beat-A
  bars 16
}
piano piano pinned@2.0 at 1 for 8 as verse, 9 for 8 as chorus {
  set felt-piano
  from chords.notes -> notes
}
ai-voice chorus_vox at 9 for 8 as "chorus voice" {
  voice anna
  from lyrics.words -> lyrics
  from chords.notes -> melody
  from weather.data -> style
}
layout drums 280 20

Header: <block type> <name> <class>@<version> [at <bar> for <bars> [as <name>] (, ...)] [bake] [lock] [refresh] {. Body: <parameter> <value> lines and from <block>.<output> -> <input> lines. Lines starting with # are comments. layout lines (at the end) keep node positions. Names with spaces or odd characters are written in quotes. The inner graph of a group or of a block like the AI voice is edited in the node editor; the text shows a comment line for it.

5. What validation checks

Check Message idea Blocks leaving?
Project line present, tempo 20 to 300, seed an integer "Tempo must be between 20 and 300." yes
Unknown block type, class or version malformed "Unknown block type 'drumz'. Did you mean 'drums'?" yes
Unknown or duplicate parameter "Unknown parameter 'patern' for drums. Did you mean 'pattern'?" yes
Duplicate block names "Two blocks are called 'bass'." yes
from points to a missing block, output or input "There is no block named 'chordz'. Did you mean 'chords'?" yes
Type mismatch between a connected output and input "Type mismatch: x.vocal is audio but y.lyrics wants text." yes
An input with two sources, a block reading itself "Input 'in2' of 'mixer' already has a source." yes
Cycles "Cycle: a → b → a" yes
Unclosed block, bad header, bar numbers below 1 "Block 'x' is not closed (missing '}')." yes
A block needs a plugin that is not installed "Block 'x' needs the plugin 'timing', which is not installed (opt-in)." no (warning)
A part reaches past bar 1024 warning no

6. How Apply maps text to the graph

  • Blocks are matched by name: the same name and type keeps its identity, its inside (groups, templates) and its cache state; a new name creates a block from the template; a block that is gone from the text is removed (the number is reported).
  • Parameters, class, version, parts and flags come from the text; missing parameters get the template default; links are rebuilt from the from lines.
  • Positions come from the layout lines, or a free spot for new blocks.
  • Applying text that equals the current graph changes nothing (cache keys stay equal).

7. Interaction with history

  • Apply and arrangement edits change the working copy; the unsaved badge compares the text with the last saved text. Save makes a revision (and clears the badge). Going to another revision with unsaved work takes an automatic checkpoint first (see History management, "Unsaved work").
  • Errors never reach a revision: a revision is only made from a valid song.

8. Open questions

  1. Should text edits made in another editor (VS Code) while AMPLE is open be picked up (file watcher) and validated the same way?
  2. Should the inner graphs of groups and templates be editable in the same text (nested blocks), or stay node-editor-only?
  3. Should comments and formatting be preserved when the text is regenerated from the graph (a lossless round trip), or is a normalised form acceptable?
  4. Should the source view offer completion and inline docs (block types, ports, parameters) from the templates?

9. Dedicated editors (lyrics)

Some blocks deserve a real editor of their own. The first one in the sketch is the lyrics editor.

  • Open it with the … button next to the file parameter, Edit lyrics in the block menu, the … Edit lyrics button in the properties, or a double-click on the block.
  • It takes over the canvas area (full screen in the editor area) instead of showing the node view. The file the block points to (lyrics/chorus.lyr) is the data: one line per row, [bar 9] text.
  • Rows: bar or seconds (switch above), text, the other unit as a read-only column, move up or down, insert after, delete. A bar can be fractional (9.5).
  • Checks, live: first line within 5 s (the block's first5s setting), lines in order, lines outside the block's placement, empty lines, long lines, too many words for the gap. A timing strip shows where the lines sit inside the placement and colours the problems.
  • Import / export: paste .lrc or .srt (times become bars at the project tempo), export .lrc.
  • Undo and Redo, one step at a time (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y outside text fields; the buttons show how many steps are left) work for edits, moves, inserts, deletes, imports and sorting.
  • Sort by time: a button orders the lines by bar (stable: lines on the same bar keep their order) and is only enabled while the lines are out of order. The check panel offers the same fix next to an order error, and auto-sort on apply (on by default) sorts silently when you press Apply and back.
  • Linking the views: hovering a mark in the timing strip highlights the matching row (and scrolls it into view); hovering a row or a check message highlights its mark in the strip, and editing a row (focusing its bar or text field) keeps its mark highlighted in a stronger colour while you type, so the mark moves live when you change the bar.
  • Two ways back: Apply and back (keeps the changes in the working copy, makes no revision, refused while there are errors) and Undo and back (throws the session's changes away, with a confirmation if anything changed).
  • The same pattern is meant for other blocks later (chords, drum patterns, a mixer, an automation lane): a block can offer a dedicated editor, always with Apply and back / Undo and back.

10. Ctrl+click navigation and read-only

  • Hold Ctrl (Cmd): in the source editor the elements that lead somewhere light up: block names (in headers and in from lines), both ends of a connection, a placement (at ...), a lyrics file, a block type. The cursor becomes a pointer over them and a label says what a click does.
  • Ctrl+click opens the node editor on that element and selects it. On the -> arrow of a from line, it selects and highlights the represented connection, then opens that connection's context menu. A placement also shows the arrangement, a lyrics file opens the lyrics editor, and a type opens its page in the language reference.
  • With errors in the text a popup asks: Fix first (stay, jump to the first error) or Show read-only. Read-only shows the last valid version of the node editor, with the element selected if it exists there ("does not exist in the last valid version" otherwise). A banner says so and offers Back to the editor.
  • Read-only means: no moving, connecting, adding, deleting, grouping, parameter or arrangement edits; selecting, zooming, opening groups and going to the source still work. It stays read-only until you go back to the source editor; entering the source view ends it, and getting back to the node editor then needs a valid song again (or the same popup).
  • The plain Blocks button uses the same popup when the text has errors.

11. The lock file (ample.lock)

ample.lock is generated and read-only. It pins everything the song depends on that is not written in the song text, so the song reproduces later: plugin versions with their toolprints, soundset and sample packs by hash, templates and pinned blocks by hash, locked external data (the recorded weather value, when it was fetched, its hash) and model files. It plays the role of package-lock.json: the text says what you want, the lock says exactly what you got. It is part of every revision, changes only when you update a plugin, a pack or a pin, or lock external data, and verify and upgrade-check compare the present setup with it. See Determinism and Tech.

Recording your voice

The arrangement panel has a Record... button. It opens a small recorder that works on your own computer and only sends something to the AMPLE server when you say so.

Steps

  1. Choose the microphone. The level meter moves when the browser hears sound. The first time, the browser asks for permission; if it was blocked, allow the microphone in the address bar and open the recorder again. The page must be localhost or HTTPS.
  2. Record. Optional: a count-in of four clicks at the tempo of the song, and playing the built song while you sing (put on headphones, or the microphone hears the music). The recording is a raw take: the browser's noise suppression, echo cancellation and automatic gain are off unless you switch them on.
  3. Listen, trim, retake. Every recording is a take in the list. Select one to see its waveform, move the start and end sliders to trim, tick normalise to bring the peak to 90 percent, and press Listen. Nothing has left your browser yet.
  4. Latency. Monitoring through the browser adds a small delay, so a voice recorded to the song lands slightly late. Type the delay in milliseconds, or press Calibrate latency: it plays a click through the speakers and listens for it, so keep the microphone near the speaker. The number is subtracted from the start of the take.
  5. Use in project. The chosen take (with trim, latency and normalise applied) is uploaded as a 16-bit mono WAV into the project folder recordings/ (an existing name gets a new one) and an import-audio block called recording points at it. The upload goes through the normal project upload of the server, so it also works when the server runs on another computer.

After recording

Clean the voice with blocks: a gate removes the noise between phrases, a deesser tames harsh s sounds, then a compressor, eq and reverb. Everything after the upload is ordinary AMPLE, so the take is stored in the project and reproducible.

Limits

  • The count-in clicks are scheduled on the audio clock and the take is cut at the frame of the downbeat (bar 1 of the song), so the count-in is not in the take and the start is exact on the clock of the microphone. The built song is started with a plain play call at that moment (a browser audio element cannot be scheduled), so what is left is the delay between the play call and the sound coming out of your speakers; the latency number (or Calibrate latency, which now measures from the frame the click was scheduled at) covers that.
  • Only one take is uploaded at a time.

Determinism in AMPLE

Status (2026-10-02): design sketch from a brainstorm. Nothing here is built or tested.

Default: strict

require reproducible is on. A build fails if a node is not reproducible and has not been recorded.

Four levels (declared by every plugin)

Level Meaning Examples
exact same input = same bytes on the declared platform rendering notes, mixing, alignment math
machine-exact same on the same machine/build/driver; different elsewhere AI synth on a given GPU
seeded-drift a seed controls it, but it differs per machine the language-model part of the AI
nondeterministic differs every time unseeded or cloud models

Three verbs for anything that is not exact

Word Meaning Reproducible?
lock / freeze record the result and reuse it yes, from the recording
pin vN choose an earlier recording yes
refresh "reason" / allow nondeterministic "reason" every time again, the difference is accepted no: explicit consent, shown in the report

Retries and checks (see examples/05-lyrics)

  • A check has a severity: warn only reports, error fails the node.
  • A retry policy must be explicit and bounded: retry up to N takes until checks pass. Each attempt gets a fixed, derivable seed (name + attempt number), so the sequence of attempts is reproducible; the chosen take is frozen.
  • On failure the policy says what happens (keep best, fail build), never an endless loop.

How it stays true

  • ample verify runs a plugin's self-test twice and compares hashes; a plugin that lies about its level is downgraded.
  • A platform fingerprint (os, gpu, driver, plugin build) is stored with machine-exact results; on another machine AMPLE uses the frozen audio and warns before any re-render that would differ.
  • Seeds per node are derived from the node's name, not its position: adding a section shifts nothing.
  • Internally always lossless (WAV/FLAC, 24-bit); mp3 only on export.
  • Honest limit: bit-exact floating-point results across different CPUs cannot be guaranteed in general; "exact" means "same hash on the declared platform class".
  • What is guaranteed (three layers): (1) a stored take plus the deterministic mix is bit-identical, verified by hash; (2) everything AMPLE renders itself (built-in blocks, mixer, PRNG) is identical on every supported platform, proven by golden hashes; (3) regenerating an AI block is only guaranteed on the same machine and toolprint. For (3) the app shows a permanent warning and runs the safe regeneration flow (old take set aside, result verified, default answer "restore previous"): see Regeneration safety.

Generation recipe audit (2026-10-17)
