The classic command prints the address and a launch address with the session token in the fragment (#token=...), which browsers never send to a server, and opens the browser by default. ample serve remains a foreground command. ample open attaches to or starts a server for a project; the former lock-and-summary operation is available as ample project open. GET /api/ping is an unauthenticated minimal liveness check used by the instance registry; POST /api/server/shutdown requires the session token.

Safety

Rule Code
Listens on 127.0.0.1 only, on a free port unless --port is given.
The Host header must be localhost or 127.0.0.1 (protects against DNS rebinding); --allow-lan lifts this and is for a trusted network only. AMP5282
A request with a foreign Origin is refused (no other site can drive the project). AMP5283
Every /api call except GET /api/ping needs the session token in X-Ample-Token (a cookie works for GET only, for audio elements). AMP5284
Optional sign-in (ample serve --login, off by default): set the user with ample auth set-password --user NAME (only a PBKDF2 hash is stored in the AMPLE user data folder, auth.json); GET /login is the page, POST /api/login {user,password} returns a 12-hour session token that works in X-Ample-Token next to the launch token. 5 wrong attempts lock the caller out for a minute (429). --allow-all (any Host, listens on every address, for a tunnel) is refused without --login. Over plain http the password travels in the clear: use an encrypted tunnel. AMP5297, AMP5298, AMP5299
Build parallelism (ample serve --parallelism N, or AMPLE_PARALLELISM): how many blocks a build renders at the same time. The default is the number of cores of the machine (one block per core), and the limit can be lowered but never raised above the cores. A project can ask for fewer (settings.build.parallelism in project.json; GET/POST /api/project/settings give buildParallelism, parallelismLimit and cores; null follows the server), never for more (AMP5941). It changes how fast a build is, never what it makes; each block still renders on one thread, so a song with one long chain gains little. Lite asks for 2 per build.
JSON request bodies default to 8 MiB; MIDI upload is capped at 64 MiB and audio transcription at 128 MiB plus multipart overhead. Responses are no-store and nosniff.
Every error is RFC 9457 problem details with the AMP code in code.

Documents

A song is edited as a working copy in the server. POST /api/doc/edits applies a list of the same edits (ops) to one version of the text, all of them or none: when one is refused the song stays as it was and the error names the edit, and the whole list is one version step. Besides the edits of /api/doc/edit it knows insertEffect (block, blockType, name, optional parameters: puts an effect after a block, everything that read the block reads the effect, the lines keep their place), bypassEffect (block: takes an effect out, what read it reads what it read, a sidechain key into it goes with it) and copyBlock (block, newName: the block with its parameters, notes, inputs and placement under a new name). These three are also accepted by /api/doc/edit. PUT /api/doc and POST /api/doc/edit carry the version the client saw (baseVersion); a stale version gets 409 (AMP5280) instead of overwriting. setParameter updates or adds a source parameter; removeParameter removes a simple parameter line when a file field is cleared. Before a save the server compares the working copy with the file on disk: an untouched copy takes the new file, changes in different places merge, and a change in the same place refuses the save with 409 AMP5307; GET /api/doc/disk then lists the differences (state, regions with base, mine, theirs, diskSha) and POST /api/doc/resolve takes the composed text. Nothing reaches the file until POST /api/doc/save, which writes through the command bus (AMPLE Redux keeps the old text).

AMPLE Redux

GET /api/redux/records is a read-only, paged journal search for project scope. Filter with ar, task, session, project-relative path, block, field, inclusive UTC from/to, or q. Pages default to 50 and cap at 200; keep the filters unchanged and pass nextCursor back as cursor to continue the same high-water snapshot. Payload and pre-image content are omitted by default; set includePayload=true with one ar reference when the recorded change itself is needed (maximum 2 MB). The search scans newest journal segments first and retains only one segment plus the bounded page in memory. Codex uses the task-authorized GET /api/ai/context/redux-search, which defaults to the current task; scope=session searches the current session and scope=project expands to project history.

Project files

GET /api/project/tree?path=&depth= lists the immediate children of a project folder and can include bounded child folders. GET /api/project/audio?path=... streams supported project audio with byte-range support for the shared player; it refuses non-audio files, private paths and linked files. GET /api/project/hash?path=... streams one project file through SHA-256 and returns its lowercase digest without entering .ample or following links. GET /api/project/peaks?path=... returns a cached, bounded 16-bit WAV waveform summary; GET /api/project/preview?path=... returns capped MIDI-note, song, lyric or file metadata for thumbnails. Both refuse private and linked paths and cap decoded file reads. GET /api/project/usage?path=... parses project songs and modules and reports blocks whose file parameters point at the selected file or a file under the selected folder. POST /api/project/upload?dir=...&name=...&onConflict=... accepts raw bytes or one multipart file, up to the server limit (512 MiB by default; configure ample serve --max-upload-mb <1..512>); multipart forms can provide dir, name and onConflict fields. Imports use the command bus; conflicts can be refused, renamed, overwritten with a recoverable pre-image, or checkpointed before overwrite. POST /api/project/folder creates a folder under an existing parent; POST /api/project/rename and /api/project/move move one file or folder to an unused path under an existing parent. DELETE /api/project/folder?path=... removes an empty folder through the journal; DELETE /api/project/file?path=... removes one project file through the journal. Each mutation publishes files.changed. Private .ample paths are not exposed by the tree, usage or mutation routes.

MIDI

POST /api/midi/upload?extension=.mid&track=all stores bounded SMF bytes under a content-addressed project path and returns its rendered bar count. POST /api/midi/module converts the file (and optional selected track) into an editable generated module. GET /api/midi/info?file=... returns aggregate track, PPQ, tempo and length data. GET /api/midi/download?file=... returns a new .mid by parsing and re-encoding the source event stream; POST /api/midi/module-download exports edited notes from the module's current working copy. Neither download writes to the project.

Audio transcription

GET /api/plugins lists analysis capabilities and declared resource needs. POST /api/audio/transcriptions accepts a WAV, local transcription plugin id, JSON options and an optional job id; network-dependent plugins are refused, GPU plugins require explicit consent, uploads are limited to 128 MiB/10 minutes, and aligned vocal/backing stems plus MIDI artifacts are bounded and validated before the result is marked complete. Pitch metadata is capped at 8 MiB. analysis.progress events carry the job id. GET /api/audio/transcriptions/{id} returns provenance and artifact URLs; GET /api/audio/transcriptions/{id}/{role} streams the source, a stem or MIDI artifact with range support; GET /api/audio/transcriptions/{id}/peaks?role=source&points=N returns the bounded 16-bit WAV waveform summary. Results are private project analysis data under .ample/transcriptions/, not takes.

Dangerous acts are two steps

Dropping a line, the history cleanup, retagging and replacing a take first return a dry run with a one-use token (ten minutes) and the text the user must type. Only POST /api/acts/confirm with the token, the typed text and a reason does it. A confirmation without an open dry run is refused (AMP5281).

Audio and waveforms

GET /api/data/{id} serves stored data with range support; WAV data is audio/wav, so an audio element can stream it. GET /api/takes/{id} carries audioDataId, the data of the take that is WAV audio (the role is the name of the output port, so it is found by content). GET /api/takes/{id}/peaks?points=N (16 to 4000, default 800) returns { rate, channels, seconds, points, rms, peak, peaks } where peaks is points min and max pairs ([min0, max0, min1, max1, ...], values from -1 to 1) over the whole take; it is computed in one streaming pass (a ten-minute take is never held in memory) and cached. Only 16-bit WAV can be summarised.

POST /api/project/upload?dir=...&name=...&onConflict=... imports supported files through the command bus (512 MiB default maximum, adjustable with ample serve --max-upload-mb <1..512>); conflict choices are refuse (default), rename, overwrite and overwrite-record. GET /api/project/tree?path=...&depth=... lists a project folder and immediate children without following links or entering .ample. POST /api/effects/preview accepts a song path, effect block, its selected upstream take, parameters and a range of at most 30 seconds; it returns WAV from the built-in integer renderer without recording a take or journal entry. Preview output is kept only in a bounded process-local cache.

History and control views

GET /api/history/graph (every revision of every line with its parent, the lines, tags and current line; each node's reduxRef is the compact AR reference of its exact durable history command, or null), GET /api/history/diff?from&to, GET /api/history/peek?ref (the files of a state as text; changes nothing), POST /api/doc/parse (parses text that is not open, for a state that is only looked at) and GET /api/control/block?path&block (freeze level, seeds with their history, selected take, variants, supported and unsupported variant fields, the explainer, open regeneration decisions). POST /api/control/variants/preview returns deterministic per-take field changes without rendering; POST /api/control/variants accepts selected field names and renders temporary values into immutable take plans. count may be 1–20, optional startIndex selects a deterministic segment of the same proposal sequence, and optional baseVersion prevents a multi-request batch from continuing after its song changes. The Studio requests one take at a time and aborts the active request on cancellation. Seeds are 64-bit numbers and travel as strings.

GET /api/redux/records provides bounded, read-only journal search with cursor paging; GET /api/redux/status returns aggregate storage and budget status; GET /api/redux/compact-preview previews exact compaction impact; POST /api/redux/compact performs the separately confirmed compaction.

Library

GET /api/library (linked folders with their live state, assets, duplicates), POST /api/library/mounts (link and scan), /scan, /relocate, /access (read-only or read-write), /import (copy into the project), GET /api/library/uses?path (where the song uses assets), GET /api/lock and POST /api/lock/update, and the two-step act /api/acts/unlink-mount. The home folder of the library is ServerOptions.LibraryHome (default: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data of the user).

Storage and build estimates

GET /api/storage returns takebank usage, protection/reclaimable totals, storage options and cleanup state. POST /api/storage/plan creates a dry-run plan; POST /api/storage/clean starts it only if its fingerprint still matches. GET /api/storage/status and POST /api/storage/cancel inspect or cancel cleanup. POST /api/storage/compress, /api/storage/move and /api/storage/settings manage lossless compression, takebank relocation and project storage options. Cleanup and compression progress use storage.progress and storage.done events.

GET /api/build/estimate?path=... performs a plan-only estimate for the song and reports rendered block count, estimated bytes/time and whether the takebank drive has room. It does not render or store data. Builds under 50 MiB skip the space refusal; other estimates require 120% of estimated bytes free. Build statistics are learned per project in .ample/analysis/build-stats.json.

Finals

GET /api/finals?song=... lists defined finals and the implicit full final when none are defined. POST /api/finals adds or updates a definition; POST /api/finals/delete removes one; POST /api/finals/render deliberately builds, cuts and exports one final after estimate and disk preflight. Finals are project metadata, stored in .ample/finals.json, and are not song-language syntax.

GET /api/game/score?score=... describes a game score (default game/score.json): the checked definition in short, its problems and which builds exist. POST /api/game/score/build builds the song (or one variant), cuts the loopable stems and writes them with the manifest to renders/game/ (estimate and disk check first, one build at a time; a rebuild with the same takes writes nothing). GET /api/game/manifest?id=...&variant=... returns a built manifest, GET /api/game/stems/{file} a stem, stinger or manifest file (WAV with range requests). POST /api/game/state is how a game reports a change of music state (kept in memory, published as the event game.state, never changes the project); GET /api/game/state lists the latest reports. POST /api/game/variant builds a variant in the background and answers with the events game.score.ready or game.variant.failed. See game-score.md.

Assistant context

The /api/ai/context/* routes provide scoped read-only context (project, song, block, files, history, docs and analysis), structured proposal edits, score import, task memory and project-log access. GET /api/ai/context/access requests permission to write outside the project; POST /api/ai/context/write-outside and /api/ai/context/findings are the mediated write paths. These routes are task-context scoped and do not replace the proposal/accept flow under /api/ai/tasks.

Backup

GET /api/backup (what the project remembers and the backups in that target), POST /api/backup/create, /verify, /policy (target and backup before every dangerous act), POST /api/export (archive file), and the two-step acts /api/acts/prune-backups and /api/acts/restore-in-place. GET /api/health carries the last backup.

Events

GET /api/events is a server-sent event stream: build.progress, build.done, doc.changed, history.changed.

Not yet

The library routes are a placeholder until chunk 85. The API is version 0.1 and may still change until the UI has used it.

The web UI (as built)

Status: the shell, canvas, ports and links, palette, groups and block properties; history, branches, compare, variants, seeds, the freeze ladder, playback and the arrangement; and the editors and managers are built. The Studio UI track adds the advanced dark Studio skin and controls while preserving the current app's complete feature inventory.

Opening a song resets the Source editor's file binding and reloads it when visible; a hidden Source editor follows the active song when reopened. Song switching asks before discarding unapplied source text. The editor file picker and project browser share this guard (2026-10-10; browser acceptance pending). The last opened song is kept in the user's recent-project record, so F5 and a server restart reopen it even if the port changes. If that song was removed, Studio opens the first available song.

Block playback shows a pending loading indicator; click again or use Stop to cancel. Only the latest playback request may start after asynchronous loading/output initialization. Audio metadata loading times out after 15 seconds. The browser retains its token in tab session storage across F5. Media/event cookies are named per server port and token generation, so an old tab cannot overwrite a newer tab's cookie after restart. A genuinely stale session token still requires opening the new launch tab; authentication is not weakened (2026-10-10; runtime/browser acceptance pending).

The Assistant bottom panel uses its available height: heading/actions/search stay fixed and only the conversation list scrolls. In the AI task dialog, excess wheel movement at the Activity log or sample-list boundary scrolls the outer content. Its message composer places attachments above a full-width field, grows to three lines and then scrolls; Enter inserts a line break and Ctrl+Enter or Alt+Enter sends. When reviewing a completed proposal, Codex's written summary appears beneath the fixed tab row in Output, Changes and Checks; newest presented audio samples appear first (2026-10-16).

Folder tree expansion uses an open/closed folder icon in place of the arrow. The size slider changes between details and tiles directly, without a resistance zone. Audio waveforms carry an invisible accessible range input for direct mouse/touch scrubbing and keyboard arrow seeking. Playing detail rows expand their name cell to show a waveform and collapse on Stop or natural end. Tile width presets start at 240px and reach 540px; the default is 360px, constrained by available panel width. WAV peaks are supported; other audio formats retain the placeholder when server peaks are unavailable. These follow-up changes are source/syntax checked; browser/audio acceptance is pending (2026-10-10).

Project browser tiles are wide cards suited to audio names. Folder and file-type SVG icons appear in the tree, detailed list, tiles and picker. Audio tiles lazily load waveform peaks, with a patterned placeholder when unavailable. Hover or keyboard focus exposes Play/Stop, Loop and a seek slider; touch devices always show them. Preview uses the shared player and local playback volume, starts only on Play, and stops on card leave, folder/view/filter changes, bottom-tab navigation, dragging, page hiding or window blur. Scrubbing keeps playback alive during the pointer drag. Browser/audio acceptance remains pending (2026-10-10).

Block status and local listening volume (2026-10-10)

The right title-bar dot is now a status control. Red ! identifies a source/build error; amber ! identifies a block skipped by an upstream error; blue pulses while building; filled green means newly rendered in the last build involving that block; outlined green means an existing take was reused. Grey means not built/out of date, with a dash when disabled. Status tooltips include the available error or build time. Clicking an error opens Log, selects Song log or Build log, follows upstream failure messages and scrolls/focuses the corresponding error row. Completed build/cache badges no longer occupy the block body; current step and detailed progress remain visible during a build, then disappear for each block as its result arrives. Semantic flags such as dynamic/baked remain separate.

Ordinary Play/Stop actions use icons; Build and play/Cancel build retain their explanatory labels. The small arrow beside Play opens Loop, whose toggle keeps the menu open. The volume icon opens a vertical 0–150% fader with a reset to 100%; moving away from baseline gives the icon an amber tint and a tooltip explicitly distinguishing listening volume from master volume. It is held in this tab's memory, resets on reload, and is never written into song settings, output files or render plans. Shared playback, proposal audio, loop playback, file/clip previews, A/B, transcription stems, recording auditions and live MIDI previews use the local gain. Shared source meters remain before this gain. Values above 100% amplify playback and can clip at the device; they do not modify the rendered waveform.

The default studio-dark theme is token-driven by web/styles/tokens.css. Shared element treatment lives in skin.css; Studio panels build on studio.css. Available themes are studio-dark, light, high-contrast, auto and classic; the selection is remembered in the browser. Custom graph and waveform drawing reads the same CSS tokens.

ample serve serves the web app at /. It looks like the clickable sketch on purpose: the sketch's CSS is the app's CSS, and the same regions, buttons and behaviours are used. What is real here that was a mock there: every change goes to the server as an edit of the song text, so the graph and the source are always the same document, and the history, the takes, the seeds and the audio are the real ones.

What works

Project exports (2026-10-10)

Right-click a project file and choose Export to download its original saved bytes. Audio files additionally offer Export as → WAV / MP3 / FLAC. Folder menus omit ordinary Export and expose only Export as → ZIP. ZIP includes nested files and empty directories without following links or entering private .ample directories. Project sources are never overwritten.

Converted and ZIP exports run as temporary jobs. The progress dialog shows the current step, elapsed time, and either compressed source bytes/files or converted audio seconds/output bytes. ZIP has a byte-based progress bar after file discovery; audio conversion uses an indeterminate bar with live timing/size updates rather than guessing a percentage. Cancel export stops compression or terminates only the job's own ffmpeg process and discards its temporary output. A completed job starts a browser download and offers Download again for 30 minutes. Conversion requires ffmpeg on PATH or AMPLE_FFMPEG; a missing encoder is reported in the dialog. WAV conversion uses 24-bit PCM; FLAC is lossless, MP3 uses ffmpeg's MP3 encoder. Export reads the saved project file, not unsaved source-editor text. The source editor supports Ctrl+mouse-wheel font scaling from 8 to 24 px; the browser page does not zoom while the pointer is over the editor, and aligned gutters and diagnostic overlays follow the same size. Ctrl+Space and inline completion offer sequencer channel keys such as pan, filter project audio samples by the text typed after sample=, and complete project file or sample-folder parameters by substring within the file types accepted by their block. GM SoundFont fields also complete pack: with the MuseScore General alias.

Area Behaviour
Layout Library left, canvas, properties right, tabbed panel below. Each panel can be hidden; the bottom panel and the side panels resize; the layout is remembered in the browser.
Component layout A component with a ui block draws its own controls: knobs, sliders, switches, choices, an xy pad, readouts and meters in rows and groups, in the properties panel (all of it), on the board card (the card block; a knob on the card never moves the block) and in a window (⤢). Dragging only previews; releasing writes one step. A component that says preview live has a Live switch: the sound that feeds the block loops through a real-time chain and changes while a knob moves (approximate, nothing is built or written; the build is the truth). A double click on a knob opens a field to type the value (Enter applies, Esc cancels); Alt+click gives the default back.
Component library The fourth tab of the left panel lists every component of every .amplec file of the project (GET /api/components/library), also the ones the open song does not import: a row per component with a kind icon (♪ notes, ∿ audio), the friendly name, a ✓ when the song imports it and a ⚠ when its name is taken by other code. The details (full name, version, seal, processors, description, tags) are in the tooltip; the description and the #tags (#[Tags("echo", "space")]) show under the selected row, and a tag chip filters. / puts the cursor in the quick search (name, #tag, description, file; every word must match), the arrows choose, Enter adds, Esc clears. ＋ imports and adds a block, ⤓ only imports, </> shows the file; an entry can also be dragged onto the board (a component the song imports becomes a block at once; one it does not import is imported first, the lines shown, then the block stands where you dropped it); the lines that will be written are shown first, and a taken name offers import "file" as alias. The list is cached per file and read again only when a file (or a file it imports) changes; ⟳ reads everything again.
Palette Generated from spec/templates (GET /api/templates): categories, class and version badges, search, drag onto the canvas or double-click, right-click for template info.
Canvas Wheel zoom about the pointer, background drag pans, Fit, 1:1, minimap (click or drag to move the view), click, Ctrl or Shift click and Shift-drag rectangle select, Ctrl+A. Blocks snap to a 10 unit grid; cards start at a readable width and expand up to 680 px to fit longer titles and port labels. Automatic columns size themselves to their widest card, with node-height-based row spacing. Opening a song automatically runs Fit after its graph is loaded and the canvas is visible, so all blocks start in view. Fit explicitly shows the entire graph. Double-click a block title to rename it inline; collisions receive the next free suffix. The arrow beside type and version opens that block's Studio GUI, or selects its properties when it has no dedicated GUI. Audio sources list connected effects in signal order, including disabled effects shown dimly; choosing one focuses its block and properties. The right-click menu groups Add, Build & export, Layout, Edit, block-specific tools, AI and Remove; pinning and Auto format are under Layout, as is Fit in the canvas menu. Add divides effects into EQ & filters, Dynamics, Space, Modulation, Levels & stereo, Timing & transforms and Other submenus; effect bypass is under Edit. The source icon remains at the toolbar's right edge. A dim pin beside the block name becomes bright when pinned. The source block's Properties Advanced dialog can add, remove, reorder or bypass effects while preserving the downstream route as one undoable graph edit. Keyboard: Tab between blocks, arrows move, Enter shows the source, Delete, Ctrl+Z/Y/A/G.
Ports and links Drag from an output dot. Compatible inputs light up and the others dim while dragging; an incompatible drop shows a message and changes nothing. Connect and disconnect are edits (from lines).
Auto format Right-click, Layout, Auto format arranges the selected blocks by the way the signal flows. Pressing it again on blocks that are still where it put them (so it would do nothing) tries the next layout: top to bottom, then in rows (a long chain folds into bands), then left to right again.
Moving Moving blocks writes layout name x y lines. Blocks that never moved are placed by an automatic layout.
Groups Select blocks, Ctrl+G; links that cross the border become the group's ports; double-click opens it, Ctrl+Shift+G ungroups.
Project files File parameters have an editable project path, picker, Open and Clear actions. Open routes audio into shared playback, MIDI into bounded details and its linked block, lyrics into the linked lyrics editor, text into Source, and unknown types to their Project location. Clearing removes the parameter line in one versioned edit. Project audio streams with range requests.
MIDI modules Project MIDI files can be imported as MIDI blocks, inspected using bounded metadata and converted in place or into a new song through a generated module. Generated clips, instruments and mixers remain editable in the nested node view; per-track event nodes expose every retained event in paged, filterable properties with bounded payload previews, while the banner flags only remaining source-level features. General MIDI instrument properties can preview a test note or up to 128 routed track notes, including the all-channel setting. A/B comparison reports note/timing/velocity differences and switches audio at the matching relative position.
Audio transcription review Choose a local analysis plugin and WAV, then review source/vocal/backing stems on a shared scrub timeline and inspect the plugin's confidence-bearing vocal pitch lane. Correct the derived note estimates, download them as MIDI or import them as a MIDI block. Results stay in the project's private .ample/transcriptions/ folder. No separation model is bundled.
Properties The block heading has a source button beside its title and the Advanced GUI button at the far right when available. Rename, template parameters (showing template defaults until overridden in the source), lock, bake, refresh and disabled state, ports, notes. The Info tab repeats the template's read-only description as a tip. Long text uses the template-declared expanded editor. Several blocks: group, align, distribute, delete. For a dynamic block also the seeds and the controls (below).
Build and players The Build button builds the song; each block shows built, cache hit, failed or skipped. The Build log lists new entries first with timestamps and elapsed time, retains entries for the session, and can be cleared or exported as .txt. Audio blocks get a ▶ with a progress bar after a build.
History The History tab has Project history (every revision of every line, graph or newest-first list, tags, details, checkpoint, fork, promote and cleanup) and Edit history (undo / redo) (the open song or nested module's undo states, current working state and redo states). Select a step to preview it read-only, return to the live buffer unchanged, or restore it as one new undoable edit. Double-click asks before restoring; Ctrl-double-click restores directly. A compact AR reference appears only when the exact file text hash matches a durable saved pre-image in AMPLE Redux.
Look only "Look only" reads another state without changing anything on the server: the song of that state is shown read-only under a banner; building, saving and editing are off. Leaving restores the exact local working document and view, including unsaved edits.
Branches The Branches tab lays one line out left to right: the path from the root line to the focused one, its direct leaves, dots for revisions. Right-clicking a branch card offers go, look, compare, fork, tag, fold, and drop or restore as applicable. The Structure tab lists the lines and tags plus a searchable block list (name, type or class).
Compare Compare... opens a wide, scrollable diff of two states (lines, tags, revisions), with both revision selectors visible even for long titles, expandable files, added and removed lines, line numbers and surrounding context. Opening an older revision from History keeps it selected even outside the twenty recent choices. A final newline is a line terminator, not an extra blank line; missing final newlines are marked. In the variants view, two takes can be compared A/B with synchronised playback and a loudness-matched switch.
Variants Choose output-affecting numeric, fixed-choice and seed fields, preview each deterministic before/after value, then make 2, 4, 8 or 20 takes. Each card shows the fields recorded in its immutable render plan, waveform, ▶, your score (0-100) and flag, keep, discard and pick. Temporary field values never edit the song source.
Seeds Locked by default. Unlocking says what it breaks at the current freeze level; typing a seed or randomizing is journaled and kept in the seed history. Seeds are 64-bit numbers and are shown exactly.
Controls The freeze ladder (free, seeds, melody plan, take) writes freeze and bake into the source; the table lists what each kind of change does at that level (from the server's rules); Regenerate is safe: warning first, the old take stays, and a different result asks what to do (default: restore the previous take).
Playback A ▶ on every built audio block, each block's cached waveform with click/drag seeking, the built song waveform, a loop switch and one lit global stop control beside Preview song. Preview song builds what is missing and plays the song; dragging over the ruler chooses bars and previews just those. Audio streams with range requests; waveforms use GET /api/takes/{id}/peaks.
Playlist (beta, behind Playlist view (beta) in the ? menu (on a narrow screen, the More menu)) The same song as lines: a line is a chain from its sources to its bus. Clips, sections, groups, the tail and the master, a routing gutter with cables, lanes (automation curves, drum patterns and sequencer clips that can be edited in place, control blocks), a graph of the picked line, modules that open from their row, mute and solo as preview. Derived by web/lib/playlist-model.mjs; every edit is a command of the other views (web/app/playlist-actions.js), several steps as one list (POST /api/doc/edits). See the guide page "The Playlist". Not in Lite or Remix.
Arrangement Lanes generated from the blocks and their parts (at N for M as name), ruler in bars and seconds, zoom; the labels stay fixed at the left while the timeline scrolls horizontally, and the waveform and ruler keep their own rows when scrolling vertically. The bottom panel batches height changes while its grip is dragged. Drag clips to move or resize, double-click or right-click to set exact timing, and trim a configured bars scope when shortening. Edits use a versioned source operation and one undo step.
Assistant and log The bottom Assistant tab manages searchable, compact project-local Codex sessions, opens the latest request, and folds earlier requests into each session; threads resume after restart, and selected checked changes can be accepted while continuing the same conversation. The full existing prompt and proposal interface is shared with other entry points; Source remains in the top view switch. The Log panel separates Build log, Project log and Song log; Song log lists current compiler errors and warnings, removes them when resolved, and opens their source location on double-click.
Undo Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y and Ctrl+Shift+Z step through edit operations; one gesture is one step. The Edit history view lays out undo states, the current work and redo states in order, with read-only preview, return-to-current and explicit restore. Redux badges are looked up by hash across the file's paged durable journal records; transient states remain unbadged.
Errors A song with errors is read-only (banner); current compiler errors and warnings are listed in Song log, and double-click opens the source location.
Keyboard Space plays and stops, Ctrl+B builds, Ctrl+S saves, Ctrl+Z undoes and Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes, Ctrl+Enter applies the source editor, Ctrl+P opens the source file switcher, F2 renames the selected file, Tab accepts ghost text in the editor. On the canvas: F fits the view, Ctrl+A selects all, Ctrl+G groups, Ctrl+Shift+G ungroups, Ctrl+Delete deletes and disconnects, Backspace or Delete removes the selection only while the canvas has focus (a toast tells how to undo). In the project panel: Alt+Up goes up one folder. Shortcuts outside text fields only; every action with a shortcut shows it in its tooltip as "Name (Ctrl+X)".

Effect properties and numeric input

Numeric fields keep typing and arrow-key editing; focusing a ranged field opens a small floating slider that closes on blur or Escape. Block properties use remembered, keyboard-navigable tabs. The six audio effects have compact cards with bypass, their existing template parameters and visual summaries; ▶ builds that block and plays its resulting take.

The Studio Advanced dialog uses the same journaled edit path. Its buttons in the canvas and block properties both recognize connected audio: they offer to build the upstream input until a take is available, then allow playback. EQ and filter show estimated frequency-response plots; the compressor transfer curve follows the integer engine's steady-state linear-amplitude law, while bounded waveform and gain-reduction analysis comes from its exact render; duck edits a 16-step pattern; distortion, delay and reverb show parameter-driven plots; mixer has four gain and pan strips. Other plots are guidance, not measurements of the integer engine. With a built upstream audio take, Local preview decodes a bounded 30-second bypass render (fetched and decoded once per take, then reused across control edits) and applies Web Audio graphs for EQ, filter, compressor, duck, distortion, delay, reverb, chorus and convolution; it is labeled approximate and updates after control edits. Chorus previews a triangle-LFO-modulated delay line (fixed 20 ms base delay, depth/period/mix matching the template) so the effect is audible, not just the dry input. Convolution uses the selected project or pack impulse response, with live mix, level, predelay, length and normalization; changing the IR replaces only the impulse response while the input and playback position continue. Hear the real thing uses the renderer for the exact effect preview. The server preview is bounded and cached in process memory, and never creates a take or changes project history. A playback analyser drives the Studio output meter when Web Audio is available; the shared waveform scrubber supports seeking and loop regions.

The denoise panel's Preview runs a bounded spectral denoise approximation in a browser worker, so audio playback stays responsive without waiting for a server render. It uses the selected noise profile and current reduction/sensitivity controls; Compare / render still offers the exact AMPLE effect preview. The bypass audio for the worker is fetched once per take and reused for every slider change (it never depends on this block's own parameters), and the preview position is read again right before the filtered audio swaps in, so a control edit no longer re-fetches over the network or jumps the playback position backward. The panel's Optimize: auto / speed / memory group is shown apart from the sound controls: it is an execution-policy parameter (affectsOutput: false in the template), so every choice renders the exact same cleaned audio and only trades the server render's time against its memory use on a long sound.

The Project bottom panel shows the project tree/list with search, filters and view choices. The view mode, tile size, sort and detail-column layout are saved in the shared project settings; the current folder and tree width remain remembered per project in this browser. The detailed list includes lazy Used by and SHA-256 columns. Tile cards and the picker show lazy WAV waveforms, MIDI note-roll summaries, song tempo/block counts and lyric excerpts using bounded cached project-preview routes. Project and picker OS file drops share the duplicate dialog, including Keep both and Apply to all. The file picker reuses the project tree, reveals nested preselected paths, shows file references, accepts uploads with per-file byte progress and offers all four conflict choices with Apply to all, creates folders, and has context actions for rename/move and deletion (folders must be empty). Lists above 2000 entries render a fixed-height virtual window. Tree rows support arrow-key navigation, Left/Right expansion, double-click expansion, / search and Backspace to move up; file fields can clear their path and sampleset fields select folders. Internal project-file drags carry relative paths; OS file drops use the upload flow.

Not yet (and where it comes)

For new plugins/views and a quick check on whether existing AMPLE work needs to migrate, see Extending the Studio UI. The complete, interactive AMPLE app mockup is maintained in the Studio plan. The full mockup must preserve every capability in the real AMPLE UI, even when the redesign moves actions into compact controls; maintain the current-app parity inventory and mockup findings in the Studio UI plan's mockup/NOTES.md. The source editor, lyrics editor, plugin settings, library, projects, branch manager, export and the settings in the properties panel are built, as is the language server in the editor. Planned: studio effect panels with preview, a file picker for every file field and a Unity-like Project panel. Planned: a launcher track (instance registry, ample open, a tray hub and project picker for Windows, a user-level asset home).

Honest differences from the sketch

  • Groups live in the view, not in the song file. The language has no inner graphs yet, so a group is stored in this browser per project. The source is never changed by grouping.
  • Notes, scores and flags are also kept in the browser.
  • There is no cache probe before a build, so blocks show "not built" until a build has run (the build itself uses the cache).
  • Undo restores the song text before the gesture; it does not undo view changes.
  • "Controls" shows the rules of the server (what is ignored, what breaks reproduction) instead of the sketch's expected melody/words/sound table, which was an expectation and not a measurement.
  • Playback uses an audio element streaming from the server, not Web Audio: it never holds a whole take in memory, but it is not sample-accurate (the A/B players stay within 0.1 s of each other in the tests).
  • Arrangement sections (web/app/view-sections.js, rules in web/lib/view-sections.mjs) are bands at the bottom of the ruler, read from and written to the section lines of the song's view block (saveSections in store.js, one undo step). A change of only the view block does not stop a running build.
  • Arrangement gestures edit the source placement; the text remains authoritative. Other waveform/clip-content editing remains in the source and the relevant block editor.
  • History: going to a revision that is not the tip of a line forks a line there first (the server only moves between lines).
  • The history graph has no named checkpoints separate from revisions: a checkpoint is a revision of kind "checkpoint" with your name as its message.

Files: the project panel, drag and drop, the switcher and the save menu (2026-10-08)

The project panel is the home of file management. Right-click on a folder, on an empty spot or on the + button: Add › creates a song, timed lyrics (lyrics/*.lrc), chords (chords/*.chordpro), an empty MIDI clip (assets/midi/*.mid), a module, a sample folder, a text note or a folder, each with a valid skeleton, through the same code as ample add <kind> <name>; a new file opens in the editor that fits. Right-click on a file: Use in song › adds a block that reads it (the block types come from the accept lists of the templates), Point a block at it › changes the file parameter of a block that exists, Open as text, Show where used, Rename, Move, Delete.

The Project tab starts at the selected project root, with its files listed. Folder rows in the tree can be dragged into another folder; the move uses the same reference preview as the Move command and refuses moves into the source folder or its descendants.

In the file view, files are always listed before folders. The active sort column and direction are applied separately within each of those two groups, in tile and detail views.

With no block selected, the properties panel shows Song properties. Its Seed override is blank when the song follows the project master seed; entering a seed overrides it for that song, and clearing the field restores the project seed.

Rename and move are a refactor. The panel first lists every line of the songs and modules that names the path (also inside a voice map) and what it becomes; Move applies it, one journaled step. A song with unsaved changes stops the refactor until it is saved or reverted. Advanced › has Rename without refactor and Move without refactor: only the file moves and references may break. On the command line: ample mv <from> <to> [--no-refactor] [--dry-run].

Drag and drop. A file dragged from the panel (or from the operating system, which uploads it into assets/<kind> first) lights up where it can go: in the source editor the lines that take it (outlined) and the places between blocks (a line), the nearest one marked; a drop fills the path (a different existing path asks first, Alt replaces) or adds a block; one Ctrl+Z takes it back. Insert file… in the editor bar does the same from the keyboard. File fields in the properties and the studio panels light up and take the drop; a node that reads that kind of file takes it on its file parameter; an empty canvas makes a block. The targets come from the accept lists of the template parameters and from web/lib/file-kinds.mjs (extensions to kinds); the edit a drop makes is web/lib/drop-targets.mjs.

The file switcher. There is no list of files next to the source editor any more (removed 2026-10-21): open a file with the search box above the text (Ctrl+P), with Recent ▾, or from the Project panel at the bottom. The Recent ▾ dropdown is visible beside the project name at the top-left of the canvas and in the Source header. It shows the current song and source file under Open now, then recently opened songs and editable text files; a dot marks a file with unsaved or recoverable changes. The full-screen recovery diff lists pending source drafts and song/module undo buffers. For each other buffer, choose to restore it when opened, use its saved version or decide later. Choosing a recent file uses the normal switch flow, including its unsaved-change or recovery prompt. The quick switcher above the text still supports Ctrl+P or click, typing a few letters, arrows and Enter; with no query, recent files come first.

Moving and hidden names. Drag a file or folder onto a folder (a tile, a row or a folder in the tree) to move it into it, or onto the path at the top of the panel to move it out of the folder you are in. It asks first, listing the lines in songs and modules that follow the move (the same as Move…). Names that start with a dot, such as .git, are left out of the panel, the tree and the file picker unless the Hidden chip is on. New folders come from the + menu (New folder…) and from Add → Folder.

Uploading audio. An uploaded MP3, Ogg or FLAC file also gets a WAV next to it (song.mp3 gives song.wav; a name that exists gets -2), made by ffmpeg at the same sample rate as 16-bit PCM, because blocks play WAV files. A toast names the new file. FLAC is lossless; an MP3 or Ogg decodes to exactly what it sounds like, which means nothing is lost on top, but nothing that the encoder dropped comes back. Without ffmpeg the upload still works and the toast says the conversion was skipped (AMPLE_FFMPEG sets the path).

Changes and saving. The same control sits in the source editor, the lyrics editor, the piano roll and (as the menu only) next to Save at the top: a dot says typing, not applied (text in the source editor that is not applied), changed (the working copy differs from the saved file) or nothing (saved), the disk icon saves (Ctrl+S works everywhere; the editor applies what was typed first) and ▾ opens Save as… (a copy as a new song), Revert changes, Export…, Render block to file… (the take of the selected block as WAV or MP3 in a project folder, renders/ by default), Show in the project panel and Copy path. The Source file list and quick switcher include only songs and editable text files, not audio assets; following an audio-file link selects the block that uses it instead.

Patterns and sections (2026-10-08)

The step grid of a drums or guitar block has a pattern chooser (the main pattern, the named ones, New, Duplicate, Rename, Delete) and a section strip under it: one chip per section with its pattern, its bars (− and +), arrows to move it, a cross to remove it, and drag and drop to reorder; + section adds one. Everything writes the patterns and song parameters of the block (see Samples). The Patterns view (the Patterns view button in the panel, or the block menu) opens the same grid, chooser and strip full width, with the voice map below it for the samples of the lanes; an audio file dragged from the project panel onto a lane gives that voice the sample. The FL Studio-like workspace is the advanced sequencer block: Sequencer.

Build, play and stop (2026-10-08)

The header has three controls. Build builds what is out of date (also unsaved changes; blocks that did not change are not rendered again) and does not play. Play plays the built song; when something is out of date, or nothing is built yet, it says Build and play, lists what is out of date in its tooltip, builds first and then plays. Stop is one button: it cancels a build that runs (the blocks that were ready are kept; press again to stop audio that plays), otherwise it stops the audio. Loop repeats the audio, and when bars are chosen on the arrangement ruler a Play bars a-b button plays only those. The line next to Stop says what plays (the song, a block, a project file). A disabled button says why in its tooltip (errors in the song, a read-only state, a build that runs).

Keys: Space plays or stops (not while typing or in a dialog), Ctrl+B builds (Ctrl+Enter applies the source editor). Blocks that failed in the last build show a red badge (2 failed) that opens the build log, and the log ends the build with a line that names them. The audio of the song is downloaded from the file menu (Download the song audio, WAV or MP3). A block whose take is out of date shows no player: its take is removed as soon as the block changes.

Build errors in the code (2026-10-08)

A line of the build log that names a failed block (sq: failed: AMP5380: ...) is a link: click it and the Source view opens with that line in view. The line is underlined in red (and has a red dot in the gutter). The line is the parameter the message names (a missing file points at the file line), otherwise the header of the block. The same log line has a Show block button that goes to the block in the node editor instead (selected and in view). Hover the line for a tooltip with the code, the block and the full message in selectable text, with a Copy message button; move the pointer onto the tooltip to select. When you change that line the mark goes away; the next build puts it back if the problem is still there (a new build also clears every mark first). The same red line shows in the Source view when you open it later, for as long as the line is as it was when the build ran. Model: web/lib/build-errors.mjs.

The sequencer workspace (2026-10-08)

A sequencer block has a full-screen workspace (the Open the sequencer button, or the block menu): the channel rack, pattern tabs with step grids and the piano roll, the playlist with clips and sections, and the lanes strip. See Sequencer.

On a phone (mobile UI, 2026-10-20)

At 700 px wide or less (a coarse pointer up to 900 px for the dialogs) the page switches to a phone layout; one stylesheet (web/styles/mobile.css) and one script (web/app/mobile.js) hold it, the desktop elements stay in the page and the phone menus click them. Desktop layout and mouse behaviour are unchanged. How it feels on a real phone is owner-observed; the specs check the DOM and geometry only.

  • Header: one row (Projects, Undo, Redo, the big play / Build and play button, Stop, a small status pill, a more menu with Build, Save, Checkpoint, Volume, Loop, panels, Guide, Help, About). Buttons are at least 44 px. At 360 px with the longest label (Build and play) the status pill gives way first.
  • Bottom navigation: Arrangement, Branches, History, Project and More (Variants, Assistant, Log); a panel opens as a bottom sheet with a drag handle (drag to resize, swipe down or tap to close).
  • Canvas: pinch = zoom, one finger = pan, long press = context menu (on a button or dot: its tooltip), tap a dot then another dot to connect, bigger dots, minimap on demand. A tap that Chromium moves from a dot to a neighbouring block button goes back to the dot.
  • Dialogs and panels (MUI05): every dialog (ask and confirm dialogs, compare, the Studio, the Advanced piano roll, checkpoint, About, file picker, recorder, ...) is a full-screen page with a sticky Back bar (Back does what Esc does; the system Back button closes the top dialog), a scrollable body and safe-area padding; none is wider than the screen. The projects view was already a full page with its own Back button.
  • AMPLE Jam (Lite piano roll) on touch (MUI06): a full-screen panel (its close button is the Back button), a toolbar with 44 px buttons that scrolls sideways, pinch zoom (spread sideways = time, spread up and down = rows), two fingers moving together scroll, one finger draws / moves / resizes / selects as the current tool, a Hand tool (touch layout only) scrolls with one finger also in the Grid view, a long press deletes a note (accents a Grid step), the neighbour strip scrolls sideways.
  • Tests: npx playwright test --project=phone (390x844, touch) runs spec-tests/parity/*.phone.spec.ts; the pure gesture maths (touch-gestures, sheet-drag, dialog-history, lite-touch) has node tests in web/lib/test.
  • Bug fixed on the way: a double tap on connector dots (tap-tap connecting) counted as a double click on the block and opened its source view, which hides the canvas (#canvaswrap.bmode); a double click on a dot no longer does that.

Running the tests

dotnet build ample/Ample.sln
cd ample && npm install && npx playwright install chromium
npx playwright test --project=chromium       # spec-tests/parity/*.spec.ts against a real ample serve
node --test web/lib/test                     # geometry, graph, history logic

Specs that change history, seeds or takes start a server of their own (freshServer() in web/tests/support.ts), so what other specs did before cannot matter.

Editors and managers (as built)

  • Views: Blocks, Source, Library and Branch manager share the canvas area (web/app/views.js). The view switch stays above every view. A project that opens with errors starts in the source editor; the node editor is read-only (banner) until they are fixed.
  • Source editor (source.js, lsp.js): a locally bundled CodeMirror 6 editor with AMPLE syntax highlighting, a gutter and diagnostic/build squiggles, driven by the real language server over /lsp (live diagnostics, Ctrl+Space completion, Ctrl+click definition, rename, format, fix all). Valid song text syncs to the working copy after a short pause; the Properties panel follows the block under the text cursor and edits either way update the other view. Properties are hidden with an explanation while the source has errors. Save makes a revision; Ctrl+Enter confirms the current buffer. Text files the song refers to (lyrics, chords, notes) and the generated ample.lock (read-only) open in the same editor.
  • Unapplied edits in source files are kept as separate browser recovery drafts. Switching files can preserve a draft; after reload, opening that file offers its timestamp and size comparison, a full-window saved/recovered view, and explicit restore or continue-saved choices. Drafts stay in this browser and project; applying or reverting the file removes its draft.
  • Lyrics editor (lyrics.js, lyrics-model.js): timed [bar N] text lines with live checks (empty line, order, long line), sort on apply, import and export of .lrc.
  • Plugin settings (pluginui.js): generated from the manifest's schema, validated before it is stored in .ample/plugin-settings.json.
  • Library manager and mounts (libraryui.js, side panel "Folders and links"): linked folders, assets, details, where used, ample.lock line, copy into project. Offline mounts are marked and never become write targets.
  • Projects (projects.js): recent list with a health summary, new project, settings (black box budget, retention, default engine, master seed through the dangerous act), health (findings, black box chain, interrupted commands to restore or accept, backup age), backups, export and cleanup.
  • Dangerous acts use one dialog (dangerous.js): dry run, impact, backup suggestion with "Make a backup now", typed words and a reason; the confirm call only works with the token of the dry run (tested through the API too).

Not built

No live lyrics preview against a take, no branch rename, no replace-with-impact in the library manager, "Open project" starts a second server instead of switching.

Number fields (properties panel)

Numeric parameters are typed fields with the browser's small up and down arrows (also ArrowUp and ArrowDown in the field); a value is committed on Enter, on leaving the field or on an arrow click, and goes through the same edit path as every other parameter. A parameter whose template says number, and the known ranged ones (swing 0 to 60, humanize 0 to 100, stagger 0 to 80, gain -24 to 12, steps, bars), get this field; a value that is not a number (like derived for a seed) stays a text field. A value outside the range is moved into it with a message, and an empty field goes back to the last value. Focusing a field with a range shows a floating slider for that same value; typing remains available. The pure part (ranges, reading what was typed) is web/lib/numfield-model.js.

Multiline text parameters open in a wide responsive dialog with a tall, vertically resizable editor. Soft wrapping keeps long lines readable while preserving explicit line breaks when applied.

Progress of a block while it builds

While a build runs, a block that is busy keeps its size: its status tag names the step that is busy ("synthesis 13%"), a thin bar along its bottom edge shows the whole block, and while the pointer is on the block a panel opens below it (animated, floating over what is below) with every sub-step and its own 0 to 100 % (a step that is busy without a known end is striped). Blocks that wait for others say "waiting". A block shows its result as soon as it finishes, even when another block at the same level is still rendering; the toolbar counts results from the current build only. The build-log time estimate counts newly rendered blocks, not cache hits. The ACE-Step plugin reports plan, synthesis and isolation; ace-server only says running or done, so those bars move by an estimate and jump to the end when the step is done. The Progress button next to Map turns the bars off (remembered in this browser). A plugin reports progress with ctx.progress(fraction, step, stepFraction); the engine passes it on as the event build.block (block, state, fraction, steps), at most ten times a second.

Ctrl+click in the source editor

Hold Ctrl in the source editor and everything that can be clicked is underlined: the names of blocks (in a block header and in a from line) and the paths of project files (for example the value of file). Ctrl+click on a block name shows the block in the node editor; Ctrl+click on a file opens that file in the source editor (a song opens as the song). A file without source, such as audio, selects the block that uses it.

Sample set hints

Below the sample kit or sample set chooser the properties panel shows what the chosen set has: "N layers on disk, engine plays M" (and the same for round robins), a "what you are missing" line (layers left on the source according to set.json, files the engine does not play yet) and a collapsible region table (voice, layers, round robins, what plays, loop). The text comes from web/lib/setinfo.js (tested in web/lib/test/setinfo.test.mjs) and the numbers from GET /api/samples. Sets without extra files show nothing new. Velocity, choke and gain fields follow later.

Piano roll guide

Covers web/app/pianoroll.js (items PR01-PR22 of the piano roll). The text stays the truth: every gesture below is one ordinary edit of the clip's notes parameter (or, for the humanize block and arrangement parts, of another parameter or block), always undoable. Partial features and engine limitations are called out where they apply.

The lighter companion editor, AMPLE Jam (Lite, same notes and undo), is described in midi-loop-studio.md. In Lite Ctrl+D deselects; here it still duplicates.

Playback and long notes (2026-10-18)

Play/Space starts at the independent playhead, initially the clip start. Selecting or drawing notes and scrolling no longer change that position. Click the ruler to seek; dragging it still pans. Alt+Play or Alt+Space explicitly previews from the selection. Play again pauses; Stop returns to the clip start. Loop repeats the complete clip, including when playback starts halfway through it, and voices are cut at the loop seam.

Dragging a note edge can extend over several bars; the roll displays contiguous tied pieces as one note and resizes or deletes that whole note. The saved text has one valid entry per bar of the song meter (4 beats in 4/4, 3 in 3/4, and so on). ;tie=N joins pieces without forcing an instrument program/channel; legacy routed tie fields still work. Other position edits of tied notes remain source-only. The right edge has a visible grip and can be grabbed even on short notes. The roll follows the meter of the song (meter N/D on the composition line). A meter per clip (PR22) is not built; the ruler-grouping selector still changes the view only.

Play and hear-notes resolve the connected instrument through supported MIDI effects. Synth, built-in piano/bass, one-shot sampler and supported plain WAV sample sets reuse the local preview renderers; GM uses the configured SoundFont audition endpoint. Seeded MIDI effects use the exact effective seed. The label identifies instrument preview versus the sketch fallback; both are approximate listening previews, not stored renders. Cold or unsupported voices use the audible sketch while supported voices warm in a bounded cache. Unsupported expression/sets remain explicit fallbacks. This does not preview downstream audio effects or promise byte identity with a build. Closing the roll cancels local workers and playback.

Rendering (PR01)

The three canvases (notes grid, arrangement/automation lanes, sound row) scale their backing store with devicePixelRatio (sizeCanvas()), so they stay crisp on high-DPI screens; a window resize listener re-sizes them while the roll is open. Redraws go through a single requestAnimationFrame dirty loop (requestDraw()), so a burst of drag/wheel/resize events collapses into one draw per frame. Notes are culled to the visible time range by a binary search on a sorted-by-start index (sortedRows/visibleRows) before the per-note pixel check, so a very large clip only pays for the notes actually on screen. dialog.dataset.drawMs reports the last frame's draw time (PR13's frame-time probe; report-only, nothing fails on it). Canvas sizing and note glyph drawing live in pianoroll-draw.js; pointer coordinate conversion and note hit testing live in pianoroll-input.js. The dialog keeps gesture lifecycle and drawing composition with the shared model, undo and selection state.

Look (PR02, PR03)

By default a note is a vertical gradient keyed on velocity (cool blue to hot amber, web/lib/pianoroll-theme.mjs), with a 1px top highlight and a glow when selected. The "high contrast" toggle restores the previous flat, solid fill (no glow), for low-vision or reduced-motion use.

A clip's scale parameter ("c:minor", "f#:dorian", ..., or "none", parsed by web/lib/scales.mjs) drives: a root+scale selector in the toolbar, row shading (out-of-scale rows dimmed, not hidden), a glowing border on root rows, a thin red outline on out-of-scale notes, a "Fit to scale" button (moves the selection's out-of-scale notes to the nearest in-scale pitch, one edit), and a click-to-use Krumhansl-Schmuckler key guess (detectKey(); never applied without a click). The scale table also lives in spec/scales.json (kept in sync by hand; the C# engine/LSP side does not read it yet).

Gestures (PR04)

Gesture Result
left-drag on empty grid draw a note (length by drag); a plain click uses the last-used length
left-drag on a note / its edge move / resize
Shift + left-drag on empty grid brush: paints notes of the last-used length, one per grid step, never stretching
right-click on a note / right-drag delete / eraser sweep (one undo step for the whole drag)
double-click a note note properties popover (pitch, bar:beat, length, velocity, slide)
double-click in the lower lane reset the nearest note's lane value to its default
double-click a ghost note switch the roll to that clip (PR05)
wheel on a note velocity +-1 (Shift +-5)
Ctrl+wheel / Alt+wheel / Shift+wheel zoom time / zoom rows / scroll sideways (unchanged)
Ctrl + drag on empty grid rubber-band selection (replaces the old Alt/right-button binding)
, / . select the previous / next note in time
Delete/Backspace, arrows, Shift+arrows, Ctrl+A/C/X/V/D as before
S toggle Slide on the selection (not while step input owns s as a piano key)
Alt+U / Alt+S / Alt+R hi-hat chopper / strum / configure humanize
Alt+Left return from a ghost focus-switch
? shortcuts card

Hum… records and reviews a sung line, then converts the parsed note entries to the roll's absolute-time note values before adding them to the clip. Detected notes are estimates; correct them in the roll before building.

Not implemented: Alt+wheel fine-pitch on a note (needs PR06's per-note fine field to matter to the ear first; the data field exists, the gesture does not yet), the "Unlimited Paint" brush drawing a ramp rather than a straight paint (shift+drag always uses one fixed length, not a stretch).

Ghost notes and focus-switch (PR05)

Other midi-clip blocks whose arrangement parts overlap this clip's are drawn as faint read-only outlines under this clip's own notes (toggle: "ghosts"), read from their notes text or rendered from chords/melody (own ppq and part offset are converted into this clip's tick/bar space). "Ghost clips" has one visibility checkbox per source; hidden ghosts cannot be focused or copied. Double-clicking a shorthand ghost opens its conversion prompt before editing.

Per-note properties (PR06)

Entry grammar: bar:start:length:pitch:velocity[:channel:bank:program[:tie]] followed by zero or more ;key=value pairs:

Key Range Meaning
pan -100..100 stereo position of this note's voice
fine -100..100 cents fine pitch offset of this note only
rel 0..5000 ms release time of this note (no default: unset means the instrument's own)
cut 0..100 % low-pass cutoff (100 = no filter)
slide 0 or 1 this note glides the previous note's voice to its pitch (PR08)
port 0..2000 ms portamento time into this note from the previous one

A value equal to its default (0, 0, -, 100, 0, 0) is never written, so a clip stays byte-identical until a property is actually used. Unknown ;key=value pairs are kept verbatim by the roll's own model (web/lib/notes-model.mjs) and re-emitted unchanged; the C# reader (StructuredMidiNotes.cs) and the JS validator (expanded-midi-notes.js) agree on the same grammar and ranges, and the midi-clip renderer passes the values through into its JSON note objects. The gm/SF2 renderer honours pan, fine, rel and cut in sound (see PR07 below); slide and port are handled by the GM/SF2, synth and pitched sample-set renderers; one-shot sampler behavior remains unchanged. The language server completes these keys after ;; invalid values produce AMP2012.

Edited MIDI-module export maps pan to CC10, fine pitch to pitch bend after setting the bend range to one semitone by RPN, release to CC72 and cutoff to CC74. Each distinct combination uses a free channel, separate from retained source channels; export fails if no free channel remains. Pan uses 0..127, release maps 0..5000 ms linearly to 0..127 and cutoff maps 0..100 linearly to 0..127. Import reconstructs values at each note start. Portamento maps to CC65/CC5 on an isolated channel. Slide notes export as a 32-point pitch-bend ramp plus a private AMPLE marker so reimport can restore the editable slide note; other MIDI applications can play the ramp and ignore the marker. These MIDI controls remain lossy representations.

Lower lane (PR07)

A switcher (velocity / pan / fine pitch / release / cutoff) under the grid draws one stem per note. Pan and fine pitch are centred lanes (a value draws up or down from a midline); the others draw from the baseline like velocity always did. Dragging re-picks the nearest note at the current x on every move, so one drag paints a freehand ramp across several notes (one undo step). Shift-drag draws an exact straight line between the first note and the pointer, recalculating every note in that span from the original values; double-click resets the nearest note to the lane's default.

Engine: src/Ample.Audio/Engine/SamplerRenderers.cs's SF2 note player (PlaySf2Note) sets a note's resting pan (CC10), pitch bend (fine, within the renderer's fixed +-200 cent bend range) and brightness/cutoff (cut, CC74) from its own values, reusing the exact mechanisms already built for controller-lane automation; rel replaces the SF2 region's own release time outright when set. An actual CC10/CC74/PitchBend event in the song still overrides the resting value from the frame it occurs, unchanged. Synth renderer v2 also applies pan, fine pitch, release and a per-note low-pass before its master filter. Sample-set piano, bass and guitar apply pan/fine/release/cutoff during sample playback and use integer pitch paths for slides. Drums and the one-shot sampler keep their existing clip-level sample behavior.

Slide notes (PR08, GM/SF2 audio)

A note's slide flag is reachable via the S shortcut (toggles the selection) and the note-properties popover; a slide note shows a dashed diagonal connector from the nearest earlier note. GM/SF2, synth and sample-set piano/bass/guitar renderers continue the most recently started voice on the same MIDI channel, glide in cents across the slide note's duration, and do not strike a second note. A slide without an active voice is silent. MIDI export writes the bend ramp and AMPLE marker described above.

Chord stamps (PR09)

spec/chords.json / web/lib/chords.mjs: 47 chords (triads, suspended, sevenths, ninths, elevenths, thirteenths, sixths, jazz/altered, power, cluster - scoped down from the plan's "about 80"). A dropdown plus a "Stamp" arm toggle: while armed, a plain click on empty grid plots the chord rooted at the clicked row. The canvas shows an outline preview under the cursor. "Chord options" sets inversion, spread, drop-2, octave doubling and a bass MIDI pitch; preview and placement use the same options.

Hi-hat roll chopper (PR10) and strum (PR11)

Alt+U slices the selection into N equal pieces (web/lib/chop.mjs: 1/2 through 1/32, or 1/4t/1/8t/1/16t triplets) with exact tick arithmetic (the pieces always sum to the original length), a gate-length percentage and a velocity ramp (flat/rising/falling/seeded humanised). Alt+S (web/lib/strum.mjs) groups notes that start within a 32nd-note tolerance and staggers each group over a beat span following a curve (even/slow-then-fast/fast-then-slow/guitar/harp), fading velocity toward the end; direction is down/up/alternate. Both open a plain popover (division/curve/options + Apply), not a custom floating dial widget as sketched in the epic.

Humanize (PR12)

Alt+R creates or updates a midi-humanize block, configures its velocity and timing parameters, and previews the exact drift with the same stable random stream as the engine. The preview reads the block's effective seed, including a locked or overridden value; if the seed cannot be read, preview and Bake are disabled. Bake applies the previewed changes directly to the notes as one undoable edit. When inserting a new block, the roll routes the clip's existing MIDI outputs through it and preserves disabled connections.

Performance, accessibility, polish (PR13)

A frame-time probe (dialog.dataset.drawMs) reports each draw's duration (never fails anything). Popovers return focus to the canvas on Cancel. A ? shortcuts card lists every gesture above. Not verified: touch gestures (no touch device in this pass), prefers-reduced-motion (there is no CSS animation to gate - the only "motion" is per-frame canvas redraw, already driven by actual changes, not a timed animation), and a full screen-reader audit beyond the existing note-navigation announcements.

Extra tools (PR15-PR22)

  • PR15 arpeggiate, PR16 legato/staccato/remove-overlaps, PR17 flip/mirror/reverse/scale-time: web/lib/roll-tools.mjs, reachable from a "Tools" dropdown in the toolbar (same-count transforms write back by index; arpeggiate replaces the selection, like the chopper). "Flip pitch" uses the selection midpoint; "Mirror pitch…" lets the user choose a MIDI pitch as the mirror axis.
  • PR18 colour groups: grp (1-8, the same ;key=value grammar as PR06, no engine change needed since the engine already passes unknown-but- valid-integer keys through). A group filter dims notes outside the chosen group, "Select group" selects them, a colour tab marks each note. Choose a group and MIDI channel, then use "Move group" to change every note in that group in one undoable edit.
  • PR19 scale-lock and chord-lock: scale-lock snaps newly drawn, brushed and moved notes to the current scale; Up/Down transpose selected notes within the scale. Chord-lock uses sounding notes in visible chord/melody ghost clips for the same gestures. When both are enabled, pitches meet both locks; when no chord tone is sounding, scale-lock still applies on its own.
  • PR20 riff machine: web/lib/riff.mjs, a seeded step generator (density, accent, pitch spread, optional scale snap) reachable from the Tools menu; scoped from "in the selection" to "from the cursor/selection start, for N bars" (the roll has no empty-time-range selection).
  • PR21 multi-clip editing: "Copy ghosts" pastes every visible ghost note into the open clip; a "Reference clip" picker keeps any clip visible even without arrangement overlap. "Split edit" opens two independently editable roll dialogs side by side; both write normal undoable edits.
  • PR22 per-clip meter (not built): the agreed design is a meter per clip. Arrangement at N stays on the project timeline; each clip's meter defines its own bar length in quarter-note beats. Four bars of 3/4 take 12 beats and do not auto-align to a project bar. Today the meter is one value for the whole song (a song-level meter); the view-only selector does not claim to change playback until a meter per clip is built end to end.

What's still open

Remaining manual acceptance: a full screen-reader audit. PR22's agreed semantics are recorded, but a meter per clip must update the parser, arrangement and playback together. The piano-roll tour example and in-app help entry are now present; automated verification follows after the feature changes.

AMPLE Jam (Lite piano roll)

Renamed on 2026-10-20: this was called "MIDI Loop Studio" (plan folder, file name and block ids keep the old name).

AMPLE Jam is the piano roll of AMPLE: a non-modal floating panel for editing a midi-clip. (Until 2026-10-21 there was also a heavier "Classic" roll; everything it did is in Jam now and it has been removed.) Every gesture is one ordinary, undoable edit of the clip's notes text through the same store, so there is one undo history; the text stays the truth. The FL-style sequencer block (a step sequencer block of its own) is a different thing; the Grid view is only another view of one clip's notes.

Opening it

  • Select a midi-clip and press AMPLE Jam (or Track view, which also shows the arrangement, sound and automation lanes). A clip written with chords or a melody is first written out as notes after you have seen how many notes that makes (one edit; Undo brings the chords back). A MIDI block opens Show notes read-only, with Make an editable copy as notes in the menu.
  • The lower lane under the notes edits one value per note: velocity, pan, fine pitch, release or cutoff (the choice at its left). Drag a bar, Shift+drag for a ramp, double-click to reset.
  • The ☰ menu folds its tools into groups that open one at a time: On the selected notes (reverse, speed, flip pitch, legato, staccato, remove overlaps, strum, chopper, humanize), Create (arpeggiate, riff machine, stamp a chord, hum a melody), Scale (root and scale, snap, fit, guess the key), Colour groups and properties (group colour tabs, show one group, group MIDI channel, exact bar/beat/length/pitch/velocity, slide and portamento), Lanes and clips behind (arrangement, sound and automation lanes; the other clips as faint outlines, copy them, chord lock). Settings open as a small card in the window; Enter applies and Esc closes. Edit as text and Play the built song from here are in the menu too.
  • A small corner dot on a note marks slide or portamento (set it in Properties of the selected notes).
  • The view memory is per browser, not per project folder (ample.rollview:<project>:<song> in the browser's storage): the view a clip opens in, zoom, scroll, snap, loop bracket, Roll/Grid mode and panel position. It never creates a song edit or an undo step and does not travel with the project.

Window management (2026-10-20)

The panel is a small window. Double-click the title bar or press – (Collapse) to roll it up to its title bar (it can still be dragged; do it again to expand). The window slides sideways so the mouse stays on the title bar (or on the button): a second double-click in the same place expands it again, back to exactly where it was. The collapse button shows a longer ▁ while the window is rolled up. ▢ (Maximize) makes it a locked-in full-screen window on a dimmed backdrop; Esc or ❐ (Restore) leaves it and the previous place and size come back. Not shown on a phone, where the panel is already full screen. Code: web/app/window-chrome.js.

Sequencer channels (LSQ, 2026-10-20)

A note channel of a sequencer pattern (the rows of an .ampleseq or an embedded sequencer, e.g. the Mozart K525 song) has a 🎹 AMPLE Jam button in the sequencer workspace. It edits the same row text and writes it back into the pattern; Classic and Lite switch the row both ways. Differences from a clip: no neighbour strip and no remembered view (a row is not a block); Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z undo inside Lite only (every commit keeps the previous text), the sequencer's own Undo still steps through the same writes; drum channels (step rows) have no roll.

Roll view

Toolbar order: transport (Play/Pause, Stop, Loop, Follow, metronome), Classic, Roll/Grid, seven tools (Draw P, Paint B, Delete D, Slice C, Select E, Playback Y, Zoom Z), typing keyboard, MIDI, snap, zoom. Below it the optional neighbour strip, the ruler with the loop bracket, the grid with the piano keys, and an always-on velocity strip.

Gesture Effect
Click / drag on empty grid (Draw) add a note; a plain drag stretches it; length = last touched note, else the snap step
Drag a note body / its right edge move / resize (several selected notes together); resizing across a bar line stores tied pieces
Shift+drag a note clone it
Right-click, right-drag delete
Ctrl+click, Ctrl+drag (Select) select, rubber band; Ctrl+Shift+click adds; Ctrl+drag on the ruler selects the notes in a time range
Alt (held) draw and drag off the grid (the snap box says free)
Alt+wheel on a note, Ctrl+Alt+wheel velocity (Shift = 5 steps), fine tune; one edit shortly after the last step
Wheel, Shift+wheel, Ctrl+wheel, Alt+wheel on empty grid scroll pitch, scroll time, zoom time, zoom rows (anchored at the pointer); middle-drag pans
PgUp / PgDn, Shift+1..3, Shift+4, Shift+5 zoom, zoom levels, fit the clip, zoom to the selection
Ctrl+C / X / V copy, cut, paste (at the pointer if over the grid, else at the playhead); every field is kept. Copy also puts the notes on the system clipboard as note text
Shift+Ctrl+V paste note text from the system clipboard (the "MIDI clipboard": text copied from another clip, the Classic roll or any app) at the same place; text that holds no notes pastes nothing
Ctrl+B duplicate the selection to the right
Ctrl+D deselect (FL). In Classic Ctrl+D still duplicates
Ctrl+Q, Ctrl+Alt+Q quick quantize the selection (or all notes) to the snap, 1/16 when snap is none; running it twice equals once
Shift+arrows, Ctrl+Up/Down, Alt+Left/Right move the selection by a step / semitone, by an octave, nudge by 1/48 beat
Backspace, Delete snap on/off, delete the selection
