Space, Ctrl+Space start/stop (stop returns to where play began), play/pause
Ctrl+T, [ ], Alt+NumPad 2-6 typing keyboard on/off, octave
Paint tool, Shift held monophonic: each step column keeps one note, moving to another pitch in the column replaces it
Playback tool (Y) a click starts playing from the snapped position (a playing roll jumps there); right-click stops
Zoom tool (Z) drag a box to fill the view with it, click to zoom in around the pointer, right-click to zoom out; edits nothing
? shortcut card (Esc closes only the card)

Ruler: a click sets the playhead; a drag creates or edits the loop bracket (a Lite extension; FL selects a time range there); right-click clears, double-click resets it to the whole clip. Edits made while playing are heard on the next lap. The playing notes and piano keys light up; pressing a piano key or a typing-keyboard key plays that pitch (nothing is written). The MIDI button (where the browser has Web MIDI) only listens.

Grid view (step sequencer)

The Roll/Grid toggle shows one row per sound and one cell per step over the same notes:

  • Rows: the pitches present plus the rows Grid already showed; an empty clip starts with seven GM drum rows; + Row adds any GM percussion row (added rows are not stored in the song).
  • Step = the current snap grid (1/16 when snap is none). A note longer than a step fills every cell it covers (the later cells are drawn lighter and joined); clicking any covered cell clears the whole note. A note that starts off the grid shows in the cell it covers.
  • Click toggles a step (new velocity = last used, 96 at first); a drag repeats what its first cell did, as one edit; Shift+click or Shift+drag accents (127); right-click or right-drag clears. The plain wheel over a step changes its velocity (this differs from Roll, which needs Alt).
  • M box at the right of a row label mutes that row while playing (and for Play selected). It is a playback setting of this browser, remembered with the view memory; it never changes the song text and never silences the audition of a step you draw.
  • Alt+wheel makes the rows taller or shorter (14 to 56 px) around the pointer; the height is remembered per clip like the other view settings.
  • The tool strip is hidden in Grid. Ctrl+Q works in both views.

Neighbouring-clips strip

A strip under the toolbar shows a chip for every other placed midi-clip part within 8 bars of the open clip (AMPLE has one lane per block and an instrument takes one clip, so "same track" cannot be read, hence any lane). Clicking a chip opens that clip in place (same position and size; the current panel closes) in its remembered view. Back (chip) or Alt+Left returns; with notes selected Alt+Left stays the nudge. The strip edits nothing and hides when there is nothing to show.

Not built / deliberate limits

  • Recording onto the grid is MLS09, not scheduled. Pre-decided options if it is: reuse the FL block's record from a MIDI keyboard (FL07), count-in, independent metronome click, record-arm, overdub/replace, no auto-quantize by default with an optional snap-while-recording toggle, one commit per take.
  • No per-clip meter: the grid and bar length stay 4/4 (PR22 is open). The "+ bar" control only extends the view, not the clip.
  • The note mute tool (T) is not built: it needs a text-format key plus engine and reader support (plan decision 22, option A). Ghost notes are Classic-only; Ctrl+Left/Right time selection is not in Lite.
  • Shift-stretch (FL: Shift+drag sets the note length) is not built because Shift+drag already clones a note (plan decision 32). A plain drag on empty grid already stretches the new note.
  • The duplicate rule covers the whole span of a tied note: drawing on a tail piece does nothing, a move, clone or paste that lands a piece on another note's piece replaces that note, and a growing note stops before the next piece at its pitch.

What is unverified

Tests are DOM and unit tests only (web/lib/test/lite-*.test.mjs, spec-tests/parity/piano-roll-lite*.spec.ts, including the scripted 12-step session and a seeded UI fuzz in piano-roll-lite-acceptance.spec.ts, plus the two optional steps: an instrument setting changed while the roll is open, and drawing past the clip end). No sound is heard by any test. Not verified by tests: real audition latency against the 40 ms / 15 ms budgets (and any Bluetooth delay), the loop seam by ear, drag smoothness, cursors, wheel feel, scale tint, the hand-over between the modal Classic dialog and the non-modal Lite panel, and every FL "same/differs" verdict in PARITY.md, which the planner could only check against the FL manual, not a running FL. Open decisions: view memory in browser storage, Split leaves Classic closed, Ctrl+Q alongside Ctrl+Alt+Q, Alt+NumPad octave digits, draw drag stretch vs move, the Grid and strip rules above, and the meter per clip (PR22).

Extending the AMPLE Studio UI

The Advanced piano roll uses roll-transport.mjs for playhead/loop math and roll-preview.js for connected-instrument audition through existing client-side renderers. Preserve its explicit approximate/fallback label, exact effective MIDI-effect seeds, bounded cache and close-time disposal when adding views. Bar-crossing notes remain valid per-bar entries joined by ;tie=N; never synthesize a GM program/channel merely to attach a tie.

Project exports use project-export.js and the token-protected /api/project/export job API. Long conversions/compression must remain asynchronous, show progress, support cancellation, and write only to the job's temporary directory. Do not buffer a completed archive in browser memory; download through the completed job endpoint.

Title-bar status controls use .node-status; completed render/cache states belong there, while .tag.stat is reserved for live build steps. Route error inspection through showBlockStatusError so the log panel, source diagnostic and upstream failure navigation remain consistent. New playback paths must use playbackOutput(context) after their processing/meters, or registerPlaybackAudio(element) for native audition audio. Do not put this tab-local 0–150% gain into offline rendering, exports, song parameters or recording capture. See web-ui.md.

Canvas blocks use a two-row header: a compact cyan nameplate with an automatically sized title and pin toggle, then a toolbar with type, version, the current block's GUI/properties arrow, connected effects and the source-editor action at the right edge. Double-click the name to rename through the normal edit command; the title remains a drag handle, with pointer capture kept on the title so double-click or double-tap still reaches its rename handler. Two-finger touch gestures on the canvas zoom around their midpoint and pan the graph; native browser touch zoom is disabled only on that surface. RDP gestures forwarded as Ctrl+wheel use the existing canvas wheel zoom. Canvas geometry uses the complete 60-pixel header height for ports, links and layout. Volume blocks remain narrower and taller with their channel controls on the node. Each channel has a fader and a live output meter in dB; Link/Mono and channel mutes use compact switches. Live preview plays the resolved upstream signal through the block settings without rebuilding, and meter ownership follows that block rather than any unrelated audition. Built-take playback remains available separately.

Clicking the active bottom-panel tab collapses the panel; clicking a different tab or a tab while collapsed opens it. Tab clicks use the existing layout toggle so visibility controls and saved layout stay aligned.

This guide is for AMPLE plugins, built-in blocks, editors and panel work. It explains how to fit new work into the default dark Studio UI and how to tell whether existing work needs migration.

Start here

  1. Treat the Studio mockup as a historical reference only; it does not define current UI behavior and must not be updated. Read the Studio UI plan for current implementation guidance.
  2. Read the web UI status and the relevant chunk in the plan table. The plan distinguishes real behavior from mock-only behavior.
  3. Search the existing UI before adding a new control. Reuse its components, token names, command path and panel registration.

Visual language and controls

  • Use semantic CSS variables from web/styles/tokens.css for surfaces, text, borders, focus and state. Use skin.css for common element skins and studio.css for advanced panels. Do not add a local hard-coded palette.
  • Respect data-theme and reduced-motion preferences. Keep readable contrast and visible keyboard focus in every theme.
  • Use web/app/ui.js helpers (el, ask, showMenu, toast) and existing field/control modules rather than building ad hoc dialogs or numeric editors.
  • Keep controls keyboard operable and named. Sliders, knobs, curve handles, toggles and menus need keyboard behavior, an accessible name and appropriate ARIA state/value attributes.
  • Use the shared studio/knob.js control for rotary parameters. Drag in normalized position and then apply the parameter's linear/logarithmic scale, matching its indicator; a linear value delta across a wide log range causes low values to hit minimum with tiny drags (verified in source, 2026-10-10). Keep incremental pointer deltas, an unsnapped drag position for stepped controls, and Shift fine control so changing sensitivity or reversing at an endpoint does not jump or stick.
  • One pointer gesture should commit one edit. Preview the drag in the UI, then submit a single batched edit when it ends; Escape/cancel should leave the document unchanged.

Source editor

The Source view is a locally bundled CodeMirror 6 editor. Its pinned dependencies and offline bundle are maintained by package.json, package-lock.json, web/codemirror/ample-language.js and tools/build-codemirror.mjs; rebuild with npm run build:codemirror. The AMPLE mode uses lexical facts from spec/tokens.json and the documented block-header shape. Theme colors use Studio tokens, and the bundle is lazy-loaded from web/vendor/ with no CDN. Preserve the source view's LSP client, Apply/Save semantics, read-only file support, gutter, diagnostic/build overlays, links, completion, drops and keyboard actions when changing the editor. Focused browser acceptance is tracked in CM01.

Adding a block, plugin or view

  1. Define the block/template contract in spec/templates/ and its language/data behavior in the applicable spec and tests.
  2. Use the library and graph paths in web/app/libraryui.js, canvas.js and graph.js. Keep node state and each effect's bypass state separate. A node can use the independent disabled header flag and its context-menu toggle under Edit; it remains visible but produces no take, and required consumers are implicitly disabled with the warning AMP5253. Effects are ordinary typed AMPLE blocks joined by audio links. Open an effect's advanced controls to edit its own parameters; use the audio block's arrow to navigate to connected effects, with search when multiple are connected. Add → Effects → EQ & filters → Equalizer inserts a normal neutral EQ block connected in the graph. Keep new block actions in the existing Add, Build & export, Edit or Block tools context-menu groups instead of lengthening its top level. Graph links are the source of truth; do not add embedded chain managers or badge-based effect controls. Build, undo and source editing use the normal language/command path. A delayed context-menu action must read its group from the current store when clicked. Saving the view may reload group objects while a submenu is open, leaving references captured when the menu was built stale (verified 2026-10-16).
  3. Preserve the existing port types. Inputs always sit on the left of a block; outputs always sit on the right. Audio and render ports display their compatible stream names on both sides: audio → audio, render → render. Tooltips retain the underlying port names, including numbered mixer channels; source connections retain those identifiers. The graph presents midi as Events. Event-processing blocks may be added later using existing event types and links, but do not imply that analogue signals, new event types, or new backend processing are implemented by the Studio UI.
  4. Render ordinary parameter editing through the existing properties and fieldFor paths. Add bespoke advanced controls only when the block benefits from a visual editor; register it in web/app/studio/panels/registry.js. web/app/studio/modal.js owns the accessible dialog shell and transport. Panel modules belong under web/app/studio/panels/; share controls from web/app/studio/. Hidden properties tabs use display: none; only the active tab contributes height. Verified 2026-10-17: overlapping tabs hidden with visibility: hidden still reserved space, so a delayed master-level result in Info moved the Parameters action buttons down. Keep the actions immediately after the active content and cover delayed hidden-tab updates in layout tests.
  5. Obtain current values through the document/store and send changes through edit() or the documented command API. Do not write project files directly from a component.
  6. For custom visualizations, read tokens at render time. Canvas/SVG drawing must respond to the current theme, selection, enabled/bypassed state and reduced motion.

Preview contract

  • Label browser DSP or plot estimates as approximate. Do not present a visual estimate as a measurement of the integer renderer.
  • The server effect preview is the exact audible reference for the same ControlService-selected input take, range and parameter values. It is bounded, does not create a take, and does not touch the takebank or journal. Keep the preview range and cache bounded. A preview request must use the take selected for the immediate upstream block; do not silently change selection as a preview side effect. An explicit Build and use input action may build and select that take.
  • Offer the exact server preview only for types registered with the built-in effect preview route. Generic blocks can still expose input playback and ordinary properties, but must not send unsupported effect preview requests.
  • Live local preview uses web/app/studio/preview/audio.js and the shared player: it loads the selected upstream take with the selected effect bypassed, then plays it through a persistent Web Audio approximation graph. Label the result approximate. While playback continues, knob movement updates the live graph immediately without restarting the audio; commit one document edit when the gesture ends. A/B toggles the selected effect's bypass in the active live graph, or replays the rendered comparison when rendered preview is active. Keep input playback and exact server-rendered preview under the Compare / render details disclosure.
  • Generator blocks without audio inputs play their own built take. Keep their controls distinct from effect previews; do not require an audio input for generator playback.
  • Keep unavailable preview controls disabled with a short reason (for example, no source take). Never build a take silently just to make a preview button work.
  • For costly exact-render analysis, make the action explicit. The compressor's waveform and gain-reduction analysis only requests the bounded integer render after the user presses Analyze; show the analyzed range and distinguish input and output traces.
  • Plot-based effect panels should update their curve, taps, room shape or timing readout from knob preview values, then commit through the shared control callback once at gesture end.
  • Advanced preview transport exposes a Loop toggle beside Play for the full sample; Shift-drag selects a loop range. Keep the panel's loop preference across Stop/Play and transient preview reloads, and restore the pre-panel player loop state when closing. Native full-sample looping must survive playTransient replacing its audio source.
  • Resolve effect preview input from the latest upstream build take, matching block playback; use separately selected takes only as the initial fallback. On input identity changes, cancel pending audition work and stop old preview playback. Key decoded audio by take identity. Verified source mismatch on 2026-10-10: the source block could play a new voice while Advanced still requested its older selected take. Server previews must ignore disabled audio/render links.
  • A live spectrum uses the shared player analyser and unsubscribes when its panel is replaced or closed. A decoded take estimate is a separate display and must remain labeled approximate.
  • Tempo-based effect playheads derive bar phase from the shared player clock and project tempo; dispose the player listener with the panel.
  • Playback, transport and scrubbing should reuse the shared player rather than creating competing audio clocks.

File fields and project assets

Use web/app/fields.js so each file field inherits its accept rules, picker, clear, open/reveal and drag/drop behavior. Internal drag payloads carry project-relative paths; OS drops go through the journaled upload/conflict flow, which reports per-file transfer progress. The shared picker windows lists above 2000 items; reuse filelist.js instead of rendering an unbounded list in a plugin panel. Do not bypass the command service for upload, overwrite, rename, move or delete.

Do concurrent changes need migration?

Use this quick check when another AMPLE feature was started before a Studio UI change:

Check No migration needed when… Migrate when…
Layout The feature already uses the current library/canvas/properties/bottom-panel shell and remains usable at narrow sizes. It adds a competing full-page shell, hides required transport/panels, or breaks resize behavior.
Styling It uses semantic tokens and shared skins, with focus and reduced motion handled. It hard-codes colors/surfaces or loses contrast/focus under the current themes.
Editing All project changes use the store/command path, remain undoable and preserve one-gesture/one-step behavior. It writes files directly, bypasses journal/pre-image safety, or cannot be undone.
Effects/state Effect bypass and node enablement remain independent; the source node's Advanced dialog manages its ordered connected chain, and each effect's parameter editor stays inside that same dialog. A new path conflates node disable with effect bypass or lacks its canvas/property affordance. Chain edits must preserve type-safe links, terminal consumers and one-gesture/one-undo behavior.
Files It reuses the project picker, accepted-file rules and project-relative drag payloads. It adds a second picker/upload flow or writes around journaled file operations.
Help and proof The web UI docs, help, parity matrix and a scenario/spec describe the behavior. The behavior has no current documentation or the scenario no longer matches it.

If all checks are in the “No migration needed” column, link the change to this guide and the full mockup in its handoff. Otherwise update the affected app region, mockup, docs, parity scenario and tests in the same implementation chunk. These migration rules apply only to AMPLE.

Checks and references

  • JavaScript syntax: node --check <changed-file.js>.
  • Pure web unit tests: one focused node --test web/lib/test/<file>.test.mjs.
  • Server/language change: build the touched project; run one focused dotnet test --filter ... when it fits the agreed narrow test window.
  • Browser interaction: add/update a Playwright spec and its .scenario.md; run it only when browser/test-host execution is authorized for the task. AMPLE browser checks use a fresh Playwright Chromium context, not the Codex browser integration.
  • Report synthetic-fixture Playwright results separately from active-demo results. Synthetic audio verifies UI and request wiring; it does not establish that a selected take in the active demo plays correctly.
  • Always run git diff --check. A syntax/unit/build check is not visual or browser acceptance.

Generation settings and reproduction (2026-10-17)

For audio cards, request bounded server waveform summaries; never fetch/decode every complete song just to paint a thumbnail. Serialize background summary requests, cache their in-flight promises, and release media sources on Stop. Every recurring poll needs an in-flight guard and teardown cancellation. Avoid redundant polling of a task already shown in its dialog. Close event streams in hidden tabs and reconnect on return. Browser regression coverage: spec-tests/parity/ai-network-budget.spec.ts.

Generation fields must display effective numeric defaults, including model-aware CFG, rather than leaving an ambiguous blank. Preserve explicit edits through source reload. Review the seed/CFG near miss checklist for source → request → take coverage. Producer controls expose Check reproduction with separate reference/new-render playback and warnings for changed configuration/software; the original take stays selected.

The language server (as built)

Status (2026-10-03): built in chunk 80. The fresh VSIX was installed and exercised in an isolated VS Code 1.140.0 profile on Windows.

Ample.Lsp is a Language Server Protocol 3.17 server for .amplet songs. It holds no language logic: every answer comes from Ample.Language (parser, queries, formatter, edits), so the editor, the CLI and the web UI cannot disagree. A test runs the server over the whole conformance corpus and compares its diagnostics with the library's.

Using it

How What
ample lsp [--root <ample folder>] [--help-base <url>] Stdio transport (Content-Length framed). Editors start this. Nothing else is written to stdout.
ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/lsp of ample serve WebSocket transport: one JSON-RPC message per text frame. The browser's session cookie is the token; the same host and origin checks as the API apply.
editors/vscode/ The VS Code extension: starts ample lsp, TextMate grammar, snippets, language configuration, commands.

What it does

Capability Notes
Text sync Incremental; positions are UTF-16 (positionEncoding: utf-16).
Diagnostics Pushed on open, change, save; pull (textDocument/diagnostic) too. Each carries the code, a codeDescription.href to <help base>#AMPxxxx, the hint in the message and the related line.
Hover Block type, block, parameter (from the spec data).
Definition, references, rename (with prepare) A block and every from reference.
Symbols, folding, selection ranges Document symbols (blocks), workspace symbols over the open documents, folding of blocks, selection from word to line, block and document.
Completion Block types as snippets (class, version and parameters filled in from the spec), parameters, the values of a parameter with fixed choices, block names, ports after from x. and ->, classes, at and for after the tag, the # view group/size/pin lines with block names, keywords. The studio editor also shows the best guess in grey while typing (Tab takes it; Esc hides it until another line or a space) and Ctrl+Space opens the list.
Signature help The parameters of the block type around the cursor.
Formatting Whole document (a range request formats the whole document too, because the formatter works on whole songs).
Code actions Every quick fix of the library, "Fix all", "Bake" and "Lock" for the block under the cursor.
Semantic tokens Full and range: block types, names, parameters, flags, classes, numbers, strings, comments.
Inlay hints The type of each connection after a from line.
Cancellation, order Requests are handled one after the other, so results are in order; a cancelled request that has not started is dropped (error -32800); after shutdown requests are refused; exit gives code 0 after a clean shutdown, 1 otherwise.

Measured budgets (2026-10-03, Windows 11, one developer machine, Debug build)

What Budget Measured
Diagnostics after an edit in a song of more than 5,000 lines (parse, analyse, publish) 150 ms 52 ms
Completion in the same song 50 ms under 1 ms

The numbers come from LspTests.Budgets_for_a_five_thousand_line_song, which fails above 1 s and 500 ms; the budget is checked by reading the printed numbers. A Release build and other machines were not measured.

Decisions

  • No OmniSharp, no StreamJsonRpc. The protocol is a thin layer over System.Text.Json (about 700 lines): no dependency, nothing to keep in step with a library, and the in-memory channel makes every capability testable without a process.
  • The grammar and the snippets are generated from spec/ by tools/gen-editor-assets.mjs; --check is part of check-all. Grammar tests (editors/vscode/test/grammar.test.mjs) use vscode-textmate with the same regex engine as VS Code.

Not done (and where it goes)

  • Code lens, document links, on-type formatting, semantic tokens delta, declaration and type definition: not built (the language has few of the things they need).
  • Cross-file references and a project folder are not used: the language has no includes yet, so every document stands alone. The read-only fallback for sources outside the project comes with the editor chunk (77).
  • Hover does not show the seed lock state or take information, and there are no "extract to group" or "unlock seed" actions (groups are not in the song file yet; seeds live in the project, not the song).
  • Diagnostics are pushed on every change (no debounce); at the measured speed this is fine.
  • The VS Code integration test packages and installs the VSIX, activates the extension, checks its commands, and sends a completion through the language client to a deterministic local LSP fixture. The real CLI also passed a separate stdio initialize/shutdown smoke check on 2026-10-03. No second client (Neovim or Helix) was tested.
  • Diagnostic columns are code points in the library and UTF-16 units in the protocol; the server converts them (tested with an astral character).

Instance registry

AMPLE records each running project server below instances/ in its AMPLE home: %LOCALAPPDATA%\ample by default, or AMPLE_HOME when set. The record format is defined by the JSON Schema. The .launch sibling contains the current browser URL and token; it is restricted to the current user (Windows ACL without inherited rules, Unix mode 0600). The token never appears in the JSON record or ample instances output.

Each record contains the project id and name, folder, server pid and process start time, port, start/update times, AMPLE version, machine name and start source. Agent starts include their self-reported name, reason and optional session. ACE health is optional. ample instances lists only records whose process still has the recorded start time and whose port answers GET /api/ping with the same project id. ample instances --clean removes stale record and launch files; --json emits records without launch URLs. --home <folder> selects a registry home for isolated use and tests.

The server registers after it has bound its port, refreshes updated every 15 seconds and removes both files during clean shutdown. A crash can leave files behind; readers treat them as stale, and --clean removes them. GET /api/ping returns only { "ok": true, "id": "<project-id>" } without a token. POST /api/server/shutdown uses the normal session-token requirement.

Verification covers fake process and ping probes, atomic concurrent writes, stale cleanup, private launch-file permissions and the live server ping and token-gated shutdown route. The registry does not prove that an agent's self-reported identity is authentic.

Opening AMPLE projects

ample open <project-folder> attaches to a registered server for that project or starts one in the background, waits for its local liveness check, and opens the private launch URL in the default browser. --no-open prints the launch URL instead. A .amplet or .module target resolves to its containing project. With no target, ample open lists recent projects; --last selects the newest one.

The last successful port is saved in recent.json. A later open tries that port first and chooses a free port if it is already occupied. Child server output goes to <AMPLE_HOME>/logs/<project-id>.log; each log rolls at 1 MiB and retains two older files. Launch tokens are kept in the per-user .launch file and are not written to the server log. Set AMPLE_HOME or pass --home to use a different writable user-data folder.

ample open --agent <name> --reason <text> records self-reported agent attribution. When the sibling Ample.Hub.exe is installed, the CLI starts it if needed and sends a correlated v1 JSON-lines request over the current-user-only pipe. When the hub is not installed or reachable, agent starts use the visible CLI fallback. AMPLE_AGENT and AMPLE_AGENT_REASON provide the same attribution through the environment. The hub pipe's versioned fields and limits are documented in the L05 plan; the pipe server is implemented by L05.

tools/AMPLE.bat [target] is the Windows double-click/command launcher. It uses a packaged ample.exe beside the batch file or at the package root one folder above; otherwise it runs the CLI project from source. The classic ample serve command remains a foreground server, opens the browser by default, and prints its launch URL as before. If the instance registry cannot be written, classic serving stays active but ample open cannot discover that server.

The optional --song value is validated by the CLI, but the web UI does not yet consume a song deep link.

Packs and ACE-Step settings

AMPLE looks for installed packs in this order: AMPLE_PACKS, packsFolder in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ample\settings.json, %LOCALAPPDATA%\ample\audio-packs, the AMPLE root supplied to serve --root, then ancestors of the executable and project. ample packs list shows that order; ample packs where explains a missing General MIDI bank; ample packs link <folder> creates a junction instead of copying an existing audio-packs folder.

The fetch commands install into %LOCALAPPDATA%\ample\audio-packs by default. Add --into to retain the repository audio-packs layout. The same settings file can contain ace.exe, ace.models and ace.port; tools/start-ace-server.bat reads those values or the ACE_EXE, ACE_MODELS and ACE_PORT environment variables.

Plugins (as built)

Status: protocol version 1 is implemented and marked experimental; the ACE-Step plugin is the first real plugin that uses it.

A plugin is a program in its own folder with a plugin.json. AMPLE starts it as a separate process, talks to it over stdin and stdout and never lets it write outside its job folder. Everything that is not built in (AI voices, analysers, effects) arrives this way.

The manifest (plugin.json)

Field Meaning
id, version, title Lower-case id with dashes, dotted version, display name.
kind voice, analysis or effect.
protocolVersion 1. A newer major is refused (AMP5271).
experimental True until the protocol is frozen.
entry command and args of the program; arguments are relative to the plugin folder.
platforms windows, linux, macos.
blocks The block types it renders (for example ai-voice).
determinism exact, machine-exact (same bytes on the same machine and toolprint) or unverified.
toolprintFields What the plugin puts in its toolprint (engine commit, model hashes, hardware class).
needs gpu (the host runs one GPU job at a time), network, diskMb, secrets (names; only these are passed, as environment variables).
settings.schema A small JSON Schema (type, enum, minimum, maximum, pattern, required, default, additionalProperties) that drives the settings editor and validates the values (AMP5279).

All problems of a manifest are reported at once (AMP5270). ample plugins validate <folder> checks one.

The protocol (version 1)

JSON-RPC 2.0, one JSON message per line on stdin (host to plugin) and stdout (plugin to host). Stderr is captured as log text.

  • initialize {protocol, host} returns {protocol, id, version, blocks}; the protocol must be 1.
  • describe {} returns {toolprint, determinism}; the toolprint becomes part of every plan.
  • validate {block, settings} returns {ok, messages}.
  • render {jobDir, block:{type,name,parameters}, seed, sampleRate, samplesPerBar, firstBar, barCount, activeBars, inputs, settings} returns {outputs:[{role, path}], meta}. Large data goes through files: inputs are in jobDir/in/, outputs must be written inside jobDir and are named by relative path.
  • analyze {jobDir, analysis, input: "in/audio.wav", options} returns {result} and may return bounded {outputs:[{role, path}]} artifacts for file-producing analysis jobs. Analysis output paths must be relative to the private job folder and point to files the plugin wrote there.
  • cancel {id} and shutdown are notifications; progress {id, fraction} and log {level, message} flow from the plugin.

Local audio transcription

Local reference voice synthesis

Quoted voice parameters are decoded as language strings, including an empty reference_text. With auto_detect on, an empty transcript invokes Whisper rather than being passed to Qwen as literal quotes. Plugin 0.1.5 invalidates takes made with the former decoding behavior.

Each engine can have its own interpreter: voice-clone.pythonXtts, voice-clone.pythonQwen3 and voice-clone.pythonChatterbox (empty means not set). The one for the block's model wins over voice-clone.python, so an environment that only works for one engine is used only for that engine. An explicit voice-clone.python is authoritative for every engine: dependency checks report missing modules or incompatible versions instead of changing interpreters or automatically installing into that environment. Progress shows sys.executable. Qwen with auto_detect on also requires faster_whisper; disable auto detection when supplying the transcript manually, or prepare that dependency in the selected environment. The generic python default retains automatic setup behavior. Plugin 0.1.4 invalidates previous takes so a former CPU-fallback result is not silently reused.

Dependency compatibility note (verified 2026-10-10): qwen-tts 0.1.1 requires Transformers 4.57.3; a shared environment with Transformers 5.2.0 failed to import check_model_inputs. Use a separate Qwen interpreter with compatible Transformers and Hub versions. An environment may reuse existing CUDA packages through a .pth entry and keep its conflicting packages local; this avoids downloading PyTorch again but depends on the shared environment remaining available. Import/CUDA checks establish dependency readiness, not successful model synthesis.

The experimental voice-clone block uses a project audio file as its voice reference and speaks its text parameter. A pause is written in the text: I'm walking [pause 800 ms] down [pause 1.2 s] this road is made per piece with the same reference and AMPLE puts the silences between them (at most 10 s per pause and 60 s together; a pause only at the start or end is allowed). To put pieces of different blocks one after the other use a join block, and to start a sound later by seconds or beats a shift block: a placement (at <bar> for <bars>) is in whole bars. XTTS and Chatterbox need no reference transcript. Qwen3 requires reference_text; when that is blank, auto_detect on runs faster-whisper. The block refuses to build when Qwen3 has neither. MP3 and other accepted formats are converted to mono 24 kHz WAV with the configured ffmpeg when the engine requires it. Configure the local Python executable, model root and ffmpeg in the plugin settings. On first use, the plugin prepares an isolated Python environment and installs the selected engine's packages there; model weights are not downloaded. Qwen3 does not support Dutch or Flemish. Generated WAVs are checked for samples, finite values and non-silence; empty or silent output fails the build with an explicit error. A plugin version upgrade invalidates the previous voice-clone takes once. Speech quality and GPU runtime remain unverified until a build is run with the selected local model. Loading and synthesis progress explicitly show the selected GPU (CUDA) or CPU device, including long-running heartbeat updates; a CUDA check in another environment does not verify the active worker.

plugins/analysis-local-transcription is an optional local adapter for the transcription wizard. It expects audio-separator, basic-pitch, soundfile and scipy to be installed in a local Python environment and requires a complete, preinstalled Audio Separator model folder. Nothing is bundled, installed or downloaded. The compute-device choice defaults to GPU and requires explicit permission for each job; choose CPU to hide CUDA from the worker. GPU use requires GPU-enabled dependencies in the selected Python environment; otherwise GPU mode may fall back to CPU. The worker sets offline environment flags and blocks Python socket connections; missing model companions cause the job to fail instead of downloading them.

In the wizard, select Local stem separation and MIDI estimate and provide options such as {"pythonPath":"C:\\\\Python310\\\\python.exe","modelDirectory":"C:\\\\AudioModels\\\\UVR","separatorModel":"UVR_MDXNET_KARA_2.onnx","modelLicense":"license name or URL","drumMode":"skip"}. The model and all companion files must already exist in that folder. The result records the model SHA-256 and license text supplied in options; the UI labels the latter as user-entered, unverified metadata. The adapter aligns returned stems to the source duration, asks Basic Pitch for vocal and accompaniment MIDI estimates, and returns vocal pitch activity for review. When the selected model returns separate accompaniment stems, it emits one MIDI artifact per stem and a combined multitrack MIDI artifact for one-step import, and suggests editable GM programs from safe stem labels; a single instrumental stem produces one backing artifact. Stem labels are not instrument recognition, and the clamped 0–1 Basic Pitch amplitude is not calibrated confidence. Drum stems are omitted by default because Basic Pitch does not map drum hits; set drumMode to pitched to request a rough pitched estimate. Runtime and transcription accuracy have not been measured on this machine. Model terms are separate from package licenses; verify the selected model's terms before use.

What the host guarantees

  • A clean environment: nothing inherited except PATH and the few variables a program needs to start; a declared secret is passed only to the plugin that declared it, and its value is redacted from captured logs.
  • A private job folder (deleted afterwards); an output path outside it is refused (AMP5272).
  • Timeouts (AMP5276), cancellation (the process tree is stopped), crash containment (AMP5275), invalid output (AMP5273), oversized messages and outputs (AMP5274), plugin-reported errors (AMP5278). A failed render is a failed attempt in the takebank: the plan stays, there is no take, and the next build can try again.
  • One GPU job at a time for plugins that need the GPU.
  • The plugin's description (toolprint) and determinism claim are stored in the plan of every take it makes, so regeneration warnings and reproduction checks know what produced a take.

Writing a plugin

plugins/sdk/ample-plugin.mjs is a small Node helper (serve({initialize, describe, validate, render})); plugins/echo is the reference plugin (deterministic, no GPU) and plugins/flaky misbehaves on purpose (crash, hang, garbage, huge output, path escape, errors, logging a secret) for the host tests. Any language works: read lines, answer lines.

Commands

ample plugins list|describe <id>|validate <folder>|run <id> (run is a self-test: handshake and description).

Voice-clone warm cache (2026-10-10)

voice-clone.keepWarmS (default 600, 0 = off) keeps one Python worker per interpreter alive and the loaded model (and Whisper) in memory, so a rebuild shortly afterwards goes straight to synthesis instead of loading the model again. Only one engine is kept: asking for another engine unloads the first.

The worker gives the memory back by itself and logs why (voice model cache: evict (reason); the log holds the event, the reason, counts and megabytes only):

  • idle for longer than keepWarmS;
  • free video memory of the device below voice-clone.minFreeMb (default 1000);
  • video memory used outside this worker grew by more than voice-clone.pressureMb (default 1024) since the model was loaded. This is computed from the device totals (torch.cuda.mem_get_info) minus what the worker holds itself; it never looks at other processes, their names or their arguments.

A pressure check only runs between builds, never during synthesis. A timeout or a crash ends the worker and so empties the cache. When the generic python default re-launches into the plugin's own isolated environment, that one-shot child has no cache: use an explicit interpreter (per engine) to benefit. Not measured on real hardware yet: the speed-up and the eviction on real VRAM pressure.

Contention while a build runs (added the same day): the worker keeps looking at the device totals while it loads and synthesizes. When it sees pressure (free memory below minFreeMb, or memory outside the worker grew by more than pressureMb), the running build is allowed to finish, and the model is unloaded right afterwards instead of being kept (log: contended, then evict). All three values and keepWarmS are plugin settings. Measured on one machine (8 GB card, torch 2.6.0+cu124): the totals are readable (mem_get_info), and allocating 300 MB inside the worker does not change the "outside this worker" figure, so the worker's own use is not mistaken for another program. Not yet measured: a real load that competes with another program.

GPU plugins kept warm by the host (2026-10-10)

The host starts a plugin process per job and used to stop it afterwards, so nothing a plugin kept in memory survived to the next job. A plugin that needs the GPU and declares the setting keepWarmS (seconds, 0 = off) is now kept running by PluginHost after a successful render and reused by the next job of the same plugin; it is stopped when it has been idle for keepWarmS, when PluginHost.ReleaseWarm is called (for a "free GPU memory" action), when the host stops, or when a job fails or times out (a failed job's process is never kept). The events ("kept for up to N s", "reused", "released (reason)") go to PluginHost.OnWarmEvent; they name the plugin and a reason, nothing about any other process. Only voice-clone declares keepWarmS so far (default 600).

The host also watches the memory totals of the GPU while it keeps a process (NVML nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo, fallback nvidia-smi --query-gpu; totals only, never processes): every five seconds it releases a kept process when free memory is below the plugin setting minFreeMb (default 1000) or when the memory in use grew by more than pressureMb (default 1024) since it was kept (our idle processes do not grow, so growth is another program). Every keep, reuse and release is appended to .ample/logs/gpu.log (time, plugin, reason). GET /api/gpu returns the totals and what is kept; POST /api/gpu/release gives the memory back now (the button "Free GPU memory now" in the plugin settings view). The GPU settings are the voice-clone plugin's keepWarmS, minFreeMb and pressureMb.

Not kept warm on purpose: ACE-Step (its server backend keeps the models loaded in the server you run; the command line backend starts the program per job, so a kept Node process would hold nothing) and the local transcription plugin (it runs through the analysis path, blocks the network and asks permission per job for the GPU, so a long-lived worker would go against that). Only the first GPU is looked at.

When the environment of an engine cannot be used, the error names which setting chose the interpreter and which setting to change (for example: "The chatterbox engine runs in the Python from voice-clone.python. It is missing: ... Set voice-clone.pythonChatterbox to a Python that has them"). Nothing is installed or switched automatically.

ACE-Step plugin

Status (2026-10-03): built against a stand-in server. The /lm → /job → /synth transport is regression-tested locally, but real-server audio behavior remains unverified and needs the owner's GPU approval.

plugins/acestep turns ai-voice and ace-music blocks into requests to an acestep.cpp server and brings the audio back as 16-bit mono PCM at the project's sample rate, cut or padded to the block's length. ace-music may intentionally include accompaniment and may be instrumental when no lyrics are linked. ai-voice first requests an a-cappella performance and then extracts its vocals stem from the resulting mix, so the delivered take is the extracted stem rather than the initial music-generation result. The manifest says determinism: unverified, so regeneration warns (AMP5101 and AMP5102) until a reproduction check has come out the same.

Inputs and meaning

  • Lyrics editor file is the canonical lyric source. Its timed markers are removed before ACE receives the words. ai-voice refuses to render without it; ace-music accepts no lyrics.
  • Vocal direction is written performance guidance, not an identity picker or a promise of a named singer.
  • Mood / scene arrives through style and is appended to the ACE caption.
  • Melody arrives as the MIDI clip's JSON at the configurable melodyField (default melody) in the /lm request. Set that field to the exact server revision's documented conditioning property before a real run; the linked edge is recorded as melodyPlan: requested, rather than being silently ignored.

Download formats

Built WAV takes download without conversion. MP3 export runs the configured AMPLE_FFMPEG executable (or ffmpeg on PATH) with libmp3lame; the response identifies the exact encoder banner in X-Ample-Mp3-Encoder. If the encoder is unavailable or fails, AMPLE returns AMP5290 rather than serving a renamed WAV.

What it sends and expects (ACE-Step server API)

Step Request Answer
Plan POST /lm with JSON caption, lyrics, language, seed and duration { "id": "..." }
Render POST /synth with the completed plan { "id": "..." }
Voice-only extraction POST /synth as multipart form data: extraction request plus the rendered WAV in audio { "id": "..." }
Poll/fetch GET /job?id={id} then GET /job?id={id}&result=1 job state, then the multipart audio result

The extraction request uses task_type: "extract", track: "vocals" and a Base or SFT DiT model. It is on by default for ai-voice (vocalExtraction: true). The plugin discovers a compatible model through GET /props; the first Base or SFT model that /props lists wins, which is a light (non-XL) one when you have it. Set vocalExtractionModel (the file name as /props lists it; a missing .gguf is added) when you want a specific model, for example an XL one for more detail. The model used is written into the take's metadata (vocalIsolationModel). A Turbo-only server fails before it creates a take, rather than returning a music-backed result labelled as vocals. An optional bearer token is read from the secret ACESTEP_TOKEN.

Rules the plugin follows

  • Only a local endpoint (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) unless the setting allowRemote is on.
  • Lyrics, prompts and file names never go to the logs; only "job submitted" style messages do.
  • The seed is the block's derived seed (or the locked seed from the seed history); lm_seed and steps come from the block parameters.
  • The result records whether a melody was requested and whether vocal extraction ran; it does not claim that unverified MIDI conditioning was honoured by a particular server revision.
  • Errors become plugin errors with a plain message (server unreachable, HTTP status, answer not JSON, job failed, timeout), never a hang: the host's timeout and cancellation still apply.

Trying it without a GPU

node ample/plugins/acestep/stub-server.mjs prints a port and answers with a tone (modes: ok, nobase, error500, malformed, neverdone, noaudio). Point the setting endpoint at it. The stub models the request contract only; it cannot demonstrate audio separation quality.

Manual verification on the real server (to be run by the owner)

Needs a running ace-server (GPU in use, so confirm first) and a tunnel to it.

  1. Confirm /props advertises a Base or SFT DiT model, or set vocalExtractionModel to one installed model file name (ace-server only accepts the name exactly as /props lists it; before 2026-10-03 the plugin cut off the .gguf and every extraction failed at once).
  2. Make a project with one ai-voice block and a lyrics block, build it, and listen: the take should be the extracted vocal stem, the right length and mono.
  3. Run ample verify-reproduction on the block: same means the server is reproducible for that seed on this machine (the plugin's determinism can then be recorded as verified-local); different means regeneration will always ask.
  4. Note the server commit, the model files and the GPU in docs/kb with the date.

Isolating the voice: ace, demucs or off (plugin 0.4.0, 2026-10-03)

The setting vocalIsolation chooses how the voice is separated from the music that ACE-Step makes:

Value What happens Needs
ace (default) A second ACE job with task_type: extract. Works with a light Base or SFT model (acestep-v15-base-Q4_K_M.gguf 1.45 GB, -Q5_K_M 1.70 GB, the same for sft) and with the heavy XL ones. Set vocalExtractionModel to pick one. A Base or SFT DiT in the server's models folder
demucs Demucs (htdemucs, two stems) runs on the CPU in a Python of your own: python -m venv demucs-venv, then pip install demucs soundfile, and set demucsPython to its python.exe. The Python, about 2 GB for torch and the model
off Take the synthesis as it is: fastest, may keep some music. Nothing

Set modelsFolder to the folder of the server's models and the take records the sha256 of the model that was used (vocalIsolationSha256), so a sound can be traced to its exact model; for Demucs the hash is that of the checkpoint in the torch cache. All four light ACE models and the XL base model were tested end to end on 2026-10-03 (RTX 3070, 8 GB); the models come from Hugging Face Serveurperso/ACE-Step-1.5-GGUF and their sha256 matched the repository's. tools/start-ace-server.bat starts the server in a window of its own.

Choosing the model that makes the sound (plugin 0.5.0, 2026-10-03)

A block can choose its own model (and where it runs) with its engine parameter, for example engine "faer:xl-sft"; that wins over synthModel and synthModelFile in the song settings for that block. synthModel picks the ACE-Step model for the synthesis: default (an explicitly resolved turbo model, 8 steps), turbo, sft (cleaner and softer voices, about 50 steps, slower; the usual choice for singing), base (the raw model, about 50 steps), or the large xl-turbo, xl-sft and xl-base. For automatic family selection, the plugin lists the models the server offers (GET /props) and takes the best file of that kind: Q5_K_M first, then Q6_K, Q8_0, Q4_K_M and BF16. synthModelFile names one file exactly and wins. On the server backend, an explicit filename is sent directly even if /props omits it, so ACE itself can accept or reject the attempt with its actual response; on the CLI backend it must be present in modelsFolder. The steps parameter defaults by family (turbo 8, SFT and base 50). Both ACE blocks expose guidance as CFG, visibly resolved to 7 for Base/SFT and 1 for Turbo; that exact value is sent as guidance_scale and recorded in take metadata. Changing CFG can change the generated result, so use the same value for seed comparisons. shift is also exposed (SFT 1, Base/Turbo 3); solver defaults explicitly to euler. The model that was used is written into the take (synthModel). Model selection remains in plugin settings.

Backend: server, command line tools or both (plugin 0.6.2, 2026-10-17)

Generation recipes must survive the complete path into the immutable take; seeds alone are insufficient. See the 2026-10-17 near miss and review checklist. LM sampling is explicit: temperature 0.85, CFG 2, top-p 0.9, top-k 0 and an empty negative prompt. lmModelFile selects the LM explicitly for either backend; the legacy cliLmModel remains accepted. Otherwise an advertised 4B Q8 model is preferred, then a stable sorted selection. The resolved LM and synthesis requests, returned plan and available hashes are retained. These defaults are a reproducible baseline, not a listening-quality guarantee.

The setting backend says how the sound is made, and every song states it itself (the schema marks it x-songRequired; the project value is only the default for new songs, which is server):

Value What happens
server ace-server on endpoint (it must be running).
cli The acestep.cpp tools ace-lm and ace-synth, run by the plugin (needs aceBinFolder and modelsFolder; lmModelFile picks the language model; the selection policy is described above).
server-then-cli The server when GET /health answers, otherwise the command line tools.

Same seed, same models and same request give the same audio on the server and on the command line tools: on 2026-10-04 a 30 s demo (turbo Q5, language model 1.7B) gave the same sha256 for the server (twice) and for ace-lm plus ace-synth on this machine. Not checked: other models (sft, XL), other graphics cards or builds, a freshly started server; so the takes stay unverified. The take metadata records the backend that was used.

A song without acestep.backend gets the warning AMP2013 in the editors with a quick fix ("Add acestep.backend (the project default)", also in Fix all) that writes settings { acestep.backend server }; a build of such a song fails the block with AMP5370 and the same advice, which also appears in the build log.

A voice from a recording (reference)

ai-voice and ace-music take an optional reference audio input (link another block, for example an ACE block with another seed, or set voice_sample on ai-voice to a project file; the link wins). Measured 2026-10-22 on the local server (acestep.cpp b7ba6d9) with the SFT model, two female vocals:

  • Reference only (ACE ref_audio, the timbre encoder): the server receives and encodes it, but the voice stays close to what the voice text and the seed decide. Weak.
  • Reference plus voice_strength (a cover of the reference, task_type cover, the language model codes dropped): the voice clearly follows the reference (owner's listening test with strength 0.9). The melody follows the reference too; reference_noise (cover noise) lets it drift.
  • Faer cannot take a reference yet: AMP5384, use engine local. The reference file/audio hash is part of the plan.

Measured on 2026-10-22 (same server, SFT model, one female reference of 19 s, owner's listening and a pitch-contour check):

  • A cover (voice_strength, also with reference_noise, reference_melody new or a low strength such as 0.15) always keeps the melody and the register of the reference (contour correlation 0.4 to 0.56, register equal); those three knobs change this hardly or not at all on this server revision. A cover is therefore a way to sing the same line again with the same voice, not to put the voice in a new song.
  • A new scene with the voice of the reference needs the timbre route (the reference input without voice_strength). The voice is clearly recognisable there; a reference of 19 s, 10 s or 5 s made no audible difference in the owner's test.
  • The first test sounded shrill and echoey with every reference length and also without a reference, so it came from the voice text and not from the reference: "raw powerful energetic rock vocal, fast and aggressive, gritty" at CFG 7. A soft direction (for example "powerful warm rock vocal, smooth and full, natural, close microphone, no harshness") was reasonably good; CFG 4 and 3 were not preferred.
  • The register still follows the style text (a rock direction sang about 6 semitones lower than the soft reference).

Note (2026-10-22): the parameters reference_noise (sent as cover_noise_strength) and reference_melody (new kept the codes of the language model plan) were built and measured, then removed because they changed nothing audible on this server revision. They can come back if a newer acestep.cpp makes a cover follow them.

Adapter (LoRA) test, 2026-10-22: the server must be started with --adapters <folder> (then /props lists the adapters). With the usual Q5_K_M models it fails (ggml_cuda_cpy: unsupported type combination (q5_K to f32), the synthesis job fails); only acestep-v15-base-BF16.gguf worked with acestep-vocals-lora (strength 1.0 and 0.5). The owner judged the result "not really good", so the adapter is not used; the parameters adapter and adapter_scale stay available for other adapters.

Library manager

Status: the service, the CLI and the API are built (see "As built" at the end); the library screens are not. The rest of this page is the design; where the built version differs it says so below, and section 8 (the screen) describes the planned screen only.

A song depends on things that are not in its text: sample packs, sound fonts, voices, plugins and their models, block templates, external data, imported audio, lyrics and chord files. The library manager lists all of them in one place, shows where each one is used, and lets you replace one by another (with an impact analysis), also per folder. It builds on the linked folders (mounts) from Tech: global catalogs reach AMPLE as read-only links, and the library manager is how you browse and use them.

1. What is in the library

| Kind | Examples | Comes from | | --- | --- | --- | | drum kit, synth pack, sound font, sample, audio import | kit/tape, felt-piano, old-take.wav | a catalog (a linked folder, global or project) or the project folder | | text file | lyrics/chorus.lyr, chords/main.chords | the project | | voice | anna, bo | a plugin (the voice engine) | | plugin, model | acestep 0.9, acestep-turbo-q8 | installed, with their pins in ample.lock | | block template | drums 1.2, piano pinned 2.0 | the template library | | external data | weather.example/api (locked 2026-10-01) | recorded once, part of the project | Every entry has a name, kind, version, hash (content fingerprint, strict, content or loose per Tech), size, where it lives (catalog or project folder, with the virtual path), access (read-only or read-write) and a status:

  • ok: present and matches the hash in ample.lock.
  • changed: present but different from the pinned hash. You can accept the new hash (a change to the working copy) or restore the pinned file from the catalog or a backup.
  • missing: not reachable (a link that points nowhere, a file that was deleted, a plugin that is not installed). Relocate repairs a link without touching the project (a machine-local setting).

2. Identity: every catalog and every asset has a uuid

  • Each catalog gets a uuid the first time it is linked (cat-7f3a-91c2). The uuid, not the path, is what projects, ample.lock and the usage index refer to, so a catalog can be moved, renamed, put on another drive or opened on another computer and everything keeps resolving. Only the machine-local mapping "this uuid lives at this path here" changes.
  • How a folder is recognised as that catalog: the uuid is written to a small marker file in the catalog root (.ample-catalog.json) when the link is writable at link time; for read-only media (a locked drive, a shared network folder) AMPLE cannot write one, so it keeps the uuid in its registry in Home together with a fingerprint of the catalog (a hash over the sorted file hashes, sampled). Relocating to a new path runs an identity check: marker uuid match, or fingerprint match (with a percentage when files were added or removed). A mismatch says "this looks like a different catalog" and asks before relinking.
  • Project assets get a uuid the first time AMPLE sees them (ast-3c1d-9b02), stored in .ample/ and in the usage index. A rename or move (a refactor) keeps the uuid; a copy gets a new one and records "copy of". Catalog assets get their uuid from the catalog index (a hash-derived id plus the catalog uuid), so the same file in two catalogs is two assets.
  • In the song and the lock: the song text shows names (readable); ample.lock stores ids and hashes (asset ast-3c1d-9b02 "kit/tape" @ cat-7f3a-91c2 sha256:...). Renaming an asset or moving a folder changes the name shown, not the id, so history, tags and sealed releases keep pointing at the same thing. Two catalogs with an asset of the same name are told apart by catalog uuid.
  • Duplicates and conflicts: two links that report the same uuid are the same catalog (a mirror); AMPLE uses the one that is reachable and warns when their fingerprints differ.

3. Global asset catalogs: linked folders ("hard links")

  • A global catalog is a folder (for example D:\Music\Samples) linked into AMPLE for every project; a project link exists for one project only. Links are AMPLE-level virtual links, not filesystem hard links (see Tech, "Linked folders (mounts)").
  • A link is read-only or read-write. A read-only link is never written to (by AMPLE or by plugins) and can never be an output folder. Catalogs are almost always read-only.
  • AMPLE indexes and fingerprints a catalog (content hashes, pack hashes, fingerprinter plugins; incrementally and cached), so the song can refer to an asset by id (shown as its name) and hash, and a changed or moved file is noticed.
  • The library manager shows catalogs with a link and a lock icon, their folders as a tree, a missing badge when the link is unreachable, and offers: Relocate (where is this on this computer), make read-only / read-write, Unlink (dangerous act: it lists how many uses would turn missing), Link a folder.

4. Reference or copy (and what a backup contains)

Using a catalog asset references it by id (shown by name) and hash; nothing is copied. That keeps the project small but means the asset must exist where the project is opened. Two ways to make the project travel:

  • Copy into project (per asset or folder): the files go into the project (packs/), the song can then point at the copy (use Replace), and backups and exports contain it.
  • Backup profiles decide what happens with referenced assets: by reference (only name, hash and size are recorded; restore says exactly which catalog assets are needed), or include the assets that are in use (vendoring): AMPLE copies exactly the used files into the backup. See Backup. A restored project asks once where each named catalog lives on this machine (the machine-local setting), then verifies the hashes.

5. Where is it used? (the usage index)

  • Now: the working copy is scanned: block parameters that name the asset (a kit, a set, a voice, a file, a data source), block types for templates, needed plugins and models. Uses inside groups and templates are found too and show the full path (chorus_vox › ACE-Step render).
  • In history: a reverse index in history.db (asset_use(asset hash, revision, block, parameter)), updated when a revision is made, answers "in which revisions, on which lines, in which tagged or sealed releases is this used". Old revisions keep their reference; nothing in history changes when you replace something now.
  • Navigation: each use has Block (shows it in the node editor) and Source (jumps to the line); the properties of a block show a library button next to a parameter that names an asset.
  • Unused: assets nothing uses now. Project assets that are unused are cleanup candidates (see below); catalog assets are never removed by AMPLE.

6. Replace, with the impact analysis

Replace changes references in the working copy, never the catalogs, and never history.

  1. Pick the asset, tick which uses to replace (all by default), choose a replacement of the same family (a drum kit by a drum kit, a sound font by a sound font, a voice by a voice, a lyrics file by a lyrics file).
  2. The dry run shows: each use and its change (drums.kit: kit/tape → kit/808), the blocks that will rebuild (their cache keys change, so they and everything downstream turn grey), sealed or tagged revisions that still use the old asset (they keep it: a release stays reproducible), whether the replacement comes from a read-only catalog (referenced, never modified), and how to undo.
  3. A thick warning (the shared dangerous-act dialog): it changes what the song sounds like; typed acceptance (the asset's name), a backup suggestion and an optional reason (kept in the operation log).
  4. Undo: revert in the source editor, go back to the last revision, or replace it back. Replacing is not saved until you save. Not replaceable by reference: block templates (updated per block with Update), plugins (installed, updated or removed in the plugin list) and models (they belong to a plugin). Replace a folder: choose the folder or catalog that takes over; assets are matched by relative name and family; the dry run shows the mapping (pairs, and the unmatched assets that keep their old reference); then the same warning and typed acceptance. Useful when a library is reorganised or a better version of a kit pack arrives.

7. Other operations

Operation Applies to Notes
Relocate a missing link identity check by catalog uuid (marker file or fingerprint); machine-local; the project, ids and hashes stay the same
Accept the change a changed file records the new hash in ample.lock (working copy)
Rename, move (refactor) project assets and project folders the asset uuid stays; the names in the song are updated automatically (not a replace: the content is the same); not offered for read-only catalogs
Copy into project catalog assets makes the project self-contained for that asset
Remove unused project assets dangerous act: dry run, backup suggestion, typed acceptance; files go to the system trash; older revisions may no longer rebuild unless the take bank or a backup has them
Clean up unused (project) all unused project assets same dialog, listing everything
Verify all everything re-hashes and compares with ample.lock
Link a folder / Unlink catalogs Unlink lists how many uses would turn missing

Selecting a folder in the tree shows a summary (how many assets, how many in use, link path, access) and folder actions: Replace this folder with..., Relocate..., and Rename / move (project folders only).

9. Safety and integrity

  • The engine only serves paths inside the project and its links; .. never escapes; read-only links are never written, also not by plugins.
  • A catalog can change under the song (someone edits a file): the hash comparison reports changed, verify fails with a clear message, and builds that depend on it say so. The song never silently uses a different file than the one it was made with.
  • Replace and Remove are dangerous acts (shared dialog, see Project management); Relocate, Accept the change, Rename and Copy are not.

10. CLI twins

ample lib list [--kind kit] [--unused] [--missing] [--changed]       ample lib where <asset>        ample lib verify [--lock]
ample lib replace <asset> <replacement> [--only block1,block2] [--dry-run]       ample lib replace-folder <folder> <folder>
ample lib relocate <link> <path>      ample lib copy <asset> [--into packs/]     ample lib rename <asset> <new>     ample lib remove <asset> --accept "<name>" --reason "..."
ample links add|remove|list|set-readonly       ample lib index <catalog> [--rebuild]

11. Open questions

  1. Should block templates also be replaceable in bulk (every piano 1.0 by piano 2.0) with the same impact analysis, or stay per block?
  2. How are same-named assets in two catalogs shown and resolved (ambiguity, priority order of catalogs)?
  3. Should a catalog be able to carry a manifest (names, versions, licences, tags) that AMPLE reads, so a catalog author can describe their assets?
  4. Licences and credits: should the library record each asset's licence and feed the credits module (with weights) automatically?
  5. How much of the reverse index is rebuilt on restore versus stored in backups?
  6. Should the catalog marker file also carry a manifest (name, description, licence, version), so the uuid and the catalog's description travel together?
  7. What happens when a catalog is forked (copied to a new place and then edited): a new uuid with "copy of", or an explicit "this is the same catalog" choice?

As built

Where: Ample.Core/Library (Library, LockFile, UnlinkMountAct), the CLI ample library list|scan|link|add|relocate|verify and ample lock update|verify, and the API routes /api/library* and /api/lock* (see the API).

Thing How it works
Catalog One SQLite database per user (library.db in the home folder: AMPLE_HOME, else the local application data). Mounts and assets; project links carry the project id.
Mounts Linked by a person naming a folder; nothing is found by itself. Read-only unless you say --read-write. A writable link gets a marker file .ample-catalog.json with the catalog uuid; a read-only one is never written to, so its identity is a fingerprint of the first thousand file names and sizes. State is worked out live: online, offline (folder gone) or other (a different catalog is at that path).
Assets Uuid (ast-...) on first sight, kept across renames, moves and content changes (a changed file is a new revision, same uuid). Name = the path without extension (kit/tape), or name@version for packs and plugins. Kinds come from file names; only files of known kinds are opened, for hashing (sha256). Other files are listed by name and size and never read. Hidden folders and files are skipped.
Scan Incremental: size and modification time unchanged means not read. A new file whose content was just lost from another path is the same asset moved. Gone files are marked missing, never deleted. Duplicates are found by hash.
Relocate Identity check: the marker has the same uuid, or the fingerprint is the same, or at least 80 percent of the known assets are there with the same size; else AMP5292 unless forced. No song and no lock file changes. FindMoved looks for the marker two folders deep under given roots.
Read-only Every write goes through ResolveWritable, which refuses read-only mounts (AMP5293), offline ones (AMP5290) and paths that leave the mount.
Resolution order project folder (<name> or assets/<name>, with or without extension), the project's linked folders, the user's linked folders, installed packs. Missing: AMP5291 (AMP5290 when its folder is offline); pinned hash differs: AMP5294.
ample.lock Written in a fixed order (assets, packs, plugins; by name) so the same project gives the same bytes: <id> "<name>" mount <catalog uuid> <hash> size <n>. update works out what the songs use (a parameter value that is an asset name, or starts with it and a /); verify says ok, changed, missing or offline per entry.
Packs pack.json needs a name (letters, digits, -, _, .) and a version. Installed by copy into <home>/packs/<name>@<version> or linked where it is. The AI assistant can trigger this itself from a public .zip URL through ample_install_pack (GET /api/ai/context/install-pack): downloads it, extracts it, finds pack.json at the root or inside one wrapping folder, and calls the same copy-install path. Always needs the user's approval (an AiApproval of kind installPack), even when the link was in the request, since it changes the shared library rather than the task's disposable workspace; at most 200 MB.
Import Copies an asset into assets/ of the project with a .provenance.json next to it (source asset, catalog, hash, time), as a command recorded in AMPLE Redux. Never over an existing file.
Unlink A dangerous act (dry run, typed words unlink <name>, reason): the folder and its assets leave the catalog, no file is touched.
Usage index For the open song: block, parameter and line of every use (the "now" half of section 5).

Measured (2026-10-03, Windows 11, Debug build, one machine): scanning 50,000 small files took 6.5 s the first time (all hashed), 1.8 s when nothing changed (none read) and 1.7 s with one changed file (one read); making the files took 26 s. With 5,000 files (the default of the test): 0.8 s, 0.2 s, 0.2 s. AMPLE_PERF=1 dotnet test ample/tests/Ample.Core.Tests --filter Category=Library repeats the 50,000 run.

Not built yet: the screens, file watching (a rescan is explicit), the reverse index in history.db (the "in history" half of section 5), replace with impact analysis and replace folder, accepting the change of one asset (a lock update accepts all), fingerprinter plugins, voices and models as catalog entries (they belong to plugins), rename and move refactors of project assets, the language's own diagnostic for a missing asset (no block parameter is typed as an asset yet, so a missing asset shows up when the build resolves it), and network mounts beyond what the identity check gives.

Opt-in modules and plugins

Status: the reusable block modules (use, module files), the quality checks and the credits are built (see "As built" at the end). The opt-in feature switches, the plugin catalog and the settings screen below are still the earlier design sketch.

The AMPLE core stays small: text sources, a timeline, stable random, history, take bank, hashing and rendering through plugins. Everything else is a module that a project switches on, or a plugin (an external tool behind one contract). Nothing is installed or enabled by default except the core.

Enabling

In the project (.ample/ settings or at the top of an .amplet file):

features {
  quality    on        # scoring, levels, rule packs
  credits    on        # contributors, weights, declared vs measured
  signing    on        # signed releases and tags (layers 5 and 6 of tag protection)
  git-mirror off
  secrets    on        # backup secrets sealed inside the backup
  lyrics     on        # timed lyrics, checks, queries
  assist     diff      # off | diff | button | auto
}

A module that is off adds no commands, no files and no checks. Turning one on is a normal revision. A project that needs a module the installed AMPLE does not have says so on opening ("needs: quality >= 1.2"), and still opens read-only.

Modules (part of AMPLE, opt-in)

Module What it adds Notes
quality Scorers, levels (draft, review, release), rule packs, experiment mode Levels start weak and tighten. Experiment mode relaxes rules, marks results as tainted and expires. A human rating stays the gate for a release.
credits Contributors, roles, per-block weights, declared versus measured splits Records, not legal conclusions.
signing Signed releases and tags, verify of who set what The private key is not in backups by default. When on, tag layers 5 and 6 are on by default.
git-mirror One-way mirror to git, full conversions both ways Raw git objects are kept so the round trip is lossless.
secrets Credential store with its own timeline Sealed with a master passphrase, recovery key offered; see Backup.
lyrics Timed words, checks, queries, own .amplelrc format and importers Checks that need word timing need the alignment plugin.
assist Proposals for text, timing and arrangement A project setting for how much is automated: diff (shown as a patch), button (one click makes a revision), auto (applied on its own line, reviewed later).

Plugins (separate programs, opt-in per project)

Plugins talk to AMPLE through one contract; AMPLE never links against a model.

  • Transports: in-process (a .NET library), out-of-process (JSON-RPC over stdio), http, and an MCP adapter (untrusted by default).
  • Kinds: renderers (ACE-Step voice, instrument engines), analyzers/scorers (word timing, pitch/key fit, loudness, similarity), separators (voice from mix), fingerprinters (strict, content, loose hashing), importers/exporters (lyric formats, MIDI), panels (JS UI, sandboxed iframe).
  • Manifest (plugin.json): id, version, transports, what it offers, toolprint rules (what identifies the build), compatibility ranges, models it needs and where they come from, and the permissions it asks for.
  • Long jobs are async with progress and cancel. Artifacts travel by hash, never by path.
  • Models: often separate downloads (word timing, pitch, separation). A plugin declares them; AMPLE shows "not installed" and offers the install, and never silently falls back. A scorer that is missing shows as "not available" in the review grid.
  • Trust: plugins are pinned by hash in ample.lock; an updated plugin has to pass upgrade-check (does the release still reproduce) before it replaces a pinned one.

Versions and compatibility

Every module and plugin has a version, and a project records the range it works with. Compatibility groups are proven by canary renders, not just claimed (see Determinism and Tech). Format versions apply to .amplet, .amplelrc, .ample exports and plugin.json; readers keep unknown fields.

Open details

  • Which modules ship in the first version (suggested: core, lyrics, quality minimal, secrets).
  • Where the plugin and model catalog lives (per project, with an optional shared user-wide one, as for soundsets).
  • How permissions are shown and approved (network, disk, GPU).

Plugin settings screen

Every plugin has two entry points in the sidebar (and in the project settings), next to its enable checkbox, name and version:

  • ⓘ Properties opens a small dialog: what it does, id, version, status, toolprint, permissions, the models it needs (with missing ones marked), which blocks use it now, and a summary of its settings. From there: Show in the library or Advanced settings....
  • ⚙ Advanced settings (only for an installed plugin) opens a full-screen editor that takes over the editor area, like the lyrics editor:
    • Tabs per plugin, declared in its manifest (for the voice renderer: General, Models, Pipeline, Performance, Permissions). Fields are typed (select, number, toggle, text) so the editor needs no plugin-specific code.
    • Ordered lists with drag and drop for things that have an order: model priority (the first enabled model that fits is used), pipeline stages (required stages cannot be switched off), file types to index, stems to produce. Rows can also be moved with the arrow buttons, and every list has Sort A → Z, Enabled first and Required first.
    • Undo and Redo, one step at a time (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z outside text fields), as long as there is something to undo; the buttons show how many steps are left. Reset to defaults is a step that can be undone too.
    • Two ways back: Apply and back (keeps the settings in the working copy) and Undo and back (throws the session's changes away, with a confirmation if anything changed).
  • Plugin settings are project settings (stored with the project, pinned alongside the plugin version in plugins.lock), so they travel with backups and exports and show as unsaved until Save. Machine-specific values (device, threads, install paths) belong to the machine-local settings, see Project management.
  • Permissions are part of the same screen (network access, reading the project and linked folders, writing only to the output folder). A plugin cannot get more than its manifest declares.

As built

Reusable modules

A module is a file modules/<name>.module (project, linked folder or pack) and a song uses it with use <module>[@version] as <name> { ... }. The syntax, expansion rules, seed scoping and version pins are in language spec 07. In short: the tool expands every use into plain blocks named <instance>/<block> before building, so each instance has its own stable seeds; ample.lock pins module name, version and hash (AMP5328 when one changed); the editor keeps showing the short use.

  • ample modules list shows the modules of the project; ample modules add <file> checks a file and copies it into modules/; ample modules expand <song> prints the expansion and the problems (AMP5320 to AMP5327).
  • ample check, build, the variants and regeneration commands and the server's build routes all build from the expanded song.
